  **IT COUNTS CODE POINTS, BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT POSTGRES COUNTS.**
  `char_length` counts characters; JavaScript's `.length` counts UTF-16 units,
  and an emoji is two. **A server counting `.length` would be STRICTER than the
  column it protects** — refusing a 40-emoji name the database would have stored
  — which is a refusal with no authority behind it. It also counts the TRIMMED
  value, because the trimmed value is what gets stored.

  **TWO SHARED-VARIABLE RULES WERE LIVE HERE AND BOTH CHANGED THE ANSWER.**
  *(1)* `.pa` declares no `overflow`, so the DOCUMENT scrolls and the reserve has
  to sit on the root element — but this file's standing law is that `admin.css`
  shares **no rule** with `theme.css`, only its tokens (roadmap 4.4,
  `AdminPage.jsx` re-states it where it refuses to borrow `PasswordInput`). A
  bare `:root` would have written to the selector the dashboard's stylesheet owns
  and leaked a back-office number into every screen. `:has(.pa)` cannot match on
  a page without the back office, so the rule is unreachable anywhere else.
  *(2)* `--pa-top` was declared on `.pa`, and **a `var()` on `html` cannot see a
  property declared on a descendant** — it would have taken its fallback for
  ever. That is `scripts/var-scope-guard.mjs`'s whole subject: valid CSS,
  identical rendering, every browser check green, two numbers drifting apart. It
  moves up to the `:has` rule instead of being copied, `.pa-body` inherits the
  value it always read, and the guard now counts **27 root-level `var()` reads,
  all resolving**.

  alone is right on a phone, where the column is 360px and a cell lands at
  47px — a thumb"*, and ends *"the cell stays well over the 46px tap floor."*
  **360 is not the narrowest supported width; 320 is** — CLAUDE.md says so and
  `sweep-widths.mjs` sweeps it by default. The reasoning was done once, at one
  width, and then read ever after as a general guarantee. **That is this
  repo's most repeated shape, in a comment rather than in a check.**

  **WHAT IT IS NOT.** Not the sticky bar (2.15): nothing is over these cells,
  and `bar-clear` is green on this very step. Not a clip (tonight's other
  item): there is no inner scroller on this page. Not the rect trap: the cell
  has no `::after` overhang, measured — `--break=rect` changes nothing here.

  **IT IS WHY `bk-bar-clearance.mjs` SHIPS RED, AND THE RED IS DELIBERATE.**
  `legal` is graded rather than recorded, because a control under the absolute
  is a real violation and silencing it inside a check about a different fault
  is exactly how a check comes to measure less than it says. The failure names
  the width, the step and the count on every run.

  **PARKED 2026-09-23, DELIBERATELY, AND HERE IS THE REASONING SO NOBODY
  REOPENS IT AS AN OVERSIGHT.**

  **IT IS ARITHMETIC, NOT TUNING — and this is the number the whole decision
  turns on.** Seven 44px cells need **308px** of cell, plus six 5px gaps:
  **338px**, on a screen that is **320px** wide. That is 18px more than the
  whole phone and 50px more than the column, which is 288 (320 − 16px of
  `--bk-sp-4` gutter each side; the measured cell is `(288 − 30) ÷ 7 = 36.9`,
  which is the 37 the check reports). **So closing the gaps cannot fix it
  either: with NO GAP AT ALL, seven 44px cells still need 308 and the column
  has 288.** A seven-column month cannot carry a 44px-wide target on the
  narrowest phone this product supports, whatever the spacing is. Anything
  that claims otherwise has changed the layout, not the spacing.

  **SO THERE ARE EXACTLY THREE OPTIONS, AND TWO OF THEM ARE A LOOK RATHER
  THAN A BEHAVIOUR:**

  | | What it does | What it costs |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Leave it** | squares stay 37×37 at 320 | 7px under the absolute, at one width, on a control that is one of 32 identical ones |
  | **Make them taller** | 37 wide, 44 tall | **they stop being squares** — and see the ruling below |
  | **Stop showing a month at 320** | a list of open days, full-size rows | changes what the screen IS, not how it looks |

  **ANDREW HAS RULED ON THIS SHAPE ONCE ALREADY, AGAINST AN AUDIT THAT WANTED
  IT CHANGED.** `docs/MANAGER-CLOSE-2026-09-21.md`: *"Job buttons stay square
  on a phone. Leave it."* Different control, same question — whether squareness
  on a phone gives way to a size rule. **A session overturning that by choosing
  option two on its own is exactly the "deferred decision becoming an
  accidental one" CLAUDE.md warns about.**

  **THE RECOMMENDATION IS TO LEAVE IT**, and it goes to Andrew as a
  `FOR-ANDREW.md` row with the number, a picture of what each option does to
  the calendar, and one line to answer.

  **AND THE CHECK STAYS RED AND STAYS GRADED.** A real violation of the
  absolute, hidden inside a check about a different fault, is how a check comes
  to measure less than it claims. `bk-bar-clearance.mjs` fails one assertion,
  names the width, the step and the count, and will go green the day this is
  answered — by a fix, or by a hold Andrew signs.

  **THE PART NOBODY HAD, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS SURVIVED.** The comment
  above the rule already reasons about this and is **correct at 360px** —
  *"the column is 360px and a cell lands at 47px — a thumb… the cell stays
  well over the 46px tap floor."* **Nobody re-checked at 320**, which is the
  narrowest width this product supports, which CLAUDE.md states and which
  `sweep-widths.mjs` sweeps by default. The reasoning was done once, at one
  width, and read ever after as a general guarantee. **That is this repo's
  most repeated shape, sitting in a comment instead of in a check** — and a
  comment cannot go red.

  **Done when:** Andrew answers the row — either every day cell reaches 44px
  of hit area at 320, or the reason it cannot is recorded as a hold with his
  decision on it.
  **MET 2026-10-02 by the second branch** — `FOR-ANDREW.md` § *"DECIDED · The day squares stay as they are"*, his standing
  ruling applied rather than a fresh answer. The check stays red by design; see
  the top of this entry.

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-20 — the booking column had been rendering at under
  half its own declared width, on every step; the calendar's day cells are
  52 by 52 now, square, at desktop.** Found by the other session's
  booking-steps triage, 2026-09-20, root-caused on a fresh load rather than
  a resize. **The before number, so the size of this is visible without
  re-measuring anything: `.bk-wrap` rendered at 316.9px against its own
  declared `max-width` of 632px.**
  **THE CAUSE.** `.bk-wrap` (`app/src/book/booking.css`) is a flex child of
  `.bk`, which is `display: flex; flex-direction: column`. `margin: 0 auto`
  on a flex item puts AUTO margins on its CROSS axis (width, in a
  column-direction parent) — and per the flex spec, cross-axis auto margins
  absorb the leftover space and override `align-items: stretch` for that
  one item. With no `width` declared, `.bk-wrap` never stretched toward the
  `max-width` it was supposed to be centred WITHIN; it shrank to its
  content's width instead, and the margin only centred that narrow box.
  Confirmed structurally before fixing anything: `.bk-header` and
  `.bk-center`, the other two direct children of `.bk`, do not carry
  `margin: 0 auto` on themselves and do not have this fault — the max-width
  pairing that collapses lives one level deeper on `.bk-header .inner`, a
  plain block rather than a flex item, where the ordinary CSS centring rule
  applies without a flex parent's cross-axis override.
  **THE CALENDAR'S CELLS ARE DOWNSTREAM, NOT A SECOND FAULT — checked, not
  assumed.** `.bk-cal { grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr) }`: proportional
  columns, no fixed pixel width anywhere in the cell's own rule. A cell's
  size is entirely a function of `.bk-wrap`'s width, which is why the file's
  own comment already expects 47px on a 360px phone column and the design
  absolute is 44px, while the measured width gave 36.4px — one fault seen
  twice, which is why the fix is the wrap, not the cell.
  **THE FIX, AND IT IS A FIX RATHER THAN A REDESIGN, SAID IN THOSE WORDS ON
  PURPOSE.** `width: 100%;` added to `.bk-wrap`, one line, restoring the
  width the stylesheet has always declared and never reached — the
  `max-width` and the `margin: 0 auto` were always correct; nothing here
  was designed narrow. **But it is not a one-screen change and should not be
  waved through as one:** `.bk-wrap` is shared by all five booking-side
  pages (`BookingPage.jsx` — all seven steps, `BookingConfirmed.jsx`,
  `ManageBookingPage.jsx`, `PlanMemberPage.jsx`, `PlansPage.jsx`), so this
  visibly widens every one of them; step 1 alone moves from 469px to 632px.
  That is why this is held for a press at four widths rather than accepted
  on the diff.
  **SPANISH, CHECKED BEFORE CALLING THIS DONE, EVEN THOUGH THE CHANGE IS
  CSS.** Swept `booking.css` for anything sized to the narrow, buggy
  measurement — no literal `316`/`317` anywhere, and every `white-space:
  nowrap` on the five steps sits on content that either shrinks the risk
  when the column widens (a mono price, a short pill, a badge) or already
  wraps its container (`.bk-plan-chips { flex-wrap: wrap }`) rather than
  overflowing. **This is a static check, not a rendered one** — it rules out
  a value hard-coded to the broken width, it does not prove Spanish copy
  looks right at 632px, which the press below still has to do.
  **ONE THING NOT TO DO, AND IT IS NAMED HERE SO NOBODY REACHES FOR IT ON A
  QUIET NIGHT — the other session's find, kept in its own words because the
  reason is the useful part.** Do not fix the day cells with the `::after`
  negative-inset trick this repo uses elsewhere for a small, isolated mark.
  Calendar cells sit adjacent with only a 5px gap; a negative inset large
  enough to reach a 44px target would extend roughly 4px into each
  neighbour, so the 21st and 22nd of the month would steal each other's
  presses and `elementFromPoint` would return the wrong date along the edge
  of every cell. On a date picker that trades a small target for a WRONG
  one, and the wrong answer here is a booking made on the wrong day. The
  grid's width is the fix; the cell was never the fault.
  **FOUR NUMBERS DECIDE WHETHER THIS WORKED, NOT WHAT THE SCREEN LOOKS
  LIKE, AND ALL FOUR ARE THE OTHER SESSION'S TO RE-MEASURE:** `.bk-wrap` at
  632px on a fresh load (not a resize); the calendar's day cells clearing
  44px; the booking-steps gate's roughly seventy tap-target findings going
  to zero; and `.bk-cal .cell`'s own `max-height: 52px` rule — already
  written, documented as engaging once a column is wide enough to want a
  cell bigger than a thumb needs — finally engaging at desktop, for the
  first time, because desktop has never actually reached that width before.
  A fix that moves the number but leaves any of these four where they were
  is not done, whatever the screen looks like.
  **Built code-only, held for the press — the other session has the browser
  tonight and is the only one who can give this a real before-and-after.**
  **ACCEPTED 2026-09-20. Andrew pressed all four numbers, not just the
  screen.** `.bk-wrap` measures **632 exactly** on a fresh load, no resize,
  against the 316.9 it was. Walked five steps as a customer — service,
  add-ons, vehicle, place, time — wider column throughout, nothing
  overflowing, nothing stranded, no line stretched into looking abandoned.
  **THE 52 IS THE BETTER HALF OF THE STORY, SO IT LEADS THIS ENTRY RATHER
  THAN THE 632.** Measured independently, in a tab neither session drove:
  `.bk-cal` at 600px, day cells **52 by 52, square.** This item's own
  comment named the file's 47px phone-width expectation; what actually
  happened at desktop is a DIFFERENT rule, `.bk-cal .cell`'s `max-height:
  52px`, written for a 600px grid and dead the entire time the grid was
  rendering at ~285px content width. **That rule was never wrong. The width
  bug kept it unreachable.** Fixing the wrap didn't just widen a grid — it
  let a second, already-correct rule start being true for the first time.
  **THE LESSON, WORTH KEEPING FOR ITS OWN SAKE:** a rule that appears to do
  nothing is not evidence the rule is dead — it can be evidence something
  upstream is lying to it. The next person who finds a CSS rule with no
  visible effect should ask what would have to be true for it to fire
  before deleting it as cruft.
  **SPANISH HELD AT THE NEW WIDTH — the thing a CSS diff alone could never
  have shown, checked live rather than assumed from the static sweep
  above.** *"Paso 5 de 7," "septiembre de 2026,"* the weekday letters *D L
  M M J V S* across the calendar header, *"Elige un día para continuar,"*
  *"Total estimado."* Nothing that used to fit one line reflowed to two.
  **TWO HONEST GAPS, KEPT IN THEIR OWN WORDS RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP TO A
  PASS.** The other session's matrix covers steps one through five at four
  widths; it does not cover steps six and seven at any width — for those
  two the correct sentence is that they have not been compared, not that
  they look fine. And at 768px the calendar block itself was not
  captured — recorded as not-captured, not as a result. **W16's twelve
  steps that do not fit stay untriaged and stay named**, unchanged by
  anything in this item.
  **RESULT 2026-10-10 (ROADMAP 14.24 part 1): steps 6 and 7 compared at 320, 392, 768 and 1440 — nothing overflows, console clean,
  48 of 48 assertions; the 768 calendar is captured.** Full record in 14.24.
  **THE SECOND-INSTANCE SWEEP OF `booking.css`, WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT
  READER DOES NOT HAVE TO REPEAT IT.** Checked every `max-width` in the
  file against its actual parent's `display`, not assumed from the
  selector name: `.bk-wrap` was the only max-width-plus-auto-margin
  element that is itself a flex child with no `width` to let stretch
  reach it. `.bk-header .inner` and `.bk-bar .inner` carry the identical
  `max-width` + `margin: 0 auto` pairing, but their parents (`.bk-header`,
  `.bk-bar`) are plain blocks, not flex containers, so the ordinary CSS
  centring rule applies correctly there — no cross-axis override, nothing
  to collapse. `.bk-lang`'s `margin-left: auto` is a different idiom

The existing words are *"On its way"* and *"Delivered"* with a tick, and `bounced` is red with `detail` beneath it. **Reuse those exact words**; a second vocabulary for the same column is how two screens disagree |

  *"the list is NOT marked busy"* — on a screen that was marked busy for 1.8
  seconds every time. `page.waitForSelector` defaults to `state: "visible"`, and
  Playwright's "visible" means a non-empty bounding box: **the element that
  proves we are still waiting is empty by definition, so it is invisible for
  precisely the interval in which it is true.** `state: "attached"` is the whole
  fix. **It fails toward a FALSE DEFECT**, which is the rarer direction in that
  file and the one that gets working code "fixed" — an hour spent on a loading
  state that was correct, or a height given to an empty container nobody asked
  for. The count moved 106 -> 107 in the same edit, `grep -c "^## "
  docs/gotchas.md` run before and after.

- [ ] **3.1e — the mail log's new scroll box has no edge treatment, and at
  phone width its bottom is underneath the tab bar.** 3.1a bounded the list
  correctly; what nobody specified is what its two edges should look like.
  **Measured 2026-10-09 by the supervisor, at `653bf3b`, mid-scroll (50%), with
  `.manager-shots/3.1a/scroll-*-05.png` as the pictures:**

  **(a) Both edges are a hard cut.** `getComputedStyle(.mail-scroll)` reports
  `mask-image: none`, `padding-top: 0px`, `padding-bottom: 0px`. At 1440 a row
  is sliced **33px** by the top edge — the subject line's descenders are
  visible above the cut with the sender's address orphaned beneath it, directly
  under the Everything / Problems control. It reads as a rendering fault rather
  than as a list you can scroll. No other scrolling surface in this product cuts
  a row mid-sentence against a rounded card.

  **(b) At 392 the box ends 808px down a 844px viewport, and the furniture
  starts at 708.** `.tabscrim` spans **708–844** (a `linear-gradient` to
  `rgb(11, 13, 14)`, `pointer-events: none`) and `.tabbar` spans **776–832**.
  So **100px of the scroll box is painted over by the scrim and 32px of it is
  behind the bar.** The last rows wash out and then disappear while still being
  inside a box that says it is scrollable. **A hit test will not find this** —
  the scrim is `pointer-events: none`, which is `docs/gotchas.md` 100 exactly.

  **Why it happened, in one line:** `max-height: min(60vh, 520px)` takes no
  account of fixed furniture, and this product already has the number —
  **`--tabclear`, `calc(96px + var(--safe-b))`**, which `.app-main` already uses
  as its bottom padding.

  **Fix:** subtract the clearance in the box's own `max-height` rather than
  touching `--tabclear` itself — CLAUDE.md's rule about shared variables, and
  `.app-main` depends on that value — and give the box a top and bottom fade so
  a clipped row reads as "there is more" instead of as a broken row. **Done
  when:** at 1440, 392 and 320, no row is cut by the box's top edge without a
  fade over the cut; the box's bottom sits at or above `.tabscrim`'s top, stated
  as two numbers rather than as "looks fine"; and the check is broken on purpose
  by restoring the unclearanced `max-height` and catches it.
  *Found by the supervisor, 2026-10-09, by looking at 3.1a's own screenshots
  after its 20 assertions had passed. Slice 5 of 3.1.*

  ### FRONT HALF DONE 2026-09-21 — the classification, on the source.
  ### THE BACK HALF — rendering and end-to-end sending — IS NOT DONE.

  **The question this answers, and it had never been asked.** Andrew's ruling at
  the time, **reversed by him on 2026-09-21 and no longer binding — live version
  in `docs/MANAGER-CLOSE-2026-09-21.md` § 2**: *no marketing email, ever. Email
  is receipts, reminders and alerts; anything that sells goes by text.*
  **The classification below is unaffected and is still worth having** — it
  records which of the four kinds each template IS, which is a fact about the
  templates rather than about the rule. What expired is the conclusion that a
  marketing template must not exist. Every template was previously read for
  whether it is CLEAR. None was read for **which of those four it is**. Nothing
  was rendered and nothing was sent this round; nothing was fixed, by
  instruction.

  **HOW EACH CLASSIFICATION WAS ESTABLISHED — evidence, not the function's
  name.** Four tests, applied to every template: (a) **what the button asks
  the reader to do**, which is the sharpest single signal — every call-to-action
  in the file was listed and read together; (b) **whether the subject is a
  booking that already exists**, or a new one being solicited; (c) **whether it
  carries a CAN-SPAM legal footer** (`legal:` passed to `shell`), which is the
  product's own declaration of whether it thinks a mail is marketing; (d) **the
  trigger function and its gate**, read in the sender rather than assumed from
  the template.

  | # | Template | Trigger → who receives it | Class | Evidence |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `customerConfirmationEmail` | `create-booking`, `accept-quote` → customer | **Receipt** | "View your booking" — a booking that now exists |
  | 2 | `invoiceEmail` | `send-invoice` → customer | **Receipt** | money owed or paid for work done; no CTA to buy |
  | 3 | `requestDecisionEmail` · accepted / declined | `respond-to-booking` → customer | **Receipt** | the answer to a request they made |
  | 4 | `requestDecisionEmail` · quote | `respond-to-booking` → customer | **Receipt** | "See it and say yes" — a price for a job THEY asked for. A quote is solicited, so it is not a sale |
  | 5 | `customerReminderEmail` | `send-owner-reminders` sweep → customer | **Reminder** | "View or change your booking" — an appointment already agreed |
  | 6 | `ownerNewBookingEmail` | `create-booking`, `accept-quote` → detailer | **Alert** | "Open the job" — something needs attention |
  | 7 | `ownerNewBookingEmail` reused | `send-owner-reminders` evening-before → detailer | **Reminder** | same template, subject swapped; finding 6 above |
  | 8 | `staleRequestEmail` | `send-owner-reminders` → detailer | **Alert** | "Answer this request" — an unanswered request |
  | 9 | `cancellationEmail` | `cancel-booking`, `update-booking` → both | **Alert** | a state change on an existing booking |
  | 10 | `rescheduleEmail` | `reschedule-booking`, `update-booking` → both | **Alert** | as above |
  | 11 | `planCancelledEmail` | `plan-link` → customer | **Alert** | a plan they held has ended |
  | 12 | `planLinkEmail` | `plan-link` → customer | **Receipt** | "Open your plan" — sent AFTER sign-up, not to solicit one |
  | 13 | `inviteEmail` | `invite-user`, `platform-admin` → staff | **Alert** | "Set up your account" — an account action |
  | 14 | `billingEmail` | `stripe-webhook` → detailer | **Alert** | "Update your card" / "Put your page back online" |
  | 15 | `platformAlertEmail` | `create-business`, `watch-jobs` → platform owner | **Alert** | internal, to Andrew |
  | 16 | `followupEmail` | `send-invoice`, gated `email_customer_followup` → customer | **Neither — see D** | asks for a Google/Yelp review |
  | 17 | `maintenanceDueEmail` | `send-owner-reminders` sweep → customer | **SELLING** | **"Book it in"** for a service not bought |
  | 18 | `campaignEmail` | `send-campaign` → customer | **SELLING** | **"Book again"**; carries unsubscribe + postal address |

  *(Sixteen exported templates; eighteen rows because `requestDecisionEmail`
  and `ownerNewBookingEmail` each classify differently depending on branch or
  caller, which is itself part of the answer.)*

  **IT IS NOT CLEAN. FOUR FINDINGS, NOT FIXED, FOR ANDREW TO RULE ON.**

  **A — `maintenanceDueEmail` sells, is filed with the reminders, and NOTHING
  IN THIS REPO TURNS IT OFF.** This is the "your coating is due" email that
  `docs/MANAGER-CLOSE-2026-09-21.md` records as **off**. Read in the sender:
  its only gate is `settings.email_customer_reminder`
  (`send-owner-reminders/index.ts:389`) — **the same switch that controls
  ordinary appointment reminders.** There is no separate flag, no feature
  gate, and nothing implementing the ruling. Any business with customer
  reminders switched on sends it to any customer with a row in
  `maintenance_deadlines` due within 60 days, at 60/30/14/1 days.
  Its own source comment states the intent plainly: *"the email that gets the
  job booked is the one with the booking link in it."*
  **If it is genuinely off today, it is off by DATA or by something outside
  this repo — a paused schedule, an empty table — and none of that is visible
  here.** That is exactly the class of fact MANAGER-CLOSE exists to record and
  `git log` cannot show. **Not touched. Andrew's call.**

  **B — the legal half, and it falls on A rather than on B.**
  `maintenanceDueEmail` carries **no unsubscribe link and no postal address** —
  it passes no `legal:` block to `shell`, because it sits in the transactional
  set. If it is not transactional, that is the CAN-SPAM problem the ruling
  believed it had retired. It *does* honour suppression (`unsubscribed_at`,
  `email_failed_at`, checked at `:397`), so a customer who opted out elsewhere
  is skipped — **but the email soliciting the sale gives them no way to opt
  out from it.** Suppression honoured, no path offered.
  By contrast `campaignEmail` is the one template that declares itself
  marketing and is legally correct about it: member-gated, **refuses to send
  without a mailing address** (`send-campaign/index.ts:89-90`), and carries
  both the unsubscribe link and the postal address. It contradicts the ruling
  by existing; it does not contradict the law.

  **C — THE SHARPEST ONE, AND IT IS NOT A TEMPLATE AT ALL.** `ownWords()`
  drops a detailer-authored paragraph into **9 call sites across 7 of the 16
  templates** — `confirmation`, `request_received`, `reminder`, `reminder_2`,
  `accepted`, `declined`, `quote`, `receipt`, `invoice`, `followup`,
  `cancelled`, `rescheduled` (12 `MessageKind`s). The text is HTML-escaped and
  otherwise **unconstrained**. So the classification above is a fact about the
  FRAME, not about what arrives: a detailer may type a sales pitch into their
  reminder or their receipt, and the product will deliver it inside a
  transactional email that carries no unsubscribe path. **Nothing anywhere
  checks that content.** This is precisely the shape Andrew named — *a
  reminder that reads as a sale* — and it is the one the ruling cannot reach
  by deleting a template, because the seller is the tenant.

  **D — `followupEmail` is none of the four.** It thanks the customer and asks
  for a Google or Yelp review. It sells nothing, so it is not marketing; it is
  not a receipt, a reminder or an alert either. Gated on
  `email_customer_followup`, no legal footer. **Named rather than filed**,
  because forcing it into a category would be the exact "reads the label
  instead of the contents" error this review exists to avoid. Andrew's ruling
  needed on whether a review request is email or text.

  **WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE.** Nothing was rendered — `render-emails.mjs`
  was not run, it needs a dev server and the browser was another session's this
  round. Nothing was sent, received or read in an inbox, which is this item's
  actual done-when. No fix was applied to any finding. **`supabase/` was read,
  never edited.** The back half stands untouched and this box stays open.

  The earlier runs proved nothing about it — both produced zero reminder
  entries, but `get_bookings_due_for_reminder` returned **0 rows for both
  targets**, so that silence was today's data, not the gate. **A subject was
  made:** one confirmed future booking's `start_at` was moved from
  2026-09-22T16:00Z to one hour ahead of the run, which opened its reminder
  window; the RPC then returned **1**. Restored afterwards.

  **One run, maintenance flag in its normal OFF state, and it shows both
  halves at once:**

  ```
  sweep results [
    {id:"66e794c1…", kind:"owner_reminder",    sent:false, error:"the email relay refused…"},
    {id:"66e794c1…", kind:"customer_reminder", sent:false, error:"the email relay refused…"}
  ]
  ```

  **Both ordinary reminders were produced and handed to the relay, and there
  is still no `maintenance` entry anywhere in that run.** That is the strongest
  form this evidence can take: the same sweep, the same tenant, the same
  moment — **the gate is selective, not a blanket mute.** Neither reminder was
  marked as sent (`"Not marking it as sent"`), and both markers were confirmed
  still `null` afterwards.

  **ALL THREE DIRECTIONS ARE NOW PROVEN.** Flag off → no maintenance email.
  Flag off → ordinary reminders still fire. Flag on → the maintenance email is
  produced. **No email left the machine in any run** — the relay was
  unreachable by construction throughout.

  **STRUCK 2026-10-06 — NO LONGER TRUE; SEE THE CORRECTION AT THE END OF THIS
  SECTION.**
  **A measurement trap worth recording:** the sweep's HTTP response is a
  SUMMARY (`{success, count, summary:{maintenance_failed:1}}`) and carries no
  `results` array. Reading `results` off the response gives `[]` for every run
  — including the one that produced the email. The real per-item results are
  printed to the function's **stdout**. Two runs were briefly misread that way
  before the server log was read.

  **Proven by `tests/maintenance-email-off.test.mjs`, 5 assertions, and broken
  on purpose twice** — deleting the gate and flipping the fallback to `true`
  each turned 0 failures into 3. It asserts ORDER (the gate's index against the
  send's, because a guard after a send is not a guard), that exactly one
  migration adds the column, and that exactly one call site sends the email, so
  a second sender added later fails rather than quietly bypassing this.
  **What that test cannot do is prove an email does not send.** Only a press
  can, and it is queued.

  #### FAULT 1 — THE RESCHEDULE EMAIL TELLS A CUSTOMER WHICH APPOINTMENT TO ATTEND USING A STRIKETHROUGH, AND THE PLAIN-TEXT HALF LOSES IT

  **Template:** `rescheduleEmail` · **customer-facing** · **BOTH languages** ·
  fixture `customer-reschedule`.

  The plain-text alternative, verbatim, English:

  ```
  Hi Dana, your booking with Ridgeline Auto Detail has been moved.
  Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 8:00 AM
  Thursday, September 17, 2026
  10:00 AM – 1:30 PM
  ```

  Spanish, same shape:

  ```
  Hola Dana, tu reserva con Ridgeline Auto Detail cambió de horario.
  sábado, 12 de septiembre de 2026 a las 8:00 AM
  jueves, 17 de septiembre de 2026
  10:00 AM – 1:30 PM
  ```

  **Two datetimes, and not one word saying which is the old one.** A customer
  reads this and cannot tell which day to be home.

  **WHY THE HTML LOOKS FINE AND THE TEXT DOES NOT.** In the HTML the old time is
  marked **only** by styling:

  ```html
  <span style="color:#5E6870; text-decoration:line-through;">Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 8:00 AM</span>
  ```

  `htmlToText` drops both the strikethrough and the grey, because that is what
  converting to text does. **The meaning was carried entirely by a visual
  treatment**, so it survives in exactly one of the two halves the product sends.
  It is also the weaker half for anybody whose client strips styling, and a
  strikethrough is not reliably announced by a screen reader.

  **This is not a translation fault.** It is identical in English and Spanish, and
  it would have been found by reading the English alone. Nobody had read either.

  **THE FIX, NOT APPLIED, AND WHY.** One word before the old time — *"Was"* /
  *"Antes"* — which is a **new** `tt()` string plus its `es.ts` key in the same
  edit. That is new customer-facing copy on a deployed edge function, not a
  correction to an existing string, so it is neither the "one-line string with an
  obvious answer" this sitting was allowed to fix nor something to decide for
  Andrew. **Named precisely so it is a one-commit job for whoever has the lane.**

  ---

  #### FAULT 2 — THE MAINTENANCE EMAIL'S DATE HAS NEVER BEEN RENDERED THE WAY THE PRODUCT PRODUCES IT

  **Templates:** `maintenanceDueEmail`, fixtures `customer-maintenance-far` and
  `customer-maintenance-last` · **customer-facing** · **both languages.**

  Spanish, verbatim: **«Tu Ceramic Pro annual inspection de tu 2021 Tacoma vence
  el 12 October 2026.»** — an **English** date inside a Spanish sentence, and the
  eyebrow above it reads **«Vence el 12 October 2026»**.

  English, verbatim: *"is due by 12 October 2026"* — **day-month-year**, which
  this repo explicitly forbids. `i18n.ts` says the locale is `en-US`/`es-US`
  precisely to keep *"month-before-day. Three things a customer reads as WRONG
  rather than as translated."*

  **THE PRODUCT IS INNOCENT AND THE FIXTURE IS THE FAULT — checked in the sender
  rather than assumed.** `send-owner-reminders/index.ts:433` passes
  `dueOn: formatDateLong(d.due_on, lang)`, and `formatDateLong`
  (`emailKit.ts:197`) calls `toLocaleDateString(intlLocale(lang), …)`, which
  produces *"Thursday, September 17, 2026"* and *"jueves, 17 de septiembre de
  2026"* correctly. **The fixture hard-codes a pre-formatted string,
  `dueOn: "12 October 2026"`**, so the template receives text it cannot reformat.

  **So the consequence is not a bug shipped — it is that these two templates'
  date line has never once been looked at as a customer will see it, in either
  language.** The fixture is in `scripts/render-emails.mjs`, **which this sitting
  was closed out of**, so it is reported rather than fixed. The change is to pass
  `formatDateLong("2026-10-12", LANG)` where the literal now sits, at
  `render-emails.mjs:467` and `:468`.

  > **Tomorrow is the last day** · *"is due by 12 October 2026"*
  > **Mañana es el último día** · *«vence el 12 October 2026»*

  #### FAULT 5 — THE RENDERING INSTRUMENT CANNOT TELL A SPANISH RUN FROM AN ENGLISH ONE. PROVED BY BREAKING IT.

  `node scripts/render-emails.mjs --lang=es` prints **"32 emails"** and exits 0.
  `--lang=en` prints **"32 emails"** and exits 0. **Nothing in either run
  distinguishes them, and 14 of the Spanish 32 are English.**

  **THE SABOTAGE.** One Spanish key deleted from
  `_shared/strings/es.ts` — `"You're booked in · {date}"` — then the Spanish run
  repeated:

  * **2 output files changed**, so the sabotage genuinely reached the render
    (`docs/gotchas.md` #80: a sabotage that never arrives reports the same word as
    a real hole);
  * the customer subject became **«You're booked in · jueves, 17 de septiembre de
    2026»** — half English, half Spanish, on a customer-facing email;
  * **the run printed "32 emails" and exited 0.**

  `T()` is `(cat && cat[english]) || english` — it falls back to the English key
  and returns successfully, which is the documented mechanism and is why nothing
  errors. **Same family as `docs/gotchas.md` #82 and 8.3's own finding: a language
  pass must prove it rendered the language, or it measures English twice.**
  `es.ts` was restored and the tree confirmed clean.

  **What would close it:** the run asserting a declared count of templates that
  MUST differ from their English render, the way `contrast-insitu.mjs` was widened
  on 2026-09-23. That is a `scripts/` change and is not this sitting's.

  #### NOT VERIFIED, AND THE REASON IS A RULE RATHER THAN A SHORTAGE OF TIME

  **The money.** Every Spanish and English render shows `5% sale | -$20` /
  `5% de oferta | -$20` over lines of `$360 + $25 + $20`, where 5% of $405 is
  **$20.25**. So the label states 5% and the figure beside it is 4.94%.

  **I am not calling that a fault and I am not calling it fine.**
  `docs/gotchas.md` **#81 is my own entry**: `render-emails.mjs` prints PASS over a
  wrong subtotal **by design**, because `reconcile()` invents a closing line for
  any gap, so its money tie-out balances either way. **Its PASS is not evidence
  about money.** The instrument for this exact question is
  `scripts/discount-label.mjs` — *"a label that states a percentage is making a
  claim the figure beside it has to keep"* — and it needs a dev server and a
  browser, which are DP Cowork's this sitting.

  **What IS worth recording:** the figure is computed by the real pricing engine
  (`computeQuote`, `siteDiscountPercent: 5`), not typed into the fixture — which is
  ROADMAP 14.19's lesson already applied here. So the open question is rounding
  against a stated percentage, not a fabricated number.

- [ ] **4.1 — One tap completes a job, with no confirmation and no undo.**

  **4.1 (f) — THE CONFIRMATION IS PAINTED IN THE LIVERY OF THE BUTTON IT IS
  PROTECTING AGAINST. Found by the supervisor 2026-10-08, measured on both
  surfaces at both widths, in the browser, at `cfd8932`.**

  The two Decline confirmations added by `cfd8932` pass no `confirmClassName`,
  so they take `ConfirmTap`'s default — `btn primary`, the accent fill. On the
  request card on Today, and on the job record's pending bar, that puts **two
  buttons with the identical accent fill on the same surface, meaning opposite
  things**: "Accept" and "Yes, decline it".

  Measured, not read off a screenshot — computed `backgroundColor` of every
  visible button while the question is open:

  | Surface | Width | Accent-filled buttons | Gap |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Request card (Today) | 1440x900 | `Accept` and `Yes, decline it`, both `rgb(14, 165, 233)` | 101px |
  | Request card (Today) | 392x844 | the same two, same value | 101px |
  | Job record (pending bar) | 1440x900 | the same two of **12** visible buttons | 155px |
  | Job record (pending bar) | 392x844 | the same two of **12** visible buttons | 155px |

  **Why this is a defect and not taste.** `docs/design-system.md` § Composition:
  *"three or more actions take three weights — filled, ringed, ringless — because
  a set where everything is equally loud has no first thing, and a destructive
  action weighted the same as a convenience is a hazard, not a neutral choice."*
  And `RequestCard.jsx`'s own header comment records that this exact card broke
  the one-accent-fill rule once before and was fixed for it: *"ONLY THE LIT
  CARD'S ACCEPT IS FILLED … put two accent buttons on one screen."*

  **And it is sharpest precisely where this item is pointed.** 4.1 exists to stop
  a mis-aimed thumb declining a job. The step it added asks the right question in
  the right words — and then paints *yes, decline it* in the same blue as
  *Accept*, 101px away, on a card the item's own comment says is read one-handed.
  The guard is correct; its answer is dressed as the thing it is guarding.

  **Done when:** on both surfaces, at 1440 and 392, **exactly one accent fill is
  on the surface while the question is open**, measured as computed
  `backgroundColor` rather than by eye, with the console read at both.

  **Recommendation, and it reopens no ruling:** make the two Decline answers
  **ringed, not filled** — pass a `confirmClassName` that is not `btn primary`.
  **Do not reach for `btn danger`**: `docs/screen-rules.md` rules that "Didn't
  show up" and "Cancel the job" deliberately do NOT take `--bad`, because they
  are outcomes a detailer can live with rather than deletions, and a decline is
  the same kind of thing. Ringed satisfies the three-weights rule without
  touching that ruling. The supervisor did not make the change because the exact
  weight is a composition call the next worker should make with the screen open,
  not a one-word substitution made from a table.

  **What the supervisor DID reproduce of `cfd8932`, so this is read as one
  defect and not a verdict on the item:** both surfaces ask before they act, at

  rather than on the destructive answer; the question takes 375px of a 413px card

  errors or warnings at both widths on both surfaces.**
  `tests/confirm-questions.test.mjs` passes 6/6 and

  before, and when** — read off the row, never off the screen.

  *A1 P0-06*

  **MEASURED FIRST, 2026-09-20 — WHAT THE TAP ACTUALLY DID.** It wrote
  `status: 'completed'` through `update-booking` on the first touch, from
  **two** screens: the card on Today, where it is the accent-filled button on
  the next job of the day, and the job record. What that press costs:
  * it does **NOT** email the customer — only a cancellation or a move does;
  * it does **NOT** silence their reminder — the reminder rule excludes
    `cancelled` and `pending`, not `completed`;
  * it **does** push the owner's phone, unlock **Finalize payment**, move the
    job into Today's "needs paying" pile, and count it as done in Money, the
    reports and the client's history;
  * and there was **no way back**: once completed the button vanishes and only
    "Didn't show up" and "Cancel the job" remain. A cancellation has
    "Un-cancel"; a completion had nothing.

  **THE UNDO NEEDED NO SERVER CHANGE, which is why this was buildable during
  the deploy freeze.** `status` is an ordinary editable field on
  `update-booking` with no transition guard, and "Un-cancel" has been writing
  `confirmed` through it all along. The way back existed everywhere except on
  the screen.

  **NOT THE DELETE PATTERN, AND THE RULES SAY WHY.** This item says to copy
  the job page's delete-behind-a-fold with `.btn.danger`.
  `docs/screen-rules.md` names that as the reference for a DESTRUCTIVE action
  and, in the same paragraph, says "Didn't show up" and "Cancel the job"
  deliberately do NOT take `--bad` because they are outcomes a detailer can
  live with. Completing a job is the commonest outcome in the product.
  Painting it as harm would weaken `--bad` everywhere it currently means
  something, and a fold would tax every correct press to stop a rare wrong
  one. **So it asks in place instead** — `components/ConfirmTap.jsx`, one
  control, both screens, no modal, because this is used one-handed in a
  driveway.

  the ONE changed field, never the booking row**, because a booking carries a customer's name, phone and address and an append-only copy
  of them could never be erased by `delete-customer`. A reopen from completed, cancelled or no-show is recorded as `job.reopen`, since an

  ***APPEND-ONLY TRIGGER NOW PROVED ON A REAL POSTGRES THAT IS NOT OURS, 2026-10-06 (DP Cowork2, Lane B), AT THE MANAGER'S REQUEST, with no live database, no browser and no `app/src`.***
  `tests/action-log-sql.test.mjs` applies `20261006050000_action_log.sql` to **PGlite** (`@electric-sql/pglite`, real PostgreSQL 18.3 compiled to
  WebAssembly, in-process, nothing on disk) and runs nine cases: the migration applies and applies twice; a row writes; **UPDATE, DELETE and
  TRUNCATE are each refused with the table's own message and the row is unchanged**; the table's check and `not null` constraints refuse a
  bad subject and a missing before or after; RLS is enabled and forced, there is no policy, and neither `anon` nor `authenticated` holds any
  privilege (a `SET ROLE` insert is refused); and **each guard removed alone lets exactly its own thing through**: no
  update/delete trigger lets UPDATE and DELETE through (TRUNCATE still refused), no truncate trigger lets TRUNCATE through, a function that
  does not raise guards nothing, the revoke removed gives `anon` the privilege back (row-level security alone still refuses the row, so the
  two walls are separate and each is shown), and with the revoke and RLS both removed `anon` writes. **9 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.**
  **HOW PGLITE IS INSTALLED, DECIDED ON PURPOSE:** this repo has no root `package.json` and no pattern for a dev dependency in tests, and
  `app/package.json` is the Vite app's, so it is **not added to any `package.json`**. It is installed in a folder outside the repo and found
  through `PGLITE_DIR`; without it the cases print `NOT RUN` with the install line and are skipped, and with `PGLITE_REQUIRED=1` they
  **fail**, so a run that must have it cannot pass without it (checked both ways). **Two fixtures, said in the file:** the roles `anon` and
  `authenticated` (plain Postgres has neither), and Supabase's default grant of every new public table to both, without which the revoke
  could never be seen to work. **Not proved:** Supabase's own extensions, and anything about the live project, which was not touched.

  **What matches.** `ConfirmTap` asks for no-show (`BookingDetail.jsx:805`), cancel (`:831`), remove (`:865`) and, through `FinalizeModal.jsx:229`, waive; each names customer, service and time through one

  **Gaps, in the order they matter:**
  1. **The cancel question can say something false.** `BookingDetail.jsx:835` (and `appEs.js:2372`) always says *"The customer is emailed."*, but `update-booking/index.ts:239` sends only when the booking has a

  2. **Spanish names the record wrongly for some services and some hours.** `appEs.js:2368` hard-codes the article and the preposition: *"el {service} de {name} de las {time}"*. The service is the detailer's own word, so a

  unless it is his own business"* — **and an exception is a thing somebody
  removes later while tidying**, at which point Andrew is locked out of his
  own product by a policy that reads as though it were doing its job.

  **The location rule needs no exception at all.** Same person, same account,
  two different answers: acting inside somebody else's business is true for a
  support view and false for Andrew in his own dashboard, whatever either of
  them *is*. **It also makes the banner honest — it tells you WHERE you are,
  not WHO you are**, and where-you-are is the fact the failure mode turns on.
  Somebody forgetting they are a platform admin harms nothing; somebody
  forgetting which account they are in is the whole defect.

  harness cannot explain is not evidence. The fix was to call each function
  TWICE by the same actor with the same shape — once at A's own tenant, once
  at B's. Only the pair says anything:

      self 2xx + cross refused  -> isolation proved by rejection
      self 2xx + cross 2xx      -> a leak
      self NOT 2xx              -> the front door is shut to A as well, so the

    longer comes back carrying B's data, the canary does not fire, and

    skips and **0** are proved by rejection, which is the proof that the self
    call is load-bearing rather than decorative.

  AND THAT LIMIT IS NOT GLOSSED.** A function that trusts a tenant id from its
  caller would be the ideal control, and deploying one is publishing, which is

  **ROUND TWO — READING EACH FUNCTION'S OWN VALIDATION BRANCH, 2026-09-20.**
  Guessing values by field name got 15 of 39 through the front door and then
  stopped: the rest answered a bare `400`, which says *you are missing
  something* and not what. **So the guard that produced it is read instead.**
  Every one of these functions rejects in the same shape —
  `if (!thing) return json({ error: … }, 400)` — and the identifiers inside
  that negation ARE the required fields.

  Two things came out of that, and the second matters more than the first.

  1. **THE BODY IS BUILT FROM THE UNION** of what the function READS (the
     request shape, discovered from source) and what it INSISTS ON (the 400
     guards). Neither alone gets through the door: `owner-push-subscribe`
     takes its subscription as a nested object, so `p256dh` and `auth` never
     appeared in the destructure, while its own guard names them both.
  2. **A SKIP NOW NAMES THE FIELD RATHER THAN THE STATUS.** *"rejects on
     `domain_id`, which this harness does not supply"* is a piece of work
     somebody can pick up. *"400"* is a shrug. Where the guards name nothing
     missing, the skip says so — the refusal is then a lookup, a permission or
     a precondition on the row, which is a different kind of work.

  **THE THREE NUMBERS AFTER ROUND TWO: 15-16 RAN · 23-24 REFUSE · 7 PROVED.**

  **A RANGE, BECAUSE TWO CONSECUTIVE RUNS DISAGREED BY ONE AND THE SINGLE
  FIGURE WAS COMMITTED BEFORE THE SECOND RUN FINISHED.** One foreground run
  gave 16/23/7 and the next gave 15/24/7. The cause is the product's own rate
  limiter: `create-booking` answers **429** once the replay has been run
  repeatedly, so whether it gets through its front door depends on how recently
  somebody ran this. **The PROVED number — 7 — did not move in either run**,
  which is the one that matters, because it is the count of functions that
  demonstrably work for A and refuse B.

  Writing the single figure down first was the same error as the nine emails,
  one notch smaller: a number stated from one observation as though it were
  settled. It is a range, and the range is what goes in the file.

  **AND THE SAME LESSON COST A RESULT FOR THE THIRD TIME.** Seeding a
  `business_invites` row so `accept-invite` had a token to present made
  `invite-user` start answering 409 — it invites the sink address too, and an
  address already invited is a conflict — so a function that had PROVED it
  refuses tenant B silently became a skip. The seeded invite now uses its own
  reserved `example.com` address. **Three times in one script: a fixture that
  makes one function testable must not quietly make another untestable**, and
  the only reason it was caught each time is that the per-function line prints
  A's OWN status beside the cross-tenant one.

  | `accept-invite` | `business_invites`, `business_users` |

  NOT THIS PRODUCT'S RATE LIMIT AT ALL.** It was the only refusal here nobody
  could name, and a 429 handed to every actor including the service role is the

  every keystroke of the address field. Measured:

  - **The function's own three limits never refused anything today.** `rate_take`

    the function's code did not get far enough to run.
  - **Geoapify cannot produce it either.** The provider seam maps every failure
    it has to `unavailable`, which this function returns as **503**. There is
    exactly one 429 in the file and it is the limiter's.
  - **It is not latched.** It answers 200 right now to a single call, to a

  **AND HERE IS THE EVIDENCE TO BUILD IT FROM — 2026-09-21.** Four controls
  were pressed with `elementFromPoint` across **8 back-office screens at two
  widths** (Clients, Money, Calendar, Today, Hours, Booking rules, Promos,
  Monthly plans; 320x844 and 1254x720). It found **one control under the 44px
  absolute** — `.btn.sm` at 43 on Hours at 320 — **introduced by a commit
  made the same night.** The full numbers and the method are in **2.5**.

  **NONE OF IT WAS REACHABLE BY ANYTHING THIS REPO OWNS.** The four
  credential-free suites do not open these screens at all. And for anyone
  tempted to write the cheap version: **a bounding rect reports 36 or 38 on
  every one of these controls and is wrong every time** — so a rect-based
  gate files four defects that do not exist and still misses the one that
  does.

  **WHAT A REAL GATE HAS TO DO — all six learned by getting them wrong first:**
  1. **Probe the pointer, never the rect.** Non-negotiable; see above.
  2. **Open every `<details>` first.** 29 of 41 `.choice` controls on Booking
     rules sit inside two closed foldrows that still report full-size rects.
     A gate that skips them **prints clean over 71% of its population.**
  3. **Sweep sub-pixel offsets, not whole-pixel scrolls.** A whole-pixel
     scroll leaves the fraction identical, so the rounding never moves and
     the gate measures one position ten times over.
  4. **Measure the PITCH, not just the size.** The only real defect found was
     two enlarged bands overlapping — **every individual size was legal.**
  5. **Carry a calibration target.** A synthetic known-44 and known-46 box in
     the live page is what proved the probe could tell them apart, and what
     proved *43 is not reachable for a 44px band at any device scale factor*,
     correcting the mechanism 2.5 was written on.
  6. **Say what it did not measure, as `n of N`.** Three separate faults in
     this session's own probe were invisible until it printed its coverage.

  **AND THE RE-RUN THAT WROTE THE COMMITTED RECEIPT FOUND A REAL FLAW IN THE
  CANARY ITSELF — CAUGHT BECAUSE IT WAS RE-RUN, NOT TRUSTED FROM THE FIRST
  PASS.** Re-running against the just-committed SHA (so the receipt's own
  commit fields would be honest) failed twice in a row: the break was caught
  8/8 times across every trial, every time — the tap-probe detection was
  never in question — but the RESTORE check read `subjects=6` before the
  break and `subjects=8` after, and called that a fault of its own.
  **Root cause, found with a 6-trial standalone harness rather than guessed
  at:** the admin Today tab's "Detailers who need a call" panel is an async
  fetch, and `settle()`'s 2.2-second cap can return before that round trip
  lands — so the BEFORE snapshot was sometimes taken early and the AFTER
  snapshot, five break/undo cycles and several seconds later, was not. Nothing
  about the break caused the drift; two unrelated, real controls loaded in
  between. **Fixed with `page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")` before the
  baseline, not a longer guessed sleep** — 6/6 in the standalone harness
  after the fix, then 3/3 more on the real check end to end. The earlier
  report to Andrew this session (five-of-five, "restored cleanly") was true
  of the runs it was measured on and has now been reproduced reliably rather
  than left resting on that one pass — the same standard just applied to the
  "four items" claim, applied to this session's own new code.

- [ ] **4.7 — Once a job is finalized, a recorded payment can never be changed
  back.** A detailer finishes a job, says how it was paid — paid, part paid, not
  yet, or waived — and presses Finalize. **From that moment the choice is
  permanent as far as this product is concerned.** Picking the wrong one is one
  tap. There is no tap that undoes it.

  **What happens today**, read at `2c0308a` on 2026-10-07.
  `FinalizeModal.jsx:100-105` writes `payment_status` and stamps `finalized_at`
  in the same call. `BookingDetail.jsx:368` offers Finalize only while
  `status === "completed" && !finalized_at`, so **the modal that set the payment
  is gone the moment it has set it**, and the record offers nothing in its place.
  The only other screen that writes a payment state is Money's chase list, and
  `Money.jsx:275` asks only for jobs whose state is `pending` or `partial` — so a
  job marked **paid** or **waived** appears on no list that can change it.
  **The server would allow it.** `payment_status` and `finalized_at` are both in
  `update-booking`'s editable fields (`update-booking/index.ts:70-72`) with no
  guard on either, and the state's own check constraint
  (`20260827000200_tenant_data.sql:257`) accepts all four values in any order.
  **So nothing is protecting anything. The way back was simply never drawn.**

  **Why it matters, and the waived case is the sharp one.** `waived` means the
  detailer gave the work away. `moneyAdvanced.js:245` keeps a waived job in
  **owed** at its quoted price, deliberately, *"rather than being quietly written
  off where nobody can see it"* — so a job waived by accident sits in what the
  customer owes for ever, the dashboard goes on saying that money is outstanding,
  and the detailer can still invoice for it. **The mirror mistake is as bad in
  the other direction:** a job marked **paid** by mistake drops off the chase
  list and nobody is ever asked about it again. Neither is a database fault and
  neither is recoverable from any screen a detailer can reach.

  **The audit trail for this already exists**, which is what makes it a small fix
  rather than a design question. `_shared/actionLog.ts` already records a waive as
  a `payment_status` change carrying its before and its after
  (`20261006050000_action_log.sql:5`), and that table is append-only. **A
  correction has somewhere to be written down on the day it is built.**

  **Done when:** from a finalized job's own record a detailer can change its
  payment state to any of the four values and back again, **and that is not a
  second Finalize** — `finalized_at` does not move and the line items are not
  rewritten; **the change writes an `action_log` row naming the before and the
  after**, the way a waive does today, so a correction is exactly as visible as
  the original; and the destructive-action pattern in `docs/screen-rules.md`
  guards the two choices that can lose money, so neither is one unguarded tap.
  **What failing looks like, and it is the obvious build:** a *"correct the
  payment"* control that simply re-opens the Finalize modal — which stamps
  `finalized_at` again, rewrites the line items, and makes the audit say the job
  was finalized twice.

  *Found 2026-10-07 by DP Cowork while sweeping 4.1 at `2c0308a`; written up by
  DP Cowork2 the same day, not built. Wave 4 is the risk band — a state change
  with no way back — and the order inside a wave in this document is numeric, so
  it sits at the end of the wave rather than beside 4.1, which is its sibling:
  4.1 is one tap that completes a job with no undo, and this is the money half of
  the same shape.*

  **BUILT 2026-10-07 (DP Cowork, Lane A), commit `0f62d9d`. NOT TICKED, and the
  clause that is missing is Andrew's twice over.** "Correct how it was paid" sits
  under *The money* on a finalized record: a fold, copy saying what each of the
  four states does to the chase list and to what the customer owes, the shared
  `Segmented`, and one question naming the job and both sides of the change.

  **It sends ONE field**, which is this entry's own named way to fail — no
  `finalized_at`, no line items, no `status`. Measured by pressing, on
  `demo-detail` as the owner, Marcus Webb $65, restored afterwards: finalized as
  **Waived** through the real modal, then **waived → paid → unpaid → part paid**.
  `finalized_at` stayed `02:04:02.895` and `final_amount` stayed `65` across all
  three corrections. Money read between every press — earned **$255** throughout;
  collected **$0 → $65 → $0 → $0**; still owed **$255 → $190 → $255 → $255**;
  chase list **3 rows/$255 → 2/$190** on the waive, **2/$190** on paid, **3/$255**
  the moment it went back to unpaid, **3/$255** on part paid. **The job reappears
  on the chase list**, which is the half of the fault nothing else could reach.

  **Three refusals, each pressed rather than reasoned about:** no control at all on
  a job that was never finalized (Finalize is offered instead); **no answer button
  while the pick has not moved**, so nothing can write a no-op or file a row saying
  a payment changed from paid to paid; and another tenant's booking through
  `update-booking` as this owner answers **404** with that row unchanged.

  **The destructive-action pattern is all three of its parts.** Behind a fold;
  copy that says what each direction does; and `.btn.danger` on **Paid** and

  ### READ COLD BY DP COWORK2, 2026-10-07 — ONE REAL FAULT, AND IT IS A MIS-TAP ONTO THE WRONG JOB

  *A second session that did not build this read the code and the test as a
  stranger and tried to break them on paper. **The money arithmetic holds** —
  see the end of this block. **One fault is confirmed and it can waive the wrong
  job.** No `app/src` was touched.*

  **THE FAULT: `payPick` IS NEVER RESET WHEN THE RECORD OPENS ON A DIFFERENT
  JOB.** `BookingDetail.jsx:116` declares `const [payPick, setPayPick] =
  useState(null)` and nothing clears it on a booking change. `payWant = payPick
  ?? booking.payment_status` (`:414`) therefore keeps the state a person picked
  for the PREVIOUS job, the answer button appears because that pick differs from
  the new job's status, and **one press writes the previous job's chosen state
  onto the job now on screen.** The two states that can arrive this way include
  **Waived**, which this block itself marks `.btn.danger` because it loses money.

  **AND THE GUARD FOR EXACTLY THIS HAZARD IS NINETY LINES AWAY, IN THIS FILE,
  WRITTEN THE SAME EVENING.** ROADMAP 6.4's app half added
  `useEffect(() => { sendKey.current = null; }, [booking.id]);` at
  `BookingDetail.jsx:339`, with a comment saying *"A DIFFERENT BOOKING IS A
  DIFFERENT INTENT … the record is reused in place"*. **`payPick` is the same
  shape of state and got no such line.** Two blocks in one file, one guarded and
  one not.

  **WHERE IT IS REACHABLE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT A FAULT RATHER
  THAN A WORRY.** On the job page — `main.jsx:150` routes `/job/:id` to a single
  `<JobPage />`, and `JobPage.jsx:76` renders `BookingDetail` **bare: no
  `RecordHost`, no `key`**. React Router keeps the element mounted when only the
  param changes, so `useParams()` returns the new id, `load()` replaces
  `booking`, and **`BookingDetail` is never remounted.** Browser Back and
  Forward between two job pages is enough; a push notification tapped while a
  job page is open is the other way in, and ROADMAP 14.34 pointed push links at
  this very route.

  **ON THE DASHBOARD IT IS SAVED, BY SOMETHING THAT IS NOT ABOUT STATE AT ALL.**
  `RecordHost.jsx:115` wraps the record's body in
  ``<div className="record-body swap" key={`b-${title}|${subtitle}`}>``, so
  choosing another job in the wide two-column layout changes that key and React
  mounts a fresh `BookingDetail` — `payPick` goes with it. **That key is
  documented at `RecordHost.jsx:77`–`:100` as existing to RE-RUN THE ANIMATION**
  (the owner's own "it just looks like a page refresh" note), not to reset
  state. **So 4.7's correctness on four of five screens rests on an animation
  device in another file, and neither file says so.** Simplify that key for any
  reason and the mis-tap arrives on Today, Calendar, Money and Clients too.

  **AND THAT KEY CAN COLLIDE.** It is `title|subtitle` =
  `customer_name` + `"<date> · <start> – <end>"` (`BookingDetail.jsx:90`–`:93`).
  **Two bookings for the same customer at the same date and time produce the
  same key**, so no remount happens and both leaks are live.
  `RecordHost.jsx:96` asserts *"two different jobs cannot collide"* — that is
  true of two different customers and unproved for one customer twice in a slot.
  **Not measured here** (it needs two such rows and a browser, and the demo
  tenant was being measured by the other lane); the experiment is two bookings
  for one customer at one slot, switch between them at wide width, and read
  whether the pick survives.

  **THE SUGGESTED FIX IS ONE LINE AND IT IS NOT MINE TO WRITE** (`app/src` is
  Lane A's): either give `payPick` the same reset `sendKey` has —
  `useEffect(() => { setPayPick(null); }, [booking.id]);` — or key the whole
  record on `booking.id` at the one call site that renders it bare
  (`JobPage.jsx:76`), which fixes both blocks at once and removes the need for
  6.4's effect. **The first is smaller; the second is the root cause.**

  ***FIXED 2026-10-08 (DP Cowork, Lane A), `96d7eb6`. The first form, plus the
  correction the second form was really pointing at.*** `payPick` now resets on
  `booking.id` beside `sendKey`'s identical line, so correctness lives in the
  component that needs it rather than in another file's animation key. And
  `RecordHost.jsx`'s assertion that *"two different jobs cannot collide"* is
  **struck and corrected in place**: the key is `customer_name` plus
  `"<date> · <start> – <end>"`, so two bookings for one customer in one slot
  share it. The note now says what the key is for — the swap animation — and
  that nothing may lean on it for correctness, because both pieces of
  per-booking state in `BookingDetail.jsx` reset themselves.

  **REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT TO REPRODUCE IT WAS
  WRONG IN THE MOST ORDINARY WAY.** `page.goto` is a full document load, so the
  component remounted and the walk reported **0 answer buttons with the fix
  REMOVED** — a sabotage that proved nothing, and it would have been written up
  as "could not reproduce" by anybody who stopped there. React Router keeps the
  element mounted only across a CLIENT-SIDE transition, so the history is driven
  in the page and real `history.back()` / `history.forward()` fire popstate,
  which is what a thumb on the browser's own arrows does.

  | on `/job/:id`, pick **Waived** on job A, then Back and Forward onto job B | answer buttons live on B |
  |---|---|
  | reset removed | **1** — segment marked *Waived* / *Perdonado* while B's pill reads *Paid* / *Pagado* |
  | reset in place | **0** — segment marked *Paid* / *Pagado*, matching the pill |

  Both at 1440 English and 392 Spanish, console clean, and **both bookings read
  back unchanged**: the proof is that there is nothing left to press, so nothing
  was ever written. Frames in `.manager-shots/4.7-fix/`.

  **AND THE CONTROL BROKE 3 + 1 AT 392 IN SPANISH — sent back from the 392
  frame, fixed in `bb09f5e`.** The two-column rule written for 320 lived inside
  `max-width: 360px`, so between **361 and 430** the control was still the base
  `inline-flex` and a wrap filled the first row and dropped the remainder,
  leaving *"Perdonado"* alone under three others. **A wrap is always 3 + 1 for
  four items**; the grid makes the break even, which is this stylesheet's own
  "a pair becomes a stack" answer and the same shape its six-option rule takes.
  **431 is measured, not chosen:** the four Spanish labels want **395px** of
  control (74 + 125 + 85 + 94 plus gaps and padding) and the control gets the
  viewport less 36px of page gutter, so one row fits from 431 up. Swept before
  and after at 320 / 360 / 361 / 392 / 420 / 460 / 500 / 560 / 620 / 700 / 768 /
  900 / 1180 / 1440 / 1920: **before, 3 + 1 across 361–420; after, 2x2 at and
  below 420 and one row at and above 460, with no 3 + 1 at any width.** English
  wants 296px and fits on one row at every width down to 320, so it is untouched
  at all fifteen — which keeps the earlier item's *"nothing that fits today
  moves"* true. Re-shot at 392 and 768 Spanish: 392 is 2x2 with every button
  173x36, each label on one line and each its own topmost element by hit test;
  768 is one row of four at their natural widths. Frames in
  `.manager-shots/4.7-fix/`.

  **AND THE CHECK THAT WAS MISSING WHILE SEVEN WENT GREEN NOW EXISTS.**
  `tests/payment-correction.test.mjs` gains **3a** and the
  `PAYMENT_BREAK=no-reset` sabotage: **8 pass clean, and all seven sabotages go
  red on exactly the check aimed at them.** Every earlier question was about the
  block's SHAPE — is it there, does it send one field, does it refuse a no-op —
  and none of them could see state surviving a booking change, because none of
  them knew there was a second booking. It also pins `RecordHost`'s corrected
  sentence, so the old assumption cannot be re-derived from the old words.

  **WHAT THE EXISTING CHECK SAYS ABOUT THIS: nothing, and it is green.**
  `node --test tests/payment-correction.test.mjs` → **7 passed, 0 failed**, and
  the seven are the block's presence, the one-field write, the `finalized_at`
  gate, the no-op refusal, the three parts of the destructive pattern, the
  Spanish keys and the server's audit branch. **None of them is about state
  surviving a change of booking**, and no sabotage in `PAYMENT_BREAK` can reach
  it. That is not a criticism of the suite's six sabotages; it is the gap.

  **WHAT WAS CHECKED AND HELD, SAID SO IT IS NOT RE-CHECKED:**
  * **The money figures in the build note are internally consistent and agree
    with the declared rule.** `app/src/lib/moneyAdvanced.js:240`–`:252` (ROADMAP
    14.7) says **only `paid` counts as collected**, while `partial` and `waived`
    stay in `owed` — partial because nothing in the database records how much
    moved, waived because it is work given away at the quoted price. Every
    reading in the build note follows from `owed = earned − collected` with
    `collected` counting `paid` alone: waived → collected $0, owed $255; paid →
    $65 and $190; unpaid → $0 and $255; part paid → $0 and $255. **The chase
    list is a different question and a different number** —
    `Money.jsx:275` filters `payment_status in ('pending','partial')`, which is
    why the waived job leaves the list while its $65 stays inside `owed`.
  * **`payment_notes: null` really does clear the note.**
    `update-booking/index.ts:117` copies any field that is `!== undefined`, and
    `payment_notes` is in `EDITABLE_FIELDS` at `:71`. A `null` is applied rather
    than skipped, so "How they paid: Cash" cannot survive a correction to Unpaid
    or Waived.
  * **The refusals are where the note says they are:** `canCorrectPayment =
    !!booking.finalized_at`, and the answer button is behind `payWant !==
    booking.payment_status`.


## Wave 5 — Money truth

Both audits independently reached the same conclusion here, which makes it the
most corroborated finding in the set.

- [x] **5.1 — DONE 2026-09-17, resolved by 14.7. Evidence
  `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 14.7.** The screen called unpaid work "brought in" and
  the figure derived from it "net/kept". Measured again on the demo business:
  $810 earned, $515 collected, $295 still owed, so the headline read $285 over
  a cash position of −$10.
  **Now:** headline *Earned less expenses this month*, cells *Earned* /
  *Expenses* / *Avg job* / *Jobs done*, and **Collected $515** beside **Still
  owed $295** underneath them, where $515 + $295 = $810. The back office says
  *earned*, not *taken*. Pressing *Mark paid* on the $65 job moved COLLECTED
  $515 → $580 and STILL OWED $295 → $230 with EARNED unchanged; the row was
  put back to `pending` afterwards.
  **TWO PARTS OF THIS ITEM WERE OVERRULED BY 14.7 AND THAT IS ON PURPOSE.**
  *"Net is computed from collected money only"* — no: net stays accrual,
  because the six-bar chart the headline sits on, the *vs last month* delta,
  the tour step and the accountant CSV all count work done in the period, and a
  cash-basis headline would disagree with the chart under it. So marking a job
  paid does NOT move the net; it moves the pair beside it. *"Expenses paid"* —
  no: an expense row has no paid/unpaid column, so that label would be a new
  unverifiable claim replacing an honest one. It stays *Expenses*.
  *A1 P1-01, A2 4.1 — settled by 14.7*

- [x] **5.2 — DONE 2026-09-18. Evidence `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 5.2.** The
  headline compared a part-finished period against a whole one: on the 18th of
  September the demo business read *down $903 vs $853 last month*, seventeen
  days of one month measured against thirty-one days of another. `periods.js`
  had warned against exactly this in its own header since it was written.
  **CHOSEN: TRIM, NOT HIDE.** Hiding the comparison until the period closes
  would remove it for up to 30 days at a stretch on Month and 364 on Year —
  absent on every day a detailer could act on it, present on the one day they
  could not. Trimming is also what every dashboard means by month-to-date.
  **Now:** *down $792 vs $742 at this point last month*, and the label says
  *at this point* only while the period is running — a finished period still
  compares with the whole of the one before it. Eight new labels, nine new
  Spanish keys. `previousSoFar()` in `lib/periods.js` is the one place that
  decides, so the advanced screen's own arrows move with the headline.
  Check: `tests/mid-period-comparison.test.mjs`, 87 assertions, broken on
  purpose nine ways and all nine caught.
  *A2 4.2*

- [x] **5.3 — DONE 2026-09-18. Evidence `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 5.3.**
  Receipts and invoices were not findable, and a real $195 test payment is

  the receipt refuses the run. So the business's records can be taken out,

  **WHAT IS RUNNING.** A `pg_cron` job, `probe-live-site`, every five minutes.

  ping URL are configuration, not schema, and are deliberately not in the
  migration because one carries an API key and the other is a credential.

  **NOTHING WAS DEPLOYED. NO EDGE FUNCTION WAS TOUCHED, PUBLISHED OR CHANGED.**

  **THE FOUR PATHS, AND WHAT EACH ONE DOES AND DOES NOT FIRE ON.** Andrew's
  ruling governs this table: *"if he gets an email that something failed he is
  not going to do anything about it"*, so **a check that can cry wolf is worse
  than no check.**

  | path | what it proves | it fires when | it deliberately does NOT fire when |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `homepage` | Netlify is serving a real build | two cycles in a row where the body does not contain `assets/index-` | one slow fetch; a redeploy changing the hash — the assertion is the prefix, not the hash |
  | `booking_start` | the tenant profile the booking page loads first — Postgres, a definer RPC, PostgREST | two cycles where the RPC does not return opening hours | a tenant having odd hours; RLS refusing some *other* table |
  | `booking_availability` | the edge runtime computing real slots | two cycles where the function does not answer `"success":true` | **a fully booked day** — the assertion is on `success`, never on the number of slots, because no free slots is not an outage |
  | `sign_in` | the authentication service is answering | two cycles where it does not identify itself | a wrong password, a locked account, a rate-limited login — **this probe carries no credentials at all**, so no user-specific failure can trip it |

  **AND THREE WOLVES WERE DESIGNED OUT RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED:**

  - **A response that has not arrived is INCONCLUSIVE, never a failure.**
  - **If nothing could be graded, the ping is WITHHELD rather than sent.** A
    success ping we could not justify is the worst thing available here — a
    monitor reporting green because it did not look. Observed on the very
    first run: `{"ping":"withheld — nothing could be graded this cycle"}`.
  - **The probe body is a template, not a fixture.** A hard-coded future date
    is in the past a few weeks later and a hard-coded duration breaks the day
    somebody reseeds the demo tenant — both would start crying wolf about a
    product that is fine. The date and the duration are substituted each cycle
    from live data.

  **TWO CANDIDATE PROBES WERE KILLED BY MEASURING THEM.** An anonymous read of
  `businesses` and of `services` each answer **200 with `[]`**, because RLS
  refuses them — exactly as 4.4's matrix proved. Either would have been a
  green light for ever. **And the item asks for five paths where only four can
  fail independently:** `/book/demo-detail` is served by the same `index.html`
  as the homepage, so a fifth probe of it could not fail on its own. Said
  rather than faked. What the item calls "a safe database or function path" is
  covered separately by `booking_start` (database) and `booking_availability`
  (function).

  **THE CONTROLLED FAILURE, WHICH IS THE DONE-WHEN.** The homepage probe's
  content assertion was changed to a marker the page cannot contain —
  simulating Netlify serving a build without the app bundle, which is a
  failure that returns **200**, because `_redirects` makes every URL on that
  domain return 200. Then, from the check's own event log:

  - first failing cycle → the prober pinged **ok**, and healthchecks.io stayed
    **up**. **One failure says nothing.** This is the assertion that matters
    most and it is the one a monitor usually gets wrong.
  - second consecutive failing cycle → the prober pinged **`/fail`** with
    `{"failing":["homepage"]}`, healthchecks.io went **up → down**, and the
    email integration to Andrew fired.
  - an incident row was written naming the path and the reason: *"status 200,
    expected 200, body did not contain 'THIS-BUILD-MARKER-CANNOT-EXIST'"*.
  - the assertion was restored → next cycle pinged **ok** → **down → up**, and
    a recovery row was written. healthchecks.io recorded the whole thing as
    **1 downtime, 22 seconds, 99.99% uptime.**

  **THE TOLERANCE LIVES IN THE PROBER, NOT IN healthchecks.io** — healthchecks
  goes down on the first `/fail` it receives, which is correct, because the
  prober is the only thing that knows the difference between slow and broken.

  **TWO REAL EMAILS REACHED ANDREW DOING THIS, AND HERE THEY ARE SO HE DOES
  NOT HAVE TO ASK.** Both are from healthchecks.io, both about the check named
  **`detailing platform — live site paths`**, and both were caused on purpose
  by this work:

  | when (Pacific, 2026-09-23) | what it said | what it was |
  |---|---|---|
  | **21:55** | the check went **DOWN** | the deliberate break — the homepage assertion pointed at a marker the page cannot contain |
  | **21:56** | the check came back **UP** | the assertion restored, one cycle later |

  **Nothing was wrong with the site at any point.** healthchecks.io recorded
  the pair as one incident lasting **22 seconds**. Any later mail about this
  check is real.
