  ### AND A SESSION PUT AN API KEY IN A DATABASE COLUMN. IT IS OUT. 2026-09-23

  **Asked directly whether `site_probes.headers` held a key or merely could,
  the answer was the first one.** This session seeded three of the four probe
  rows with the project's publishable API key as a literal value — 208
  characters, plain text, in a table — and then wrote in the migration's own
  comment that the column *"holds an API key"*, which is how a mistake gets
  recorded as though it were a design.

  **IT DOES NOT MATTER THAT IT WAS THE PUBLISHABLE KEY**, the one already
  inside the site's own JavaScript bundle. The rule is absolute and a database
  column is an "anywhere": **a rule with a judgement call in it is not a
  rule**, and the next value somebody decides is "not really secret" will be
  the one that is.

  **WHAT WAS DONE, IN ORDER** —
  `supabase/migrations/20260923050000_probe_headers_hold_no_credential.sql`:

  1. **The value is gone.** Stripped from every row. It was never in git — the
     seeding ran from a scratch script that read the key at run time and the
     migration file never contained it — so the table was the only copy, and
     there is now none. `net.http_request_queue` holds **0 rows** and no
     header of that shape survives in `pg_net` either; checked, not assumed.
  2. **It cannot be put back.** A check constraint refuses any `headers` value
     carrying `apikey` or `Authorization`. **Broken on purpose three ways** —
     an update with `apikey`, an update with `Authorization`, and an insert of
     a fresh row carrying one — and the database refused all three with
     `23514`. **The first attempt at that sabotage was itself wrong and said
     the constraint did nothing**: it used `headers || '{...}'`, and
     `NULL || jsonb` is `NULL` in Postgres, so the update never carried a key
     at all. The check was innocent and the test was broken — which is this
     repo's own warning about breaking a check on purpose, arriving from the
     other direction.
  3. **The reference, not the value.** The row now carries `secret_name`, a
     NAME, pointing at Supabase Vault. The prober resolves it at the moment it
     makes the request into a local variable that is gone when the function
     returns — the same shape the edge functions use with `Deno.env.get`, and
     the same shape `docs/services-and-secrets.md` describes.

  **~~IT IS EMPTY~~ — IT HOLDS ONE SECRET NOW, AND HERE IS WHO PUT IT THERE.**
  `vault.secrets` held **zero** secrets when this was written. **No session
  will put one there.** Provisioning is **Andrew's**, and it was one statement
  he ran himself, with the value never passing through a session:

  ```sql
  select vault.create_secret('<the publishable anon key>', 'site_probe_api_key');
  ```

  **If the stored value ever has to CHANGE, that is a different statement and
  still his.** `vault.create_secret` refuses a name that already exists, so a
  replacement is the update form, by id:

  ```sql
  select vault.update_secret(
    (select id from vault.secrets where name = 'site_probe_api_key'),
    '<the new key>');
  ```

  **HE RAN IT. 2026-09-24, 06:52:29 UTC. THE MONITOR COVERS ALL FOUR PATHS
  NOW, AND THE PARAGRAPH BELOW IS KEPT AS THE STATE IT REPLACED.**

  `site_probe_api_key` exists — **one row in `vault.secrets`, confirmed by
  NAME**. Two full cycles were then forced and watched:

  ```
  {"ping":"ok","graded":4,"failing":[],"skipped":[]}      ×2
  ```

  **`skipped` is empty and `graded` is 4**, where it was 2 and
  `["booking_start","sign_in"]` before. Both new paths returned a **200 with
  real content** — `booking_start` a full set of opening hours out of
  `get_public_business_profile`, `sign_in` GoTrue naming itself
  (`{"version":"v2.197.0","name":"GoTrue",…}`). `consecutive_failures` is **0
  on all four** and neither new probe has ever recorded a failure.

  **`failing: []` WAS NOT TAKEN AS THE ANSWER, AND MUST NOT BE.** `fail_after`
  is 2, so a probe that failed once is absent from `failing` — the "one
  failure says nothing" rule that makes this monitor worth having also makes
  its headline unable to report a first failure. The verdict above comes from
  the **per-probe `consecutive_failures` counters and the response bodies**,
  not from the ping.

  **THE PUBLISHABLE KEY FORMAT WORKED, AND THAT WAS THE OPEN QUESTION.** He
  used a modern **`sb_publishable_`** key, not the legacy `eyJ…` anon JWT, and
  **the publishable one was what was tried first — it was not a fallback.**
  The concern was real: `probe_live_site()` sends the credential in **two
  positions at once**, as `apikey` *and* as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`,
  and the Bearer position is the one the legacy JWT was designed for, so a
  401 on either of these two probes would have been the key format rather than
  an outage. **It did not happen.** Both endpoints accept the publishable key
  in both positions. **No swap is needed and none was made** — and had one
  been, it would have been Andrew's to run, with `vault.update_secret`, since
  `vault.create_secret` refuses a name that already exists.

  **THE VALUE WAS NEVER READ.** Verification selected `name`, `created_at`
  and `updated_at` from `vault.secrets` and nothing else. `decrypted_secret`
  was not queried, not in full and not as a prefix or a predicate. The key
  format above is known from what Andrew said he pasted and from the probes
  answering 200 — **not from looking.**

  **AND THE CREDENTIAL IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN DECORATIVE**, which is the
  difference between "now covered" and a sentence. Measured directly: both
  paths answer **401 with no credential at all** —
  `POST /rest/v1/rpc/get_public_business_profile` → 401, `GET /auth/v1/health`
  → 401. So before 06:52 these two genuinely could not be probed, and the
  skip was honest rather than a missing feature.

  key; `homepage` and `booking_availability` need none. **A missing credential
  is reported as SKIPPED, never as DOWN**, because reporting it as an outage
  would make the monitor lie in order to make provisioning feel urgent — the
  exact wolf this design exists to avoid. And a skip is not silent: `skipped`
  rides on every ping, so it is visible in the check's own event detail.

  ### ARM TWO — "NO FUTURE AVAILABILITY", ASKED RATHER THAN INFERRED

  **The fifth condition was UNBUILT, not undistinguishable, and the whole
  reason this item stayed open for one more pass is that those two look the
  same in a roadmap.** Arm one catches a detailer with **no open days at all**
  — a structural fact read off `business_hours`. That is not what the item
  names. **A detailer can have seven open days and nothing anybody can book**,
  because slots are computed rather than stored: hours, buffer, slot interval,
  advance windows, vehicle rules, blockouts and existing bookings. Only asking
  produces the answer.

  So it asks. **One call to `available-slots` per detailer per hour**, across
  the next fortnight, alerting only when **no day in the whole window has a
  single slot.** **The window is the guard: nothing on a Tuesday is a Tuesday;
  nothing across fourteen days is a fault.**

  **FOUR WOLVES SHUT OFF, AND THESE ARE WHY IT WILL STILL BE HONEST IN A
  MONTH:**

  1. **The same four front conditions as arm one** — mid-setup, suspended,
     deliberately closed, never having worked. It never fires at somebody
     still building their page.
  2. **A detailer arm one already failed is not asked.** Otherwise one broken
     detailer produces two alarms saying different things about one fact.
  3. **FULLY BOOKED IS SUCCESS, NOT AN OUTAGE.** A detailer booked solid for a
     fortnight has no slots and nothing is wrong. **Any booking starting inside
     the window and the tenant is not alerted on** — one line, and it is the
     entire difference between *"your page is broken"* and *"you are busy"*.
  4. **BLOCKED OUT IS DELIBERATE.** `blockout_dates` is a real feature. Any
     blockout overlapping the window silences this arm for that tenant.
     **THE COST OF THAT CONSERVATISM IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN:** a detailer
     with one blocked afternoon somewhere in the fortnight **and** a genuine
     fault will not be alerted on. `blockout_dates` carries a `repeat` column,
     so proving blockouts cover *every* day is real arithmetic, and getting it
     subtly wrong points at mailing Andrew about somebody on leave. **Under a
     silence-unless-real ruling that is the right direction to be wrong in**,
     and arm one still covers that tenant for services and hours.

  **AND THE SERVICE TYPE IS READ, NOT ASSUMED.** Asking a drop-off-only
  detailer for mobile slots returns nothing — **the monitor would have
  invented a wolf out of a business working perfectly.** The probe asks for
  whatever that business actually offers.

  **No credential is sent, and that is measured rather than hoped for.**
  `available-slots` is public and deployed without JWT verification: called
  with no `apikey` header at all it answers 200 with real slots. `tenant_watch`
  holds no key.

  **PROVED ON A THROWAWAY DETAILER, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE BREAK WAS
  ITSELF WRONG.** `max_advance_days = 0` was **refused by the database** — the
  product will not allow that state, so **a break the product cannot suffer
  proves nothing.** Switched to `min_advance_minutes = 43200`: a thirty-day
  minimum notice, which has **no upper bound** and is a realistic fat-finger.
  Hours intact, nothing blocked, not busy, and no day in the fortnight
  bookable. Measured:

  - first bad grade → **silent**.
  - second consecutive bad grade → alert naming the reason and the window:
    *"nothing bookable in the next 14 days (2026-09-25 to 2026-10-08) — this
    detailer has taken bookings before"*.
  - restored → quiet one cycle later, recovery row written.
  - **Tenant deleted, orphan incident rows cleared**, 16 businesses active,
    nothing suspended.

  **THE PROOF SENT NO MAIL.** The ping was disconnected for its whole duration
  and reconnected afterwards — **six emails was the night's limit and it had
  been reached.** The ping-to-email path this feeds was already proved end to
  end at 22:33 with arm one; what needed proving here was the decision.

  ***6.4, THE SERVER HALF OF A CLIENT KEY FOR `send-invoice`, BUILT 2026-10-06 (DP Cowork2, Lane B). Code, one migration and tests only; NOTHING APPLIED, NOTHING PUBLISHED, no live
  database touched. The box stays `[ ]`: the app half is DP Cowork's, and the publish and the migration are Andrew's.***
  **What it fixes.** `send-invoice` writes no row, so unlike a booking it has no natural key that tells a retry from a deliberate "send it again": two presses sent two invoices and a
  thank-you email each. The only thing that can tell them apart is the client, so the function now accepts an `idempotency_key` and answers a repeat of the same key without sending.
  **Files:** `supabase/functions/_shared/sendInvoiceClaim.ts` (the state machine, import-free so node runs it), the claim wired into `supabase/functions/send-invoice/index.ts`, and
  `20261006062000_send_invoice_attempts.sql` (one small service-role-only table, no customer data, listed in `FOR-ANDREW.md` Part 1b).
  **THE CONTRACT, and exactly what `app/src` must send** (the call is `api.sendInvoice` at `app/src/lib/api.js:102`, used at `BookingDetail.jsx:668`):
  1. **Send `idempotency_key` in the body**, beside `business_id` and `booking_id`: a UUID, `crypto.randomUUID()`.
  2. **Make the key once per INTENT to send, and keep it in the component (a ref), not recompute it.** The first press of *Send invoice* on a job record makes it.
     **Every retry of that intent sends the SAME key**: a second tap while the first is unanswered, a thrown network error, a timeout, a 5xx, a 409, and the
     `email_failed` answer (the server marks a failed key as retryable).
  3. **Make a NEW key after the press succeeded** (any `success: true`, duplicate or not), so a deliberate *Send again* later is a new intent and goes through, and a new key
     whenever the record opens on a different booking. **Never derive the key from the booking id** (that would make a second send impossible), and never reuse one across bookings.
  4. **Answers to handle:** `200 { success: true, thank_you_sent }` is sent. **`200 { success: true, duplicate: true, thank_you_sent }` means an earlier press with this key already sent it: show
     the same "invoice sent" notice, not an error.** `200` with `idempotent: false` is sent but unprotected (the table is not applied yet): treat as success. **`409 { error: "in_progress" }`
     means another press of the same intent is still sending: do not show a failure; wait a moment and press again with the SAME key, which will then answer `duplicate`.**
     `400 { error: "idempotency_key must be a UUID" }` is a bug in the caller. `502 { error: "email_failed" }` is a real failure: keep the same key for the retry. Any other answer as today.
  5. **No key is the old behaviour, unchanged**: every press sends. A client that does not send one is not broken, just unprotected.
  **Server rules, the states:** per (booking, key) `sending`, then `sent` or `failed`. A claim is the primary key's insert; a `failed` key is taken by exactly one retry; a key left `sending` for more than
  two minutes is a crash and exactly one caller takes it over; both are compare-and-sets on the state, never a read then a write. A key written in capitals is the same key as its lower-case form.
  **A store that cannot be used (the migration not applied) does not stop the invoice:** the answer is `idempotent: false` and it sends as it always did.
  **Proved, in node and on PGlite, nothing live.** `node --test tests/send-invoice-key.test.mjs`, 6 pass: fifteen properties of the state machine on the real module, including two presses at once
  sending ONE email (the function's own claim sequence with a counter standing in for Resend, said in the test), a failed key retried by exactly one of two presses, a stale send taken by exactly one,
  a malformed key an error and never "no key", and **nine rebuilds of the module with one guard removed each, each turning its own probe red**; and `send-invoice` read as text: it claims after its own
  checks (so an unfinalized booking never claims a key) and before anything is built or sent, releases the key on both failure exits, settles on success and says `idempotent: false` when nothing was deduped.
  `node --test tests/send-invoice-key-sql.test.mjs`, 6 pass on PGlite (outside the repo through `PGLITE_DIR`, loud skip without it, as `tests/action-log-sql.test.mjs`): the primary key makes a claim atomic,
  the state check, the cascade from the booking, the lock against a browser role, the compare-and-set the function issues winning once, and each of the primary key, the check and the revoke removed and seen.
  **NOT PROVEN, said plainly:** that the deployed function does it (not published) or that supabase-js issues the statements the PGlite case runs (the call is read as text, and the table's own
  behaviour is proved separately); an email actually going out (no Resend call was made); and the TypeScript, which no compiler here has checked. **One residual:** if the write that marks a key `sent` is lost
  after the email went out, the row stays `sending`, and a retry two minutes later could send once more. The function logs it (`the invoice went out but its key could not be marked sent`, with the booking id); it is the only way
  left to see a second invoice with a key in use.
  **What DP Cowork should prove on the app half:** press *Send invoice* twice quickly on a fixture business's finalized job, with the function published and the table applied (Andrew's), and read `email_sends`
  for that booking: one invoice and one thank-you, not two; then press *Send again* after the first answered and read two. **Red proof:** take the key out of the call and the same two presses read two and two.
  **Incident, said because it is the kind of thing that is easy to omit:** while checking neighbours I ran `tests/email-sends.test.mjs`, which loads the root `.env` itself and so started its credentialed half.
  It signed in as the demo owner and read the demo business's bookings, **and refused §§ 2 to 4 before touching anything** (*"REAL MAIL IS OPT-IN"*), so no email was sent and no row was written. I did not run it again.

  **READ COLD BY DP COWORK2, 2026-10-07 — THE KEY HANDLING IS RIGHT; THE WAY IT GIVES UP IS NOT.**
  *A second session that did not build this read the app half, `api.js`, `core.js`, the function and the contract above as a stranger. **All four of this
  item's own claims hold**: one key per intent (`BookingDetail.jsx:355`, `||=` on a ref), the same key on every retry (read once into a local, which is the
  defect the build note records), a new key after any resolved send, and a new key on a different booking. **Two things are wrong anyway**, one of them
  user-visible and against clause 4 of the contract above. No `app/src` was touched.*

  **1 · A GIVEN-UP 409 PUTS THE WORD `in_progress` ON THE SCREEN, WHICH IS THE ONE THING CLAUSE 4 SAYS NOT TO DO.** The contract reads *"409 `in_progress`
  … do not show a failure"*. The implementation retries three times at 700ms and then **re-throws** (`BookingDetail.jsx:375`), `act`'s catch does
  `setError(e.message)` (`:149`), and `:499` renders `{error}` **raw** in an `error-box` with `role="alert"`. The message is the server's token, not a
  sentence: `send-invoice/index.ts:97` answers `{ error: "in_progress" }` and `app/src/book/core.js:62` makes `err.message` out of `data.error`. **So a
  detailer reads the literal string `in_progress` in a red box.** It also has no Spanish key, so it is that same token in both languages — **which is the one line of this item's write-up that the finding
contradicts outright**: *“No text changed on any screen, so there is no Spanish key to add — a 409 now resolves into the sent notice the press was
going to earn anyway.”* A 409 resolves **when it resolves**; the exhausted one puts a new string on the screen, and that string is `in_progress`.
  **IT IS REACHABLE, AND THE TWO NUMBERS ARE WHY.** The server's stale-send takeover is **two minutes** (`_shared/sendInvoiceClaim.ts`, the
  `updated_at < now() - interval '2 minutes'` compare-and-set proved in `tests/send-invoice-key-sql.test.mjs` § 5). The client gives up after **2.1
  seconds**. So any send that dies mid-flight leaves every press for the next two minutes answering 409 — four requests, then the token. **The failure
  mode is not the retry budget, which is reasonable; it is the sentence at the end of it.** A fix is one branch in the catch: on an exhausted 409, show
  words — *"That receipt is still sending. Give it a moment and try again."* — and add the Spanish key in the same edit, per CLAUDE.md.

  **2 · THE TWO FIELDS THE SERVER RETURNS FOR THE SCREEN CANNOT BE READ BY THE SCREEN AT ALL.** `sendReceipt` returns `answer`
  (`BookingDetail.jsx:363`), and `act` does `await fn()` and **discards the return value** (`:140`). So `idempotent: false` — the server's one way of
  saying *this send was NOT deduplicated* (`send-invoice/index.ts:286`, and the claim module's header: *"the screen can tell that nothing was deduped …
  reported, never silent"*) — is unreachable, as is `thank_you_sent`. **This is to contract** (clause 4 says treat `idempotent: false` as success) and it
  is not a bug today, so it is recorded as a limitation rather than a fault: **between publishing `send-invoice` and applying the table — an order
  `FOR-ANDREW.md` Part 1b explicitly permits in either direction — every send is unprotected, the server says so in every answer, and nothing in the
  product can tell.** The same discard means a `duplicate` answer whose `thank_you_sent` is false still prints *"Receipt + thank-you sent."*

  with `role="alert"` in the right language, and **`in_progress` nowhere**. Frames in `.manager-shots/6.4-fix/`.

  to show it *only if there is a plain, honest way to say it*. There is not, and the reason is what it would have to
  say: the field means **this send was not deduplicated, because the protection table is not applied yet**. That is a
  fact about the server's configuration, it arrives attached to a send that **succeeded**, and there is nothing a
  detailer can do with it — they cannot apply a migration. The only honest sentence is some form of *"it sent, but if
  you press again you may send two"*, which turns a successful send into a warning about something the reader cannot
  fix, on every send, for as long as the publish and the apply are out of step — an order `FOR-ANDREW.md` Part 1b
  explicitly permits. **Clause 4 already rules it success.** So the limitation stands exactly as the cold read wrote
  it, and **the reader who needs that fact is Andrew, where `FOR-ANDREW.md` already has it.**
  **One thing inside finding 2 IS a lie to a detailer rather than a silence, and it is left for its own item:** a

  claiming something that did not happen — a different kind of fault from an unreadable field — and fixing it means
  `act` returning its answer to four call sites. Not folded in here.

  choosing another job mounts a fresh `BookingDetail` and the ref is already gone. The premise holds on the **fifth** place this component is rendered —
  `JobPage.jsx:76`, bare, under the `/job/:id` route (`main.jsx:150`), where only the param changes. **So the effect is load-bearing, on the one screen
  its comment does not name**, and the comment should say that rather than the opposite. *(It is also the screen where ROADMAP 4.7's missing equivalent
  for `payPick` is a live mis-tap — written up under 4.7.)*
  **Corrected in `96d7eb6`:** the comment now names `JobPage.jsx` as the screen the line saves and says why
  the other four do not need it — *a guard whose comment points at the wrong screen is a guard somebody
  deletes while checking the screens it names.*

- [x] **6.4a — Today is readable offline only while the screen that loaded it
  stays open. Reload it, or leave and come back, and it is blank.**
  Found 2026-10-06 by DP Cowork while building 6.4(a); said in that commit
  rather than hidden. **6.4(a)'s done-when says "on a screen that had already
  loaded" and is met; this is the next thing a detailer in a driveway does.**
  A detailer who switches to Calendar and back, or whose phone reloads the tab
  after it slept, finds an empty Today with a raw network error.

  **Why:** the day's jobs live in the screen's own state (`useBookings`), so
  unmounting Today throws them away. And `app/public/sw.js` is deliberately
  *not* a caching worker (its own header: *"a worker that starts serving stale
  HTML is a far worse bug than the one it was added to fix"*), so a cold load
  with no signal gets no app at all.

  **Two halves, and the second is Andrew's call:**
  1. *Leave and return.* Keep the last good list for the session outside the
     screen, so coming back offline shows it with the same *as of* line.
  2. *Cold reload.* Either an app-shell cache (reverses a stated worker rule,
     and puts customer names and phones on the device) or a plain "no
     connection" page that says the print sheet is the fallback. **A decision,
     not a default; recommendation: leave-and-return now, and for cold reload
     the plain page, because the printed schedule already covers the outage.**

  **Done when:** with the network cut, **(1)** opening Calendar and returning
  to Today shows today's jobs and the *as of* line, and **(2)** a hard reload of
  `/app` shows either the jobs with the line, or the plain no-connection page
  if Andrew chooses that — never a blank screen or a raw *Failed to fetch*. If
  anything is kept on the device, **signing out clears it**, shown by signing
  out and reading it back. **Red proof:** drop the keeping step and (1) goes
  blank.
  *Lane:* A (`app/src`, plus `sw.js` if the cache is chosen).

  **BUILT AND TICKED 2026-10-06, commit `e6302d5` (DP Cowork, Lane A). Andrew's
  standing instruction was to do BOTH halves; the decision and its cost are in
  DECISIONS.md under the same title.**
  * **Leave and return, offline:** Today draws the saved list with *You're
    offline. Showing your jobs as of 4:11 PM.* in **0.1 seconds** (87 to 152ms
    across runs) instead of waiting out the retries for a spinner.
  * **Reload, offline:** the worker starts the app from its cached shell and
    `NoConnection.jsx` shows the saved list with the same line, phone and address
    on each row, and Print for the next day with jobs. **It is no longer the
    sign-in form or *Create your business*** (a failed membership read used to
    fall through to both). Reached in **4.4 seconds** on the weak-signal path
    (Playwright leaves `navigator.onLine` true on a reload, so the browser's own
    offline flag is not what was measured) and at once when the browser says it is
    offline.
  * **Nothing stored:** a plain *No connection* page with a Retry button, not
    blank. Retry with the signal back restores the dashboard and saves the list
    again.
  * **Sign-out clears it:** **0 keys left** after signing out; the stored entry is
    customer names, phones and addresses on the device, which is the cost named in
    DECISIONS.md.
  * **Measured offline on my own fixture business** (its own owner, five jobs,
    deleted afterward), 320 and 1440, `?lite=1`, with the address and forecast
    calls aborted in the browser so the shared hourly address budget was not
    touched: **14 of 14 checks at both widths**, no sideways scroll, console clean
    apart from the cut-wire network errors and a `platform-admin` 404 that is not
    this item's.
  * **Broken on purpose:** never saving the list (5 red), sign-out not clearing
    (red: 2 keys left), the worker without a fetch handler (the offline reload
    fails outright, *ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED*).
  * **Still true, and said:** a device that has never loaded the dashboard online
    has no shell and no list, so the browser's own offline page is all it can
    show; the worker needs one online visit after install.

## Wave 7 — Sales proof

**VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOFTWARE, 2026-09-20 — the pricing page and the five
examples, read the way the legal pages were: not for prose, but for places the
page says something the product does not do.**

**THE HONEST FRAME FIRST, because it changes what every finding below is
worth: none of these pages has ever been read by somebody deciding whether to
buy.** Zero paying subscriptions, one non-demo business. **So every defect
here is still free to fix** — nobody has been misled, nobody has paid on a
wrong number, and the whole of Wave 7 is a debt that has not yet come due.

**THE ONE SENTENCE THAT SAYS WHY THIS WAVE EXISTS:**

> A stranger reading that page today would be told they get unlimited photos
> and an export, and they would get roughly one photo and no export.

**7.6 IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY AND IT IS WORSE THAN ITS OWN LINE.** The item
already records "1 GB total, 10.2 MB promised to each", from the back office.
Reading it out of the database instead — `photo_total_bytes()` is 1 GB and
`photo_tenant_share()` is 100, so the cap is 1 GB ÷ 100 — gives the same
figure, which is the useful part: two independent routes agree. **What the
item does not say is that it is ENFORCED and how small it is in practice.**
`JobPhotos.jsx` refuses the file outright — *"Photo storage is full. Remove
some photos to add more."* — and the `job-photos` bucket accepts a **single
file of up to 10 MB**. **So one photo the product is willing to take uses 98%
of that detailer's entire allowance.** A feature sold as unlimited runs out on
the first job. **Services, bookings and staff logins genuinely are unlimited;
only "photos" is false.** On Andrew's list with both ways out and no
recommendation, because the answer depends on what storage costs him.

**7.7 IS WIDER THAN RECORDED: THE EXPORT IS SOLD IN TWO PLACES.** The item
names the terms and the pricing page. It is also the **home page's** answer to
*"What happens to my customers if I cancel?"* — *"You export them and go. The
list was always yours."* That is arguably the worst of the three, because it
is the direct answer to the question a nervous detailer actually asks. There
is no customer export and no photo export; the only download is the
accountant's CSV of jobs and expenses.

**7.10's `/ex5` ENTRY IS STALE.** It calls the site "Tampa Bay" and the
question about a real company's name is already answered: it is **"Sunglade
Auto Detail"** with an address on a reserved `.example` domain. "Tampa Bay"
survives only as a place — *"Mobile detailing across Tampa Bay"* — which is a
region, not a company. Andrew's list row was closed rather than left for him
to decide something already done.

**THE EXAMPLES DO NOT OVER-PROMISE, AND THIS WAS THE QUESTION WORTH ASKING.**
A real tenant site is built bespoke by an agent following
`docs/tenant-site-kit.md`, so a hand-built example IS the product rather than
a picture of it. Every headline feature on `/examples` maps to something
`get_public_business_profile` actually returns, checked key by key:

| What an example demonstrates | What backs it |
|---|---|
| ex4's before-and-after slider | `gallery_images.before_url` / `after_url`, published from the job screen by `publishToGallery` |
| ex5's "pick your vehicle and the prices change" | `services.vehicle_size_adjustments` and `vehicle_sizes` |
| ex3's "every price on the page" | `services` with `price`, `price_is_from`, `duration_minutes` |
| ex2's step-by-step walkthrough | `services`, `faqs`, `hours` |
| ex1's Work and Prices as real tabs | a build choice; the agent writes the pages |

**And the claim on the index page holds too.** It says *"Every price and time
on these is a placeholder. On a real detailer's site each one comes live from
their own dashboard."* The examples' booking sections are indeed drawings —
annotated `data-from="core.js stepsFor(addOns)"`, with no form, no iframe and
no request — and the kit makes the live half a rule rather than an aspiration:
*"A price, service, hour or plan hard-coded into the site — **No, and this is
the one hard no.**"*

**One framing point rather than a defect:** `/examples` describes ex3 as *"in
three colors you can switch between"*, which reads as a feature of that site.
It is a design choice Andrew was offered three ways; a real tenant has one
brand colour from their dashboard. An agent could build a switcher, so nothing
is promised that cannot be delivered — but the sentence describes an artefact
of the review rather than a tenant feature.

**7.12'S BLANK SECOND IS WORSE THAN "BLANK" AND IT NEARLY PRODUCED A FALSE
FINDING.** The item records that the pricing page is blank for about a second.
**It is not blank — for that moment it shows the LIST prices**, because the
founding lookup has not answered and the code deliberately does not render a
founding price optimistically. A read taken in that window showed *"$600 a
year"* in the terms against *"$40 a month"* in the ladder — a money
contradiction inside the AB 2863 disclosure block, quoted straight from the
page, and completely untrue. Re-probing the DOM after it settled gave
`$400` / `$40` / `$50` and a `$120` worked exit fee, consistent throughout.
**`docs/gotchas.md` carries it: a page read before its data resolves will hand
you a confident contradiction between two numbers that never disagreed.**

**AND THE PAGE DOES EXPLAIN ITSELF**, which was the third question and the one
that needed evidence rather than an opinion. In reading order: *"Two plans.
Three ways to pay."* → *"FOUNDING PRICE — 3 of 3 spots left. It is locked for
the life of the account and never rises while that account stays open. When
the last one goes, this page shows the standard prices instead."* → the build
fee, the monthly, the saving → *"BEFORE YOU PAY — The terms, in full. Not a
link to a policy page. This is all of it."* → eight plain clauses including a
worked example: *"On 12 months at $40 a month, walking away halfway through
costs $120."* **The one place it can be misread** is the summary strip, where
`TO BUILD IT $499 once · THEN $40 a month · SAVE ON THE YEAR $80 a year` puts
two prices and one saving in identical formatting. The label says "SAVE ON",
so it is defensible; named for whoever owns that screen rather than changed.

**NOTHING IN `app/src` WAS EDITED.** Every finding that needs a screen change
is written down for its owner, and the two that are promises about the product
rather than wording went to Andrew.

    **Root cause:** `.setupfee` carries `data-rv="lift"`
    (`landing.css:292,302`) — an intersection-observer-gated reveal sitting at
    `opacity: 0` until a real scroll trigger adds class `.in`.
    `elementHandle.screenshot()` scrolls the target into view but does not
    wait for that class, so the pre-reveal frame was captured. `.plans` and
    `.ladder` were not gated on their own container, which is why only this
    one region was silently empty.
    **Fixed by:** waiting explicitly for `getComputedStyle(el).opacity ===
    "1"` (a real signal with a real timeout, not a fixed sleep) before
    shooting, both on the normal path and `?lite=1`; and by asserting on the
    actual pixels rather than the file — the screenshot buffer is decoded
    back through the page's own canvas (the technique `scripts/pinned-bar.mjs`
    and `scripts/admin-contrast.mjs` already use, since there is no
    sharp/jimp/PIL here) and checked for luminance variance above 6 — this
    repo's dotted background alone runs 2–3, real content runs into the
    dozens. **Proved the assertion catches the real failure**: the exact
    original bug was reproduced on purpose — screenshotting `.setupfee` with
    the wait skipped — and variance measured 0.97, correctly flagged. The ten
    genuine captures in the same run measured 21–37.

  ── **SPEC FOR WHOEVER OWNS `scripts/`: THE PICTURE-STALENESS GATE CAN SAY
  "CURRENT" OVER A CAPTURE THAT NO LONGER MATCHES. Written to be built without
  asking this session.** ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

  **Whose:** `scripts/example-shots-check.mjs` and `scripts/capture-examples.mjs`
  (`fingerprint` and the manifest are exported from the second).
  **Not blocked by the publish freeze** — no deploy, no migration, nobody's
  permission.

  **WHAT THE GATE IS FOR.** `/examples` shows a thumbnail per example site.
  The gate's job is to fail when a picture was taken before a change to the
  site it shows, because **a stale thumbnail is a screenshot of a product that
  no longer exists**, shown to the one audience that judges this product by
  it.

  **THE HOLE, and it is one line.** `example-shots-check.mjs:122-123`
  computes `fingerprint(readFileSync(file))` where `file` is
  `docs/tenant-sites/<source>.html`, and compares it to
  `manifest.sites.<slug>.fingerprint`. **That is the site's own source and
  nothing else.** But `build-examples.mjs` injects a **paint switcher** —
  the `PAINTS` const — into `ex3` and only `ex3`, immediately before
  `</body>`, at build time. **That block is in the picture and not in the
  fingerprint.**

  **HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part that says how bad it is:** correcting
  "Colour" to "Color" inside that control changed what the ex3 thumbnail
  should show, and the gate went on reporting `current`. **It was caught only
  because ex3 happened to be re-shot for another reason.**

  **THE FIX.** Hash the injected block into the manifest alongside the
  site's: record a second value per site — call it `injected_fingerprint`,
  `null` for the four sites that get nothing — and fail when **either**
  differs. `PAINTS` must be importable for that, which is a one-word `export`.

  **THE STRONGER ALTERNATIVE, AND ITS COST, so the choice is deliberate:**
  fingerprint the **built** page under `app/public/<slug>/index.html` instead,
  which covers `PAINTS` and anything injected later without a second field.
  **It costs the gate its independence** — it would then require
  `build-examples.mjs --dev` to have been run, and today it reads
  `docs/tenant-sites/` and needs no build. **Pick one on purpose; do not end
  up with both halves of neither.**

  **WHAT A RIGHT ANSWER LOOKS LIKE.** With nothing edited: every site
  `current`, and the run prints **how many sites it fingerprinted and how many
  injected blocks it fingerprinted** — `5 sites, 1 injected block` today. **A
  count of zero injected blocks must be a failure, not a silent pass**, or the
  whole fix can rot back out the day somebody renames `PAINTS`.

  **WHAT A WRONG ANSWER LOOKS LIKE — four shapes, and the first is the one
  that exists today:**
  1. **Edit the injected block, gate still says `current`.** The live bug.
  2. **Edit the injected block, gate names the wrong site.** `PAINTS` reaches
     `ex3` only; a check that fails all five is no more use than one that
     fails none.
  3. **Gate fingerprints an injected block that no longer reaches any page.**
     Green forever, measuring nothing — the `0 injected blocks` case above.
  4. **Gate needs a build it does not say it needs.** It reports `current` on
     a machine where `app/public/ex3/` is empty, because the file it hashed
     was the source and the file in the picture was never generated.

  **CANARIES, since this repo has shipped at least six checks that tested
  nothing.** `--break=drift` already exists and pretends the SOURCE moved;
  add `--break=inject`, which pretends the INJECTED block moved. **Each must
  fail `ex3` and only `ex3`, and `--break=inject` must fail on a gate that
  has the fix and pass on one that does not** — that is the single assertion
  proving the hole is closed rather than described.

  **Done when** (written 2026-09-25; this item had none, and it has three remaining
  parts rather than one — each already specified above, so none of this is new
  scope):
  1. **`/ex3`'s hero is MEASURED, not rebuilt.** Open it at 1440x900, let the

  2. **The picture-staleness gate fingerprints the INJECTED block as well as the

     zero injected blocks failing rather than passing silently.**
  3. **Andrew has ruled on the `/ex2` wordmark** — deliberate device or overlap
     defect. `docs/TASTE-NOTES.md` § 1 describes his own reference doing exactly
     this on purpose, so **no session decides it either way.**
  **What failing looks like:** the hero rebuilt from the wrong one of two
  disagreeing records; a gate reporting `current` over a thumbnail that no longer
  matches, which is the live bug today; or the wordmark quietly edited out.

- [x] **7.13 — ~~British spellings on the example sites, and nothing that
  could catch them.~~ FIXED 2026-09-20, and the check is built.**
  **Thirty-six British words were reaching a visitor across the five example
  sites — seventeen different ones.** Hood written as *bonnet* (nine times),
  fender as *wing* (four), microfiber as *microfibre* (four), sedan as
  *saloon* (three), *fortnightly* (three), *colour* and *Colourway* (three),
  and one each of *neighbour*, *neighbours*, *kerb*, *grey*, *aluminium*,
  *cancelled*, *windscreen*, *boot lid* and *at weekends*. `CLAUDE.md` names "hood" by
  name. All fixed; a rendered sweep of all eight example pages now returns
  **zero**.

  **THREE OF THEM WERE WHERE PROSE IS EASIEST TO FORGET IT LIVES:**
  - **Alt text**, which is not decoration — a screen reader says it aloud, so
    a blind visitor was being told about a *bonnet*.
  - **A control injected by the build**, not by the site file: the `/ex3`
    colour switcher, which sits in the corner of every capture and reads
    "Colour".
  - **Inside a JavaScript array**, where `"Aluminium tanks and wheels
    polished"` and `"Windscreen polished"` are service bullets that only
    render when a visitor opens the right tab. **A source scan that strips
    `<script>` strips the copy**, and a rendered scan that reads one tab
    reads one eighth of it. Both instruments were needed; each one alone
    printed clean over words the other found.

  **THE GAP: NOTHING WE RUN WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ANY OF IT.** These were found by
  reading the sites, not by a check. Every gate here measures structure,
  contrast, routes or counts. **A spelling that is wrong for the audience and
  right for a dictionary passes all of them**, and it will come back the next
  time somebody writes a page.

  **AND THE CHECK NOW EXISTS — `scripts/american-english.mjs`, approved and
  built 2026-09-20.** It reads the FINISHED page rather than the source,
  because the source was the instrument that printed clean over "Aluminium
  tanks": it walks every text node in the rendered DOM — on `/ex5` that is
  32,779 characters against the 7,551 `innerText` returns, because seven of
  the eight vehicle panels are built and hidden — plus the strings a screen
  reader says out loud.

  **THE TWO DOCUMENTED EXCEPTIONS ARE ALLOWED BY POSITION, NOT BY SPELLING,
  and that distinction is the whole check.** An exception written as "allow
  the word cancelled" would have waved through the exact sentence this was
  built to catch — `/ex5`'s *"A slot cancelled late cannot be refilled"*. So
  `cancelled` passes only as the bare status token or inside a key-ish
  attribute, and `colour` only inside a key-ish attribute.

  **IT WAS BROKEN ON PURPOSE TWICE BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED**, and each sabotage
  aims at a different half:
  - `--break=mute` removes three words from the list. The canary stops firing
    and `receipt.mjs` refuses the receipt.
  - `--break=lax` turns the two exceptions back into spelling rules. It then
    misses "colour" in prose and "cancelled" in a sentence — which is the
    proof that the positional rule is load-bearing rather than decorative.

  The canary is **a real page, really loaded, with British prose injected into
  its live DOM** and read by the real scanner — not a flag that pretends. It
  runs both directions: seven planted words must be caught, and the bare
  "Cancelled" chip and `data-step="colour"` must NOT be.

  **IT FOUND A 37th INSTANCE ON ITS FIRST RUN, and not on an example site.**
  The platform's own pricing page said *"Cancelling stops the next charge"* —
  prose, not a database value. Fixed, along with four more the same word had
  on screens behind sign-in that the check cannot reach, each with its Spanish
  key moved in the same edit. **Three remain in developer comments and were
  left**; they are not what a customer reads.

  **WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO, said out loud:** bare "wing" is not in the word
  list, because a wing is a real part of an American car — and bare "wing" was
  four of the original 36. It scans the 11 pages reachable without signing in;
  everything behind a login needs a seeded session and is not covered. A word
  list is maintenance, which is exactly the "grep-based check coupled to a
  spelling rather than a behavior" `docs/gotchas.md` warns about. **The
  argument for it is that here, spelling IS the behavior.**

  *Found 2026-09-20 while fixing 7.10. Not from either audit — neither
  mentions it.*

  Same fault as 7.12, same page, same window, **different source**: `offer`
  was the only answer anything waited on, so `P` started as the file's
  `PRICING` table and was replaced when `platform_prices` answered.
  *Found while fixing 7.12 and named there rather than folded into it.*

  **LATENT, NOT LIVE — said plainly so nobody reads this as a bug a visitor
  hit.** `platform_prices` returns **null** today (read from the browser, no
  write of any kind), so the file table IS the truth and nothing visibly
  swapped. It becomes real the first time a price is overridden. **And no
  settings write was needed to prove the fix**, because what is being fixed is
  the ORDER of two answers, which is observable whether or not the values
  differ. Nothing was written to any tenant.

  **THE FIX IS THE ORDER OF TWO LINES, AND THE SECOND DESIGN WAS MUCH SMALLER
  THAN THE FIRST.** Both lookups now run in one effect behind `Promise.all`,
  and `setOffer` is called **after** `setP`. So `offer !== null` means *both
  answers are in*, and `priced`, `fig`, `clause` and `founding` all tightened
  without one of them changing.
  **The first attempt added a `pricesIn` flag and was thrown away.** It needed
  the same widening in four places, and `tests/landing-pricing.test.mjs` pins
  three of those lines by their exact source text — `const priced = offer !==
  null;` (9a), the `fig` definition (9a-ii), and `founding && <s
  className="was">` (6b-iv). The flag version failed the suite; the ordering
  version passes it untouched. **`tests/` was not this session's lane, and the
  better design meant it never needed to be.**
  Still parallel — both promises are created before either is awaited, so no
  extra round trip. Both fail to an ANSWER rather than to silence: the offer to
  no spots, the table to `livePricing(null)`, because a page that cannot reach
  the server must still print a price, and a rejection that left the promise
  unsettled would withhold every figure for ever.

  **THREE THINGS 7.12 LEFT, ALL FOUND BY PROBES THAT DID MORE THAN THE LAST
  ONE DID:**
  - **The four struck list prices** (`<s className="was">`). They hang on
    `founding`, which needed only the offer, so between the two answers they
    printed file figures. **Invisible to the 7.12 probe because it never
    scrolled**; found by one that did. Closed for free by the ordering fix.
  - **`monthsFree`** — *the one with no dollar sign*, and that is exactly why
    it survived: the 7.12 probe matched `/\$[\d,]+/` and cannot see a bare
    "2". It computes to 2 on both ladders today, so nothing was ever visibly
    wrong; `monthsFree`'s own comment records that an owner-typed price need
    not land on a whole number, which is when it would differ.
  - **`P.term.months`** in the commitment clause — a term LENGTH, not a price,
    and `livePricing` accepts an owner-supplied value from 0 to 60. A clause
    stating the length of a commitment is as quotable as one stating its cost.

  **VERIFIED BY HOLDING EACH LOOKUP OPEN SEPARATELY, 320 FIRST, CONSOLE AT
  EVERY WIDTH:**

  | Width | Settled | `platform_prices` held | `founding_offer` held | Console |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | **320** | 12 figures | 0 money · 0 struck | 0 money · 0 struck | clean |
  | 390 | 12 figures | 0 money · 0 struck | — | clean |
  | 768 | 12 figures | 0 money · 0 struck | — | clean |
  | 1440 | 12 figures | 0 money · 0 struck | — | clean |

  **THE PROBE PRODUCED A FALSE PASS AND THE CONSOLE IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS

  `pricesIn is not defined` throwing inside `<PricingPage>`; the ErrorBoundary

  what is committed", which found 22 of 39 edge functions stale. That one has
  an instrument now (`deployed-inventory.mjs`, which fetches each deployed
  bundle and compares it by content, exits 1, and names every function). **The
  database has no equivalent, one floor down, and it is the floor the edge

  **WHAT THE CHECK HAS TO DO, from what this failure actually looked like:**
  * **Name the drift, not count it.** `deployed-inventory.mjs`'s own lesson:

    question they have — *is the one I just edited in it?*

    says so plainly: there is no migration tracking here, applying is
    "CREATE statements … re-running will fail loudly", and nothing records
    what ran. So the check has to compare **observable database state**
    against the repo, not a ledger the repo does not keep.
  * **Functions are the tractable half and the half that bit us.** For every
    `create or replace function` in `supabase/migrations/`, the current
    definition is readable from `pg_get_functiondef` and comparable against
    the last migration that defines it. A mismatch is the exact fault above.
  * **It must exit non-zero and write a receipt**, like every other graded
    check here, so a silence can be told from a pass — `docs/silences.md`.
  * **Break it on purpose before trusting it.** This repo has shipped at
    least six checks that tested nothing, and this one would have a
    ready-made canary: the two migrations above, whose "before" state is
    recorded in 8.10a.

  differs from the repo's latest migration for it, exits 1 when any differ,
  writes a receipt, and has been proved by breaking it.

- [x] **8.1b — DONE 2026-09-19. The demo cannot hold a finished job in the
  small hours, and the gate went red over it.**

  **Checked by running it at both hours, not by reasoning about one.**
  Against a database seeded as if it were 01:00, `node scripts/sweep-widths.mjs
  320 1440 392` exits **0** — `expected-count 320px: 92/95 surfaces, 3 declared
  unreachable (job record · finished, job record · finalize, job record · send
  a text), every one accounted for`, the same at 1440 and 392 — and
  `receipt.mjs` grades it **PASS, 275/275 targets, 9 skips** (three labels at
  three widths) recorded with their reasons under the allowlist that file
  already validates. Re-seeded normally, the same command exits **0** with
  **284/284, skipped_targets 0 and no allowlist at all**: the machinery is
  dormant whenever everything is reachable.

  **HOW 1am WAS SIMULATED, because "I reasoned about it" is not an answer.**
  The system clock was not touched. `Date.now()` was pinned to 01:00 business
  time **for the seed process only**, and the seed re-run. That is the right
  thing to move and not a convenience: `Today.jsx` decides a job is finished
  from its STORED status (`status === "completed"` with no `finalized_at`),
  never from the clock, and `seed-demo.mjs` decides that status with
  `hasEnded`, which is `Date.now()` against the job's end time — **so the
  reachability of these three surfaces is settled entirely by `Date.now()` at
  SEED time.** Move it and the database is the one a 1am seed writes.
  Confirmed in the database before the sweep ran: five bookings dated today,
  **all five `confirmed`**, `needsPay` = 0, and one completed-and-unpaid dated
  the 18th. **The honest limit:** the browser's own clock stayed on the real
  afternoon, so this reproduces the 1am DATA and not a 1am screen. The data is
  what the skip turns on.

  **THE MECHANISM IS THE SUBSCRIPTION ONE, NOT A SECOND ONE.** The two
  `subscription · …` surfaces print `NOT MEASURED — <reason>`, raise no
  finding, and are absent from the expectation. Same printed line, same silence
  in `found`. One thing is added: the skip is **recorded** as well as printed,
  so the gate can tell a surface that said why from one that just went missing.
  It had to be: those two labels are absent from the expectation only because
  the run that wrote it never measured them — an accident that reads like a
  decision — and **deleting these three lines from the file would also have
  made the run pass, which is the wrong fix.** After about 08:45 they are
  reachable and must be measured. The labels stay.

  **A SKIP IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CLAIM.** Every skip carries a probe that
  re-asks whether the surface was reachable after all, and a skip over a
  reachable surface is refused and fails the run. **Proved by sabotage:** the
  `finished` locator was pointed at a class that does not exist, so the skip
  fired while the rail row was still sitting there —

      job record · finished    SKIP REFUSED — declared unreachable, and the
                               probe found 1. A skip over a surface that was
                               there is a screen removing itself from the check.

  — and **because the skip was refused it was never recorded**, so the gate
  went on to fail it anyway: `EXPECTED-COUNT GATE FAILED at 392px: expected 95
  surfaces, measured 94 / NEVER MEASURED job record · finished`. `receipt.mjs`
  failed the same run independently on the counts. Two doors, both shut. The
  sabotage was reverted and the selector re-checked.

  **Also gated:** a label that is declared unreachable AND measured in the same
  run prints `SKIP CONTRADICTED` and fails — one of the two is wrong about the
  screen and it cannot be decided from inside the run.

  **One flake worth recording, not from this change:** the first afternoon run
  died at 320 clicking the Victor Salas row, blocked by a closing sheet's
  backdrop. It did not reproduce (95/95 at 392, then 284/284 twice). ~~The
  escape-then-`settle(700)` in the Clients block is racing the 180ms exit under

  above was wrong.** `docs/gotchas.md` says to keep the reproduction when the
  explanation dies, so both stay here.

  **Instrument-only fix, no ROADMAP item of its own** (this paragraph is the
  only place it was written down, and one was not invented for it):

    the job record are **one sheet whose contents swap**, and the first Escape
    is a BACK STEP inside it, not a close — 1 sheet before, 1 sheet three
    seconds later, 0 only after a second Escape. Two Escapes fired too close
    together lose the second one mid-transition, the sheet stays open for ever
    and the click can never land. 700ms was not too short; nothing checked
    whether the press that mattered had worked.
  - **`closeOverlay()` now dismisses until nothing is covering the page**,
    bounded at five presses, loud if it cannot get there.
  - **Each width is its own unit of work.** A throw used to end the process
    past the gate, the contact sheet and the receipt — eight minutes producing
    no verdict at all. It now aborts that width by name, the others finish, and
    everything downstream still runs.

  ### THE COUNTING PASS, WIDENED TO BOTH LANGUAGES — 2026-09-23

  **Folded in from `docs/8.3-findings-2026-09-23.md`, now deleted.** No color was
  changed and none needed to be: the fix above had already happened.

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | screen/width/language combinations | **56** |
  | text elements measured where they are painted | **3,755** |
  | canary caught | **56 of 56** |
  | **distinct styles failing WCAG** | **0** |
  | console | clean at every one |

  **SO THERE IS NO SHARED-TOKEN QUESTION TO BRING ANDREW.** A token every
  failing surface shares does not exist here, because there are no failing
  surfaces. `--fog-2` is not broken: it is the documented floor for 10–13px
  labels and it holds at **4.90:1 on `--ink-1`** and **4.59:1 on `--ink-2`**. It
  measures **4.20:1 on `--ink-3`**, the highest surface, and the one place a
  label landed there was moved on 2026-09-20. Changing the token would be a
  rebuild of screens that work, **which is Andrew's standing instruction not to
  do** — the reason, not just the conclusion.

  **THE INSTRUMENT HAD ONLY EVER ASKED ENGLISH** — 32 combinations, every one of
  them English, for an item whose audits both said "everywhere". Widening it to
  both languages produced three findings, all of them about the check:

  1. **A LANGUAGE PASS MUST PROVE IT RENDERED THE LANGUAGE, OR IT MEASURES
     ENGLISH TWICE.** `localeStore.js` stamps the rendered locale on
     `<html lang>`, so every target now records what it actually rendered and a
     pass that fell back is a FAILURE. Without that the run said *64
     combinations, both languages, all clean* — and **eight of those sixty-four
     were English measured twice.** Same fault `calendar-legible.mjs` shipped and
     caught the same night: **no coverage at all, wearing the look of double.**
  2. **THERE ARE TWO LOCALE KEYS, NOT ONE.** The dashboard reads `dp.lang.app`;
     the public pages read `dp.lang`. Setting one switches five screens and
     leaves three in English. Both are set now, **as plain strings** —
     `localeStore.js` stores the bare locale, so writing JSON leaves it
     unrecognised and the page silently falls back.
  3. **THE LANDING AND PRICING PAGES CARRY NO i18n AT ALL.**
     `LandingPage.jsx` and `PricingPage.jsx` have no `t()` and no i18n import;
     `?lang=es` does not move them, and `es.js` is the booking side's catalogue.
     So the Spanish pass **skips them by declaration** rather than measuring
     English and calling it Spanish coverage. **That is why the declared target
     count is asymmetric:** `4 widths × ((5 tabs + 1 bilingual public page) × 2
     languages + 2 English-only pages)` = **56**.

  **And the tab bar is walked by POSITION now, labelled by the English name.**
  The first version filtered tabs by their English words, so the Spanish pass
  matched nothing — the bar reads «Hoy», «Calendario», «Dinero» — and twenty
  combinations printed `NEVER REACHED`.

  **Broken on purpose:** `--break` puts the original 4.20:1 defect back from the
  browser side and **inverts the verdict**, so a sabotage run that finds nothing
  is the failure. It found it: *1 distinct failing style, «11:42 PM»*. Restored,
  the run is `PASS — 56/56, canary failed as required`.

  **ONE THING THAT IS NOT A PRODUCT FAULT AND SHOULD NOT BE READ AS ONE.** An
  earlier run recorded **two `429`s** in the console while walking the booking
  page, which made the receipt FAIL. They did not recur. Per
  `docs/shared-resources.md` § 1 that is the signature of **another session's
  spend landing in your run**, not of a broken page — and the fix is emphatically
  not to clear `rate_hits` (`docs/gotchas.md` #78). Recorded rather than
  explained away.

  | 1440 | fits, 10 spare | over 254 | over 98 |
  | 768 | fits, 166 spare | over 98 | **fits, 58 spare** |
  | 392 | fits, 46 spare | over 218 | over 62 |

  **Two widths recovered; two did not, and the residual is exactly 108px at
  both** — six cards × 18px, which is what a worded row costs after the paint
  is as small as it can be while its target clears 44. **That is the floor of
  this trade, not a tuning failure.** Closing the last 108px means taking the
  words off a row of their own, which is the change that was asked for.
  Add-ons is **9px worse at every width** (the 15→17px price, three cards);
  left alone, on a step that overflows by 476 for a reason Andrew chose.
  **The whole flow went from 25 steps not fitting to 17.**

  **AND THE WORST NUMBER IN THE FLOW IS A DECISION, NOT A DEFECT — SAY IT OUT
  LOUD RATHER THAN QUIETLY PICKING ONE.** Add-ons overflows by **476px at 392,
  56% of the screen**, and the sweep names the culprit: `.bk-planpitch`, 472px.
  That is the monthly-plan pitch, and `BookingPage.jsx` and `PlanRows.jsx` quote
  Andrew's instruction three times — *"pretty big and pretty visible… like, just
  in the whole screen, like, not a button to go to the screen, but just the
  whole screen."* **Nothing was shrunk.** The pitch alone is more than half a
  phone screen because he asked for it to be.
  **W16 ("every step fits its screen") and that ruling were in direct conflict
  on this one step, and neither could be honoured without breaking the other.**

  **ANDREW'S DECISION, 2026-09-19: EXEMPT THE STEP, NOT THE CONTROL.** His
  reasoning, in his words: *"the plan-pitch size is a specific, deliberate,
  repeatedly-quoted design ruling from Andrew for that exact control; W16 is a
  general audit rule that predates this control. The specific instruction wins
  over the general one."*

  **So W16 IS SATISFIED, WITH ONE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION: the add-ons step.**
  `.bk-planpitch` is untouched and stays full-screen. `sweep-booking-steps.mjs`
  reports the exemption and the reason every run rather than a failure:

      2/7 Add-ons   EXEMPT from W16 — over 476px, and .bk-planpitch is 823px of it
        Andrew's ruling, 2026-09-19: the plan pitch is full-screen by
        instruction, so this STEP is exempt and the CONTROL is untouched.
        Everything else on the step still has to fit, and does — without the
        pitch it is 347px inside the screen. ROADMAP 8.4.

  **THE EXEMPTION IS NARROW THREE WAYS, so nobody has to re-litigate this and
  nothing can hide behind it:**
  1. **It needs `.bk-planpitch` on the page.** That control is on one step and
     the measurement returns 0 for it everywhere else, so no other step can
     reach the exemption.
  2. **It is arithmetic, not a name.** The step is re-judged with the pitch's
     height discounted and everything else on it is still held to W16 to the
     pixel. Measured: without the pitch the step fits by **465px at 1920, 342
     at 1440, 498 at 768 and 347 at 392**, so no tolerance is used and none is
     needed.
  3. **It stops firing the moment anything else grows.** Proved by sabotage:
     a `min-height: 1200px` on `.bk-choices` — a different control on the same
     step — and the exemption vanished, the step reporting a plain
     `over 1089px (121% of the screen)`. Reverted.
  **And steps 1 and 3 still fail in the same run**, which is the live proof it
  has not leaked sideways.

  **`sweep-widths.mjs` needed nothing.** Checked rather than assumed: it has no
  vertical-fit check at all (zero references to W16, fit, or viewport
  overflow), no `.bk-planpitch` reference, and the customer flow's add-ons step
  is not one of its surfaces. Adding an exemption there would be a rule naming
  something nothing carries.
  **The flow now reports 14 steps not fitting, plus 3 exempt readings** — down
  from 25 before this session.

  **SPLIT ACCEPTED 2026-09-20, five parts, in this order. EACH CARRIES ITS

  **What was measured before the split was proposed**, predictions declared

  **8.5e — REDUCED MOTION: THE DELAY THE `.lite` BLOCK FORGOT. DONE
  2026-09-20.**
  *Done when:* a visitor under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sees a step's
  content as soon as it exists, proved on a clock that is actually advancing.
  *The defect:* `.lite` forced `animation-duration: .01ms` and never touched
  `animation-delay`. The entrance staggers children at 60, 120, 180, 240 and
  300ms and `bk-rise` is `backwards`-filled, so during the delay the element
  sits at its `from` keyframe — **opacity 0**. Somebody who asked for less
  movement got no movement AND a blank screen, the one outcome that block
  exists to prevent.
  *Fixed:* `animation-delay: 0ms !important; transition-delay: 0ms !important;`
  beside the duration it already overrode.
  *PROVED ON A RUNNING CLOCK, NOT FROM THE STYLESHEET.* The browser pane this
  project usually drives **freezes the animation clock, which is what hid this
  defect in the first place**, so it was measured in headless Chromium under
  `reducedMotion: "reduce"` after confirming the clock advanced — document
  timeline +400ms over a 400ms wait, `requestAnimationFrame` firing. Watching
  a step's second child frame by frame from the moment it appears: **opacity
  reached 1 at +82ms before the fix (6 blank frames) and +31ms after it (3
  frames — React and paint, no animation left in it).** Removing the line
  reproduced 82ms; restoring it reproduced 31ms. **Measured on the 60ms
  child** because booking step 1 has three children; the same rule removes
  **300ms** on any step with six or more. Normal motion is untouched — the
  second child still computes `0.06s` there.

  **8.5a — KEYBOARD: REACH, OPERATION, AND GETTING BACK OUT. ✓ DONE
  2026-09-20.**
  *Measured and clean:* 187 controls, all reachable, all named, no positive
  `tabindex`.
  *Done when:* focus is visibly located at every step of a Tab walk across the
  five dashboard tabs and all seven booking steps; every sheet and modal can
  be left with Escape; no walk re-enters a component it has left; and the
  order follows the reading order.

  **THE FIRST NUMBER WAS 55 AND IT WAS WRONG. CORRECTED 2026-09-20, SAME
  NIGHT, BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT ON IT.**

  `elementHandle.screenshot()` captures an element's BORDER BOX, and an
  outline is painted OUTSIDE it. So every control with a perfectly good ring
  photographed identically focused and blurred, and the walk reported **55
  defective stops on a product that was drawing a ring on 53 of them.** Found
  by asking the browser what a keyboard-focused row actually computed —
  `outline: solid 3px` — instead of believing the picture. The frame is a
  page-level clip padded past the ring now.
  **THE APPROVED FIX WAS THEREFORE WRONG AND WAS NOT BUILT.** "One shared
  focus-visible rule for four classes that never got one" rested on the 55;
  those classes already have one. Building it would have added a second ring
  to controls that already draw the product's own.

  **WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, after the correction: 167 stops, both canaries
  caught 6/6, ONE real defect and ONE finding that is my probe's fault.**

  **THE REAL ONE, FIXED:** `.nav-row` inside `.card.setting-card` — the twelve
  settings rows on Business. The card is `overflow: hidden` for its rounded
  corners and the row sits **1px inside that edge**, so a 2px outline at +2px
  offset lands entirely in the clipped region. **The ring computes, paints and
  cannot be seen**, which for a keyboard user is the same as not having one —
  and it is exactly the "rendered but not visible" case this part was told to
  watch for. Fixed by moving the SAME ring inside the edge
  (`outline-offset: -2px`); no new focus style was invented.

  **THE ONE I COULD NOT STAND BEHIND WAS A REAL DEFECT AFTER ALL, AND NEITHER
  OF US HAD GUESSED ITS SHAPE.** `button.bk-peek` — the last "What's included"
  on booking step 1 — sits at **y=873 while the pinned bar starts at y=827**.
  Fully inside the viewport, entirely **underneath the bar**. Nothing scrolls,
  because by every ordinary test it is visible: `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`
  leaves it exactly where it is. `document.elementFromPoint` on its own centre
  returns the bar. **Not scrolled out of view — covered.**
  **AND THE OCCLUSION CHECK FOUND A SECOND ONE THE MOMENT IT EXISTED:**
  `button.bk-pick` — the last service card — focused under `div.total`, the
  bar's own price block.

  **FIXED WITH THE BROWSER'S OWN ANSWER:**
  `html:has(.bk > .bk-bar) { scroll-padding-bottom: calc(var(--bk-bar-clear) + 12px) }`.
  `scroll-padding-bottom` tells scrolling that the bottom of the page is
  spoken for, and the amount is **the variable ROADMAP 2.15 already keeps in
  step with the bar's real height** — not a second number that can drift.

  **TICKED 2026-09-20, ON TWO CLEAN RUNS IN A ROW**, which was the bar set for
  an instrument with this record: one clean run is just the sixth chance to be
  wrong. Both runs: 167 stops, 0 undetermined, **both canaries caught 6/6**,
  receipt `PASS — 6/6 targets, 167 assertions`.

  **HOW IT WAS CHECKED:** a real Tab walk over the five dashboard tabs and
  booking step 1, recording at every stop which element holds focus, whether
  anything on screen changes when it does (**by pixels**, in a frame padded
  past the ring, with a stability baseline and motion off), whether the
  element is in the viewport (**read the instant focus lands, before anything
  scrolls**) and whether anything is painted over it
  (**`elementFromPoint` on its own centre**).

  **THE TWO LIMITS, AND THEY TRAVEL WITH THE TICK:**
  1. **A focus ring that exists only BY ANIMATION is invisible to this walk**,
     because the walk turns animation off in order to see anything at all. Any
     clean sheet it produces is clean about rings that exist STATICALLY.
  2. **The walk sees what it can scroll to.** Controls behind a closed
     disclosure, inside a sheet nobody opened, or on a screen this walk does
     not visit are not covered by the tick — six screens were walked, not
     every screen in the product.

  **THIS PROBE WAS WRONG FIVE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT**, and every one of
  them would have shipped as a clean sheet or a false alarm: it stopped at
  `document.body`; it stopped on a repeated description; it could not tell a
  ring from a drifting gradient; it photographed a frame too small to contain
  an outline, reporting **55 defective stops on a product that was drawing a
  ring on 53 of them**; and it could not tell "covered" from "no ring". The
  two-run bar exists because of that record.

  **The two decisions, both made before the first run:**
  1. **Pixels, not computed style.** An `outline` that paints nothing still
     reads as present in `getComputedStyle`, so each stop is photographed
     focused, blurred, and compared byte for byte.
  2. **In view is part of visible.** A ring nobody can see is not visible
     focus, so the viewport test is taken from the element's rect **the
     instant it receives focus, before any screenshot** — Playwright's own
     `elementHandle.screenshot()` scrolls an element into view, which would
     have silently repaired the fault it was looking for. **Result: zero
     stops focused out of view.** That half is clean.

  **What has no visible focus, by class rather than by instance:**

  | | where |
  |---|---|
  | `button.row-item` | every job row on Today and every client row on Clients |
  | `button.nav-row` | **every settings row on Business** — twelve of them |
  | `button.bk-pick` | every service card on the booking page |
  | `button.bk-peek` | every "What's included" disclosure beside them |
  | `summary`, and two `div`s with `tabindex` | Today and Money |

  **THE PROBE REPORTED VOID FOUR TIMES BEFORE IT REPORTED A RESULT, and its
  own canaries are what said so.** Each of these would otherwise have shipped

  lands there — 0 stops on a screen with 25 controls); it stopped on a
  repeated DESCRIPTION, so two identical-looking buttons ended the walk; and
  **it could not tell a focus ring from a moving background** — this product's
  background animates for ever, so "focused differs from blurred" was true
  whether or not a ring existed, which is a false PASS. Fixed with a stability
  baseline (two identical shots first) and by running the walk under
  `reducedMotion: "reduce"` so the page holds still — which is only possible
  because 8.5e fixed the delay an hour earlier. Without it, 91 of 167 stops
  were undetermined.

  **THE LIMIT THAT BUYS, STATED, AND IT TRAVELS WITH THE FIX:** a focus ring
  that appears only BY ANIMATION is invisible to this walk, because the walk
  turns animation off in order to see anything at all. **So any clean sheet it
  ever produces is clean about rings that exist STATICALLY.** Nothing in this

  **8.5c — ZOOM TO 200%. ✓ DONE 2026-09-20.**
  *Done when:* at 200% zoom, at all four widths, nothing is clipped, no

  elements examined, 0 findings in the supported range**, receipt PASS.

  **HOW ZOOM IS EMULATED:** a 1440px window at 200% lays out as a 720 CSS px
  viewport on a 2× device, so the walk uses `viewport: 720` with
  `deviceScaleFactor: 2` — the same layout, reflow and media queries as
  pressing Ctrl and plus. `setPageScaleFactor` is PINCH zoom, which does not
  reflow, and would have measured nothing.

  **THE SUB-320 WIDTHS ARE PRINTED AND NOT COUNTED, DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN.**
  392 at 200% is 196 CSS px and 320 is 160 — both below this product's own
  320px floor. They do overflow there (up to 107px on the calendar); that is
  outside the supported range and is recorded rather than scored.

  **WHAT THIS TICK DOES NOT COVER:** six screens, not every screen; and the

  **8.5b — SCREEN READER. STRUCTURAL HALF DONE 2026-09-20; NOT TICKED, AND IT

  *Done when:* every screen has landmarks, headings descend without skipping a

  **The receipt refused the first version** — 16 assertions against a declared
  floor of 40 — and the fix was to COUNT the landmark and live-region
  questions that were always being asked, then DERIVE the floor from the
  declared screen count. **Deriving the floor rather than nudging it down to
  fit the answer is the difference between a gate and a rubber stamp.**
  **The receipt refused the first version** — 16 assertions against a declared
  floor of 40 — and the fix was to COUNT the landmark and live-region
  questions that were always being asked, then DERIVE the floor from the
  declared screen count. **Deriving the floor rather than nudging it down to
  fit the answer is the difference between a gate and a rubber stamp.**

  **AND IT FOUND ONE, ON THE SURFACE A STRANGER USES.** Every dashboard screen
  declares a `<main>` landmark; `App.jsx`, `JobPage.jsx`, `AdminPage.jsx`, the
  landing page, pricing and legal all render one. **The booking pages rendered
  a bare `<div>`** — so *"jump to the main content"*, the first thing a
  screen-reader user does on any page, did nothing on the booking form or the
  plans page. Fixed with `role="main"` on both (`role` rather than a tag swap:
  the class is doing the layout, and swapping the element would be a styling
  change wearing an accessibility fix's clothes). Re-measured: main=1
  everywhere, 0 findings.

  **THEN THE WALK WAS SEEDED AND THE PATTERN TURNED OUT TO BE WRONG.** Two
  more pages became reachable by handing the walk real ids — the manage screen
  on the booking this session made for 2.8, and a plan member's page on a
  seeded id. **Both were missing the landmark, as expected. Both were ALSO
  skipping a heading level, h1 straight to h3, which nothing in the pattern
  would have suggested** — fixing by pattern would have added the landmark and
  left a listener navigating by heading landing in a level that does not
  exist. **Four screens measured, a claim about nine avoided.**
  Fixed with `aria-level={2}` rather than a different tag: `.bk h3` carries a
  different size and weight from `.bk h2`, so swapping the element would have
  redesigned two reviewed screens to fix a structure problem.
  **The detector had to be corrected for that, and it is not the probe being
  bent to pass its own fix:** it read the tag and stopped, so it flagged pages
  that had just been given the right level. A screen reader uses `aria-level`
  when it is there. The canary heading carries none and is still caught 9/9
  every run, so its ability to see a real skip is unchanged and proved.

  **AND THEN THE LAST ONE WAS MEASURED TOO, WITHOUT A DATABASE WRITE.**
  `BookingConfirmed` is not a route — it is a state `BookingPage` enters after
  a submit — so it had never been looked at by anything, and it is the screen
  a customer lands on **at the moment they have just handed over their money.**
  `app/fixture-confirmed.html` mounts the real component against a fixture
  booking inside the REAL provider, the way `render-emails.mjs` renders an
  email without sending one. **Both branches walked**: a request being held
  and a booking confirmed.
  **THE PREDICTION WAS DECLARED FIRST AND IT WAS RIGHT** — no landmark, an
  h1→h3 skip, zero live regions, on both branches. Being right is not the
  point; it was still measured rather than assumed, and the canaries proved
  the probe could see before the result was believed.
  Fixed the same way as the others, then re-measured to 0 findings.
  **The fixture ships nowhere and that was checked, not claimed:** a
  production build contains `index.html` and `map.html` only, and no bundle
  references the fixture module.

  **THE FINDING UNDERNEATH THE COUNT, AND IT IS NOT A COUNT OF MISSING
  ATTRIBUTES:**

  > **The decisions in this product arrive silently for somebody who is not
  > looking at it — a price that moves, a step that refuses, a booking that
  > confirms.**

  Every one of the eleven screens reports **zero live regions at rest**.
  **One correction, in the product's favour:** the booking step's refusal line
  DOES announce, because 8.5a gave it `role="alert"` — it appears on a press
  rather than at rest, which is why a snapshot counts zero. It is the only
  one. **Written up with a scope, a cost and a recommendation as its own
  proposal in `FOUND.md` § "Four things this product does silently"**, rather
  than left in this note to be rediscovered. It lines up exactly with
  `DECISIONS.md` § *"The job record should stay open when a status changes"*,
  where *"Marked completed."* turns out never to have been readable by
  anybody. **Whether a listener can still complete a booking despite it is the
  question only a person can answer**, and it is the row in `FOR-ANDREW.md`.

  **WHY THIS STAYS OPEN: A SCREEN READER IS A PERSON LISTENING TO A MACHINE
  READ A PAGE ALOUD.** Every question that matters — does the order make
  sense, does it say something useful, can you find your way back — is about
  what a listener understands. The structural half is mechanical and is now
  clean; the half that decides whether this product is usable is in
  `FOR-ANDREW.md` as one screen, one question, thirty seconds.

  **THE PROBE'S OWN BLIND SPOT, AND IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE NUMBER IT
  QUALIFIES:** it finds a clickable thing by its **cursor style or an `onclick`
  attribute**, so **a React handler on an element with a default cursor is
  invisible to it**. The clean sheet above is clean about what it can see and
  no more than that. Also written into `docs/gotchas.md`, because the next
  person to write an accessibility walker will reach for the same two
  signals.
