  ### FIXED IN THE REPO 2026-09-23 — and NOT yet true for any real detailer

  **Diagnosed by DP Cowork, repaired by DP Cowork2** because the repair is one
  change inside `supabase/functions/`. Their write-up
  (`docs/9.1-findings-2026-09-23.md`) is folded in here and the file is gone;
  it existed untracked only because `ROADMAP.md` was held at the time.

  **THE PAYLOAD MOVED, NOT THE READER, AND THAT WAS THE WHOLE CHOICE.**
  `setupProgress()` cannot tell *"this business has not done that step"* from
  *"nobody gave me anything to look at"* — it returns the same confident number
  either way. Two sides could have been changed and **the reader was the side
  that was already right**: the detailer's own dashboard scores correctly
  against it. Teaching `setup.js` to also accept the back office's shapes would
  have created the second implementation this item exists to prevent. So the
  sender was widened and `app/src/lib/setup.js` was not touched — which also
  kept the change out of the other session's tree.

  **WHAT WAS WRONG, MEASURED ON THE SAME BUSINESS IN THE SAME MINUTE:**
  dashboard **9 of 12**, back office **4 of 12**, identical at all five widths.

  - **One field was sent under a name the reader does not read, and as the
    wrong type.** `counts.hoursOpen`, a boolean, where `setup.js:254` asks
    `counts.hoursRows.some((r) => r.open_time)`. `(undefined ?? []).some(...)`
    is `false`, **so every business with real opening hours scored that step
    zero.** It was not a typo — `Business.jsx` really does keep a `hoursOpen`
    boolean in its own counts object for something else, so the name looked
    right sitting next to the real one.
  - **Six of the twelve steps had no input at all**: `vehicle_types`, `hours`,
    `reviews`, `faq`, `payments`, `plans`.
  - **One field was sent that nothing anywhere reads**: `counts.addOns`.
    Add-ons and services are one step, `catalog`, fed by `counts.services`
    alone. **The now-unused `add_ons` query went with it** — it was reading
    every add-on row of every business to compute a number no screen could
    spend.

  **Now 12 of 12, and still one query per table across all businesses** — the
  existing `byBiz` grouper was reused for the hours rows and the existing
  `tally` for reviews and plans. No per-business round trip was added.

  **THEIR CHECK, WHICH I DID NOT TOUCH:**
  `node scripts/setup-inputs-contract.mjs`, credential-free, about a second.
  **`payload-complete` is now green — 12 of 12 from the back office's own
  inputs, against 6 of 12 before.**

  **AND `payload-no-dead-fields` IS STILL RED ON PURPOSE. This is the one
  judgement call in the change and it goes against the check.** It names five
  fields as dead: `pay_venmo`, `pay_cashapp`, `pay_zelle`, `pay_paypal`,
  `pay_other`. They are not dead — `setup.js:258` reads
  `pay_cash || pay_venmo || pay_cashapp || pay_zelle || pay_paypal ||
  pay_other`, and the check's own fixture fills **only `pay_cash`**, so each
  sibling looks redundant while that one stands. **Dropping them to make the
  check green would recreate this exact bug for every detailer who does not
  take cash.** Measured against the real `setupProgress`, not argued:

  | a Venmo-only detailer | score |
  |---|---|
  | all six payment fields sent | **11 of 12**, payments scored |
  | only `pay_cash` sent | **10 of 12**, payments NOT scored |

  **So the red is a limitation of the fixture, not of the payload**, and it is
  left for DP Cowork to judge rather than silently worked around — their check,
  their call. Their own findings file asked for all eight settings fields, so
  this is very likely an oversight in `complete()` rather than a disagreement.

  **AND A SECOND THING FOR THEM, FOUND BY HITTING IT: their parser does not
  strip comments.** It reads the `setup_inputs` keys straight out of the
  source, and a comment sitting between a comma and the key after it swallows
  that key — `hoursRows` was invisible to the check until the prose was moved
  above the literal. **A check that reads a payload as narrower than it is** is
  this file's own subject one level out. A warning now sits above the literal
  so the next person does not lose a field to a sentence.

  **WHAT IS STILL NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS TO A DETAILER:**
  **this is repo-only.** The back office that scores a real account runs on
  Andrew's server and changes only when **he publishes** — 0.6, and
  `deployed-inventory` counted **13 functions already running something other
  than this checkout** on 2026-09-23. **Nobody should tick 9.1 on a green
  check.** The *Done when* stands unchanged: the same account shows the same
  count **on the live site**.

  ### THE CHECK CONFIRMS THE FIX, AND THREE FAULTS IN THE CHECK ITSELF

  **Run rather than assumed, 2026-09-23 after the payload landed:** `PASS —
  17/17 targets, 18 assertions, canary caught`, graded by `receipt.mjs`. The
  payload reads `counts{services,promos,reviews,plans,hoursRows}`,
  `branding{primary_color}`,
  `settings{setup,vehicle_sizes,faqs,pay_cash,pay_venmo,pay_cashapp,pay_zelle,pay_paypal,pay_other}`,
  `business{contact_phone,contact_email}` — **12 of 12 from both sides.** The
  fix was confirmed by the instrument, not by re-measuring anything by hand,
  which is the whole reason it was built before the fix existed.

  **1 · THE PARSER COULD NOT SEE THROUGH A COMMENT, AND THAT IS THIS CHECK'S
  OWN SUBJECT ONE LEVEL OUT.** Found by DP Cowork2 hitting it. A comment
  between a comma and the next key was accumulated into that key's token, the
  token stopped matching an identifier, and **the key was dropped in silence**
  — `hoursRows` was invisible until the prose moved above the literal. This
  check exists because *a reader handed less than it needs answers confidently
  anyway*; its own parser was doing that to itself. **Two failure directions,
  and the quiet one is worse:** when the dropped key is the only thing feeding
  a step, the check falsely accuses the product; when it is one of several
  feeding the same step — as `contact_email` is — **nothing happens at all**.
  **Fixed:** comments are stripped before parsing, with strings copied through
  so a `//` inside one is not a comment. **And it carries a standing
  self-test** — the REAL literal is read out of `platform-admin`, a comment is
  injected between a comma and the key after it, and the keys must come back
  unchanged. Built from the real block so it cannot drift from what that file
  looks like, and it needs no edit to anybody else's file to prove.
  `--break=comments` reproduces the original bug exactly: `counts.promos`
  vanishes and nothing else moves.

  **2 · THE DEAD-FIELD TEST FAILED A CORRECT FIX.** It could only judge a key
  the fixture fills, and the fixture set one payment column of six, so the
  other five looked dead the moment they started being sent. The fixture now
  has every alternative on, **and "dead" and "cannot judge" are reported as
  different answers** — the second is a statement about the check rather than
  about the product, and saying which is which is the difference between a
  finding and a false accusation. Its `FEEDS` row had the same bug from the
  other side: it cleared one column of an OR across six, so the step stayed
  satisfied.

  **3 · `receipt.mjs` REFUSED THE RECEIPT TWICE AND WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES.**
  The declared target count was one short of what the run walked, one target
  never marked itself completed, **and a source-only check still owes a person
  something to look at.** It writes `artifacts/setup-inputs-contract/
  contract.txt` now — which input feeds which step, and the payload's keys read
  out of its own source. *"12 of 12"* says nothing about which is which, and
  that is the whole content of this check.

  has nothing to refer to. Every purely subtractive edit leaves a dangling

     page."* — **claims nothing at all.** The count is already in the
     headline above it. New words: `their booking page` replacing `it`,
     the noun the sibling `open` row's headline already uses.

  **A NIT, NAMED AND HELD RATHER THAN CHASED TONIGHT.** "Last vehicle"
  read *"large · Ford F-150"* — the raw `vehicle_size` enum value,
  lowercase, next to a proper noun. The vehicle-size CONTROL itself
  (`Catalog.jsx`) shows the same tier capitalized, "Large," because it
  reads a detailer's own configured tier label, not the raw booking
  column; this Marcus Webb booking's `vehicle_size_label` is empty, so
  the card falls back to `vehicle_size` unmodified — `{history[0]
  .vehicle_size_label || history[0].vehicle_size}`, no formatting either
  way. **Checked what the fix would actually touch, per Andrew's ask,
  before anyone reaches for one:** this value is not run through `t()` at
  all today, in either case — a separate, slightly larger fact than the
  capitalization alone. `appEs.js` already has `"Large": "Grande"` keyed
  on the capitalized form only; `t()`'s lookup is exact-string, so
  `t("large")` (lowercase) would silently fall back to English regardless
  of any capitalization fix, and the CURRENT code does not call `t()`
  here at all, so it is English either way, on any language dashboard,
  right now. Capitalizing the fallback alone would fix how it looks and
  leave how it translates exactly as broken as today — worth knowing
  before reaching for the smaller-looking fix, which is the whole reason
  this is written up rather than one-lined. **Andrew's ruling: leave it
  broken and visible rather than half-fix it** — capitalizing the English
  alone would make one audience happier and leave the other no better
  while looking like a fix, which he named as the worst kind of small
  edit. Held.

  **"BOOK AGAIN" — BUILT, THE FOURTH AND LAST PIECE OF THIS ITEM.**
  Andrew's ruling on the fork this session stopped at: add the prop, with
  conditions — a "Book again" that opens a blank form is worse than no
  button, because it teaches a detailer the feature doesn't work. What
  made the prop acceptable rather than a design change is that the
  behaviour already existed: `pick(c)` already sets name, phone, email,
  looks up the plan. **One optional prop, `initialCustomer`, defaulting to
  `null`, added to `NewBookingModal.jsx`.** A single effect at mount calls
  the existing `pick()` with it — not a second version of what `pick`
  does, the exact function a manual search already runs. The three
  existing openers (`App.jsx`, `Calendar.jsx`, `Today.jsx`) never pass it,
  so `initialCustomer` is `null` for all three, exactly as before.
  **Scope, named out loud, decided before writing any code:**
  - **Travels:** name, phone, email — real data, exactly what `pick()`
    already carries for a detailer who types a name and taps a search
    result. Book again is byte-identical to that same search-and-tap.
  - **Nominally travels, empty in practice:** address. `pick()` reads
    `c.address`, and `customers.address` is the dead column this item
    already found — so Book again inherits the same limitation manual
    search already has. Considered enriching it with the real address
    from `history[0]` (the same source "Last address" above uses) and
    ruled it out: that would make Book again behave differently from
    manual search for the identical customer, which is a new decision
    about where data comes from, not the existing function doing what it
    already does.
  - **Does not travel:** last vehicle, last service. The detailer picks
    fresh — `pick()` never touches either field, for a manual search or
    for this.
  On the Clients side: one new state variable, one button, and a fourth
  instance of the exact `{state && <NewBookingModal .../>}` shape the
  other three call sites already use — not a new pattern. `onCreated`
  re-runs the existing `openCustomer` so the record reflects the booking
  just made rather than going stale.
  **VERIFIED LIVE, 320 first, then 1440.** Marcus Webb, pressed from his
  record: the modal opened with him already picked (checkmark, no search
  step), "Customer name / Phone / Email" all pre-filled, and the plan
  lookup fired too — "On Bi-weekly maintenance. The plan price is applied
  automatically." Vehicle size sat at its own default ("Small"), unfilled,
  matching the scope above. **The one check that actually proves the
  three existing openers are untouched, not just unedited in source:**
  Today's own "New booking" button, pressed fresh, opened a genuinely
  blank form — empty search box, no customer picked. `scrollWidth ===
  clientWidth` at 320 with the modal open; no console error at either
  width. `tests/composition.test.mjs` 97/97, `scripts/label-guard.mjs`
  clean. No new translatable string — `t("Book again")` already existed.
  ~~**Still not ticked**~~ — **and the press found a money fault the build had
  not, which is the whole argument for the standard.**

  ***SENT BACK 2026-10-08, FIXED, RE-PRESSED AND TICKED.*** Live on his laptop:
  **the client card read "Last vehicle: Large · Ford F-150" and Book again
  opened on Vehicle size Small with Make and model blank.** The scope note four
  paragraphs up calls that deliberate — *"Does not travel: last vehicle, last
  service. The detailer picks fresh"* — and it is wrong for one reason nothing
  in that reasoning weighed: **the size is the only field on that form that
  carries a PRICE.** A tap on Book again for a customer whose truck is Large
  books it at the Small price, and the screen the detailer just read said Large.
  *"Picks fresh"* is a fair rule for a service; for a price it is a mis-charge
  one tap away.

  **THE FIX KEEPS THIS ITEM'S OWN EARLIER RULING RATHER THAN OVERTURNING IT.**
  That ruling refused to enrich Book again alone, so that it could not behave
  differently from a manual search for the identical customer. Both routes run
  `pick()`, so **the lookup went into `pick()`** — both carry the vehicle now and
  the two stay identical, which is the property the ruling was protecting. It
  reads the same booking the card calls *"Last"*, so **the card and the form the
  card opens cannot disagree**, which was the complaint. Each field is carried
  only if the previous booking had one: a blank model may not wipe a typed one,
  a null travel zone may not clear a chosen zone.

  **AND "AGAIN" IS A CLAIM ABOUT THEM.** A client with no visits now gets
  **"Book" / "Reservar"**; it defaults to "Book again" while `history` is still
  `null`, so a returning client never flashes the wrong word — this item's own
  unknown-vs-empty rule, applied to a label.

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-20 — 9.8 Manual booking flashes "No active services yet"
  before loading.** Replace false empty states with a loading skeleton; only
  show empty after a completed empty response.
  *A1 P2-14*

  **THE DISTINCTION IS UNKNOWN VERSUS KNOWN-EMPTY, NOT LOADING VERSUS EMPTY —
  Andrew's framing, and it is the correct one.** `NewBookingModal.jsx`'s
  `catalog` state started as `{ services: [], addOns: [], groups: [] }`, so
  `catalog.services.length === 0` read true for the entire time between the
  component mounting and its fetch answering — indistinguishable from a
  detailer who genuinely has no active services. A slow connection told every
  detailer opening this form that their own business sold nothing. The fix
  is not a prettier empty state; it is making the third state exist at all.

  **BUILT.** A sibling boolean, `catalogLoaded` (`NewBookingModal.jsx`), false
  until the fetch resolves — not a reshape of `catalog` itself to `null`,
  because `grouped` (a `useMemo` derived from `catalog.services`/`.groups`)
  and two other read sites consume it unconditionally on every render
  including the first; a smaller diff for the same three states. This mirrors
  the exact idiom already sitting three lines below it in the same file —
  `slots`, `useState(null) // null = not searched yet` — chosen as a sibling
  rather than adopting that shape directly, for the reason above.

  While `!catalogLoaded`, three inert pill shapes render in place of both the
  chip list and the "No active services yet" sentence — new class
  `.nb-chip-skel` in `theme.css`, sized off `.chip`'s own box model (36px,
  `--r-pill`, `--hairline`) rather than composing the class itself, because a
  skeleton must not answer to `.chip:hover`/`:disabled` and must not be in
  the tab order — a `<div>`, never a `<button>`. No new `@media
  (prefers-reduced-motion)` block — `.lite .nb-chip-skel { animation: none }`
  instead, the one answer to that question this file already has (see the
  `.foldrow` chevron's own comment on why a second copy is how two answers to
  one question start).

  Swept `app/src/` for the same shape: a `useState([])` fed by a component's
  own fetch, read straight into an unconditional "no X yet" message with
  nothing distinguishing "has not asked" from "asked and there is nothing."
  Most of the dashboard already gets this right and says so in its own

  **RULING, WRITTEN BEFORE THE BUILD SO IT READS AS A DECISION RATHER THAN
  AN INCONSISTENCY — 2026-09-20.** All three get the same underlying fix —
  stop claiming zero until the real answer is back — but not the same
  costume. **None of the three gets 9.8's skeleton.** A settings picker that
  has never animated does not need motion introduced onto it to fix a timing

  with 9.8 as its excuse. Instead each takes the quietest thing its own
  screen already knows how to do:

    **the marker for this exact case was already built and sitting two
    lines from where it was needed, just never wired to it.** That is a
    different, cheaper kind of fault than a missing feature, and it is the
    second time tonight this repo turned out to already contain what it
    needed, after 9.7 finding the client card's vehicle and last-service
    data already sitting in state. Two is a pattern worth naming before a
    third makes it one.
  - **BookingDetail** and **Catalog** each get a small sibling boolean next
    to their own fetch, matching the reasoning `NewBookingModal.jsx` already
    wrote down for the same shape of problem: their lists are read
    unconditionally in more than one place, so reshaping the list itself
    into a loading state — the way `mail` already does elsewhere in
    `BookingDetail.jsx` — would mean guarding every read instead of adding
    one flag. No skeleton, no new markup, no new translated string; the
    message just waits one beat longer before it is allowed to print.

  ### THE `app/src` HALF — what Lane A renders, so it can start without asking

  **WHERE: `/admin` only.** This is the platform owner's own figure — what the
  PLATFORM earned and spent — and no detailer ever sees it. 9.12 and
  `main.jsx:126` are why. **Read it through the `platform_net` action on
  `platform-admin`**, like every other number on that screen; `platform_costs`
  has no RLS policy at all, so a browser query returns nothing.

  **THE THREE STATES, AND THE THIRD IS THE ITEM:**

  | state | what the screen says |
  |---|---|
  | `costs_entered: true` | revenue, costs, and the net. A **negative** net is shown as a loss — never clamped, never hidden; a month that cost more than it earned is the most important thing this screen can say |
  | `costs_entered: true`, `cost_cents: 0` | a real zero, because a person asserted it. Show the net |
  | **`costs_entered: false`** | **“Costs not entered for this month” and NO net figure at all.** Not “—” beside a profit, not a greyed number, not the revenue with a warning. **The field is null; render nothing numeric** |

  **THE CONTROL IT NEEDS:** a way to type a cost — month, category, amount,
  note. **Amounts are entered as dollars and stored as cents**; `MoneyField`
  in `app/src/components/controls.jsx` already exists for exactly this and must
  be reached for before writing an input (CLAUDE.md § Conventions).
  **THE WRITE ACTION EXISTS — `platform_cost_add` on `platform-admin`, built
  2026-10-06. Nothing deployed.** Never write to the table from the browser;
  it has no RLS policy and the insert would be refused.

  | send | rule |
  |---|---|
  | `action` | `"platform_cost_add"` |
  | `period_month` | `"2026-10"`, or any `YYYY-MM-DD` inside the month; stored as the first |
  | `category` | exactly one of `hosting`, `database`, `email`, `domain`, `other` (lower case) |
  | `amount_cents` | **a JSON integer of cents.** Convert dollars on the screen with `MoneyField`; `"1250"`, `12.5` and `null` are all refused. 0 is allowed, negatives are not |
  | `note` | optional text, at most 300 characters |

  **Answers:** `{ success: true, id }` on save. **A refusal is a 400 whose
  `error` is a finished sentence — show it as-is beside the form**, e.g. *“The
  amount must be a whole number of cents, like 1250 for $12.50.”*, *“Pick what
  the bill is for: hosting, database, email, domain or other.”*, *“The month
  has to be written like 2026-10.”* A 500 is also a sentence, and until the
  migration runs it says *“Costs cannot be saved yet: the costs table has not
  been set up. Nothing was saved.”* A non-admin gets the same bare 404 as every
  other action.

  **After a save, re-read `platform_net` for that month** rather than adding
  the figure on the screen — the month's total is the server's to compute.
  **No edit and no delete yet**: a wrong bill cannot be corrected from the
  screen. Ask for them when the screen exists rather than building around it.

  **FOUR CATEGORIES PLUS `other`, as a segmented control and not a `<select>`**
  — five mutually exclusive choices is what `Segmented` is for, per the same
  convention.

  **WHAT FAILING LOOKS LIKE:** a net figure on a month nobody has entered costs
  for (the item's own words), a loss displayed as zero or as a positive, or the
  cost list read directly from the browser — which returns an empty array with
  no error and looks exactly like a month with no costs.

  **AND IT CANNOT BE SEEN UNTIL THE MIGRATION RUNS.** `platform_costs` does not
  exist in the live database; `node scripts/migration-drift.mjs` names it today.
  Until then the action's cost query errors rather than returning empty — which
  is deliberate (a failed read must not read as “costs not entered”), so the
  screen will show an error and not a confident zero.

  ***THE SERVER HALF WAS ALREADY BUILT. WHAT 2026-10-07 ADDED IS THE TABLE RUN
  ON A REAL DATABASE (DP Cowork2, Lane B). NOTHING APPLIED, NOTHING DEPLOYED,
  NO DDL AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE.*** A session was sent to build this half
  and found all four pieces — the migration file, `_shared/platformNet.js`, both
  actions and `tests/platform-net.test.mjs` — present and green. **The one thing
  the standard asked for and this item did not have was a test that asks the
  DATABASE rather than greps the migration.**

  **WHY A GREP WAS NOT ENOUGH, and it is this repo's own scar.**
  `tests/platform-net.test.mjs` § 7 reads the migration as text and asserts the
  words `enable row level security`, `force row level security` and `revoke all
  …` are in it. That is a lock that READS correctly.
  `20260921000000_revoke_locked_table_grants.sql` is the record of ten tables in
  this project that read exactly that way and were not locked: RLS on, zero
  policies, and Supabase's default grant still in place — **`anon` held INSERT
  on the audit trail until it ran.** This table holds what the platform spends
  and no detailer may ever read it, so the lock is now asserted by asking
  Postgres, under the roles a browser actually arrives as.

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | the new test | `tests/platform-costs-sql.test.mjs` |
  | how to run it | `npm install @electric-sql/pglite` in any folder OUTSIDE the repo, then `PGLITE_DIR=<that folder> node --test tests/platform-costs-sql.test.mjs` |
  | what it ran on | **PGlite — real PostgreSQL in WebAssembly, in process.** Nothing touches the live database, and it is in no `package.json`. The same arrangement as `tests/send-invoice-key-sql.test.mjs` and `tests/action-log-sql.test.mjs` |
  | the result | **9 pass, 0 fail**, at the commit carrying this block |
  | with no PGlite | every case prints `NOT RUN — needs @electric-sql/pglite …` and skips; `PGLITE_REQUIRED=1` turns the same run into **9 fail**. Both measured, because a guard that skips must say so |

  **WHAT IT PROVES, AND IT IS THE LOCK FIRST:** zero policies on the table; both
  RLS flags set in `pg_class`; `anon` and `authenticated` hold **none** of
  select, insert, update, delete; and under `set role anon` and `set role
  authenticated` a `select *` and an insert are both answered **permission
  denied** — the read asserted as its own case, because reading is the one 9.14
  cares about most. Then the shape: the period constraint takes the 1st and
  refuses the 15th; the five categories are exactly what the table takes and
  `Hosting` is refused by the DATABASE as well as by `costEntry`; a zero bill is
  allowed and a negative one is not; `updated_at` moves on an update while
  `created_at` does not, so the trigger from `foundation.sql` is really
  installed.

  **AND IT FOUND SOMETHING NO SOURCE SCAN COULD: `integer` ROUNDS, IT DOES NOT
  REFUSE.** Inserting `12.5` cents — dollars-with-decimals arriving where cents
  belong — is accepted by the column and stored as a whole number. So
  `costEntry`'s *“The amount must be a whole number of cents, like 1250 for
  $12.50.”* is **the only thing between a screen bug and a wrong figure in the
  database**, and the case is in the suite so nobody later removes that guard as
  redundant because "the column is an integer anyway".

  **THREE SABOTAGES, EACH ASSERTED TO HAVE CHANGED THE SQL BEFORE ITS VERDICT IS
  BELIEVED** (`docs/gotchas.md` 95): the period constraint removed and the 15th
  goes in; the amount check removed and a negative bill goes in; **the revoke
  removed and `anon` holds `select` on the platform's costs.**

  **THE THIRD SABOTAGE IS THE ONE WORTH READING.** With the revoke gone, RLS is
  still enabled and forced — and `anon`'s `select` **does not fail. It returns
  an empty answer with no error at all.** An empty answer is indistinguishable
  from a month with no costs: 9.14's own unknown-versus-known-empty trap,
  arriving at the security layer instead of on the screen. **The revoke is what
  turns that silence into a refusal**, and it is the half this repo has already
  shipped without once.

  **WHAT IT CANNOT SHOW, said rather than implied:** that `force row level
  security` does anything, because the role running the statements owns the
  table and PGlite's superuser bypasses RLS regardless. Those two flags are read
  as declarations. **That is the same split the live database has** — the
  service role bypasses RLS too, so the GRANT is what stands between a browser
  and this table, and the grant is the half that is proved behaviourally.

  **THE ARITHMETIC SUITE RE-RUN AT THE SAME COMMIT:** `node --test
  tests/platform-net.test.mjs` → **16 pass, 0 fail** (15 cases and their parent).
  **`PLATFORM_NET_CANARY=1 node --test tests/platform-net.test.mjs` → 2 fail**,
  section 9 and the parent it hangs under, which is the canary asserting 9.14's
  fault — a net equal to revenue with no costs entered — and failing as it must.

  ### THE CONTRACT, COMPLETED — THE READ'S REQUEST WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN

  Everything the screen SENDS to save a bill is specified above, field by field,
  and re-checked against `_shared/platformNet.js` at this commit: it holds.
  **The read's own request shape was missing.** Lane A found it from the source
  while building; the next session should not have to.

  | send | rule |
  |---|---|
  | `action` | `"platform_net"` |
  | `period` | **optional.** Any date string inside the month — `"2026-10"`, `"2026-10-01"`, `"2026-10-17T22:10:00Z"` all ask about October 2026. **Omit it and the server answers for the month it is in**, so the screen has a figure before anybody picks a period |
  | nothing else | no `business_id` — this is the platform's own figure and has no business on it |

  **The answer carries the period it answered about:** `period_month`, always
  `YYYY-MM-01`. **Render that, never the month the screen asked for** — the
  server normalises, and the two disagree the moment a screen sends a bare
  `"2026-10"` and reads its own string back.

  `marketing`) and `TAB_NEEDS` in `App.jsx` hides a whole tab, not one
  row, when the ticked list doesn't cover it. **So this is not "one row
  hidden," it is a real permission tier**, already built, already
  enforced on the database side per that file's own comment ("hiding a
  tab is never the enforcement — the migration is"), and this item's

- [x] **9.17 (original entry) — Opening the Settings gear puts a 404 in the console, twice, at
  every width — and the request it comes from is working exactly as designed.**
  Found 2026-10-07 by DP Cowork sweeping 4.1 (`c8cd339`); it predates that work.
  **The 404 is not the bug. The bug is that a deliberately silent endpoint
  announces itself in red, on a screen every detailer opens, in a way nobody can
  tell apart from a real failure** — and it was read as a failure, which is how
  this item got filed.

  **WHICH REQUEST, measured rather than reasoned about.** `POST
  /functions/v1/platform-admin` with `{action:"whoami"}`, fired from
  `GearMenu.jsx:163` in a mount effect. `platform-admin/index.ts:97` answers
  **404 to anybody who is not a platform admin**, on purpose, and its own comment
  says why in terms this item must not break: *"What it must never become is an
  action that returns `{admin:false}` instead of 404 — that would turn a silent
  endpoint into one that confirms itself to anybody who asks."* `GearMenu.jsx`
  agrees from the other side: *"A 404 IS THE ORDINARY ANSWER HERE, not an error."*

  **WHAT HAPPENS, measured 2026-10-07 on a worktree dev server at :5181 and a
  production bundle at :5182, signed in as `demo-staff@detailplatform.com`, an
  ordinary non-admin member, three gear opens per width.** Re-take: sign in as a
  non-admin, open the gear, count `platform-admin` responses.

  | | dev server | production bundle |
  |---|---|---|
  | `platform-admin` calls on the FIRST gear open | **2**, both 404 | **1**, 404 |
  | on the second and third open | **0** | **0** |
  | widths showing it | **5 of 5** (1920, 1440, 768, 392, 320) | **5 of 5** |
  | gap between the pair | 52–142ms | n/a |

  **SO THE DOUBLING IS DEV-ONLY AND THE 404 IS NOT**, and the two halves have
  different costs. The pair is `React.StrictMode` (`app/src/main.jsx:72`)
  double-invoking the mount effect, and the cache that exists to stop repeat
  calls cannot stop it: `adminSeen` is assigned at `GearMenu.jsx:172`, **after**
  the `fetch` resolves, so both invocations are already in flight before either
  one writes it. **The cache is not broken** — opens two and three make zero
  calls, measured — it just cannot see a sibling that has not answered yet.

  **WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not the detailer's cost.** One wasted edge-function
  call on a first gear open is nothing. What it costs is **every reader of this
  repo's console**: a red `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a
  status of 404` on the one screen every browser check passes through, and the
  product's own design says it must stay a 404. It has already been paid twice —
  once when this was filed as a defect, and once in the instrument: three browser
  scripts here carry console-noise filters, and a line that must be filtered by
  name is a line that hides the next real one behind it. **`docs/gotchas.md`'s
  running theme is a check that cannot tell a pass from a did-not-run; this is a
  console that cannot tell a designed answer from a failure.**

  **ONE DOOR IS SHUT AND A LATER ITEM SHUT IT, so nobody should reopen it
  without saying why.** The obvious fix is to let the browser read its own row
  out of `platform_admins` instead of asking an endpoint — a 200-or-empty query
  rather than a 404. **It is the wrong door.** That table is RLS-on with zero
  policies (`20260906001000_platform_admin.sql:51`) **and** had its grants
  revoked from `authenticated` deliberately
  (`20260921000000_revoke_locked_table_grants.sql:38`). Opening a self-read
  policy on it would be undoing a lock a later migration put on on purpose, which
  is CLAUDE.md's shared-variable rule exactly.

  **Done when:** **(a)** a first gear open makes **one** `platform-admin` call,
  not two, at every width on the dev server — so the fix is in the cache's
  timing (an in-flight marker written before the request, not after its answer)
  rather than in StrictMode being switched off, because StrictMode is a
  development aid and turning it off to quieten a log would hide the class of
  fault it exists to surface; **(b)** `platform-admin` still answers **404** to a
  non-admin, unchanged, and a check asserts it — anything that makes it answer
  `{admin:false}` fails this item rather than completing it; and **(c)** the
  remaining console line is something a reader can tell apart from a failure, or
  it is recorded in one named place as expected noise with the reason, so the
  next person reading a console does not re-file this.

  **(c) IS THE ONLY OPEN DESIGN QUESTION AND IT IS NOT MINE TO SETTLE.** A 4xx
  from `fetch` is logged by Chrome and **cannot be suppressed from JavaScript**,
  so the only ways to remove the line are to stop using a status code to carry
  the answer — which (b) forbids — or to stop asking. Parked for Andrew rather
  than decided here, because the alternative is inventing a third option and
  calling it a requirement.

  observation ran on an isolated worktree on :5181 and :5182 so that lane's

- [ ] **9.18 — The back office's System health tab cannot read the email log,
  and the error it shows is about a parameter it never sent.** Found 2026-10-07
  while sweeping the back office for 9.11e: **HTTP 400 from
  `/functions/v1/platform-admin` at every width**, 9 console lines across five

  checkout. It is a publish gap wearing a code fault's clothes**, which is why
  it is filed rather than fixed.

  **WHAT HAPPENS.** `AdminPage.jsx:2172` renders `<EmailList />` inside
  `TabPipes`, and `AdminPage.jsx:1981` asks `{action:"email_list", limit:100}`
  on mount. The answer is **`400 {"error":"business_id is required"}`** —
  measured 2026-10-07 by calling the live function directly with a throwaway
  platform admin's token, not inferred from the browser. The screen does what it
  should with that: it prints *"Could not read the email log: business_id is
  required."* **On a screen that has no business on it, and from a call that
  never mentioned one.**

  **WHY, AND THE DEDUCTION IS FROM THE ANSWER ITSELF.** In this checkout
  `email_list` is handled at `platform-admin/index.ts:181` and returns
  `emailList()`'s own messages — it **cannot** produce the string
  `"business_id is required"`, which exists only at `:634` (the `get` guard) and
  `:851`. So the running bundle has no `email_list` branch and the request falls
  through to a later guard. `email_list` entered the function in **`dd33fbc`,
  2026-10-06, *"ROADMAP 3.1 server half"*, which is also the last commit to
  touch it** — and it was never published.

  **Confirmed against the deployed inventory rather than assumed:**
  `receipts/deployed-inventory.json`, **another lane's run**, finished
  2026-10-08T02:08Z at `8fcb154`, names
  *`platform-admin`: 6 file(s) differ — `index.ts` | `_shared/email.ts` |
  `_shared/emailTemplates.ts` | `_shared/platformNet.js` |
  **`_shared/emailList.js`** | `_shared/strings/es.ts` (newest commit is 15.1d
  after the deploy)*. **The module that implements this action is not on the
  server at all.** *(That receipt was READ and deliberately not re-run, because
  it was already dirty in the working tree — `docs/shared-resources.md` § 7.)*

  **WHY IT MATTERS, and the publish gap is only half of it.** The back office's
  email log is the one place anybody can see what this product actually sent —
  that is what ROADMAP 3.1 built it for — and it has shown an error instead since
  the day the screen started asking. **The sharper half is the sentence.** A
  reader is told a parameter is missing. It is not missing; it was never asked
  for. **An unshipped action silently inherits a different action's refusal**,
  and the message sends whoever reads it at the wrong thing entirely — which is
  this repo's recurring shape, a failure that reads as a different, plausible
  failure. **The next action that ships ahead of its server half will do exactly
  the same**, and nothing anywhere will say so.

  **NOT A CODE CHANGE, AND NOBODY SHOULD MAKE ONE FOR THE FIRST HALF.**
  Publishing is Andrew's (CLAUDE.md, and `FOR-ANDREW.md` carries the shipping
  order). A session that "fixes" this by editing `app/src` or the function would
  be repairing something that is already correct in the repository.

  **Done when:** **(a)** `platform-admin` is deployed from this checkout and
  `node scripts/deployed-inventory.mjs` stops naming it; **(b)** an
  authenticated `{action:"email_list", limit:100}` answers **200 with a `rows`
  array** — pressable with a throwaway admin's token the way this was found;
  **(c)** the System health tab draws the list with **no 400 in the console at
  any width**; and **(d)** — the part that outlives the deploy — **an action
  the function does not handle answers `"Unknown action"`, never another
  action's refusal.** Today an unhandled action falls through the handler chain
  until some later guard happens to reject it, and a check should fail when a
  known action name produces a message naming a parameter that action does not
  take.

  **(d) is the one worth building**, because (a) to (c) stop being true of
  nothing the moment Andrew publishes — undeployed as of 2026-10-07, per the
  receipt named above — and the fall-through will still be there waiting for the
  next action.

  ***(d) BUILT 2026-10-07 (DP Cowork2, Lane B). CODE AND A TEST, NOTHING
  DEPLOYED.*** The box stays `[ ]`: (a), (b) and (c) are a publish, and
  publishing is Andrew's.

  **THE FIX IS A GATE, NOT A MESSAGE.** Every action below
  `platform-admin/index.ts`'s shared per-business guard needs a `business_id`,

  function does not handle at all. The eight business-scoped actions are now
  named in a `BUSINESS_ACTIONS` set immediately above it, and **anything else
  gets the same `400 "Unknown action"` the tail of the handler has always
  returned.** 400 and not the admin gate's 404: that 404 means *you are not an
  admin* and has to keep meaning only that.

  **WHY A SET RATHER THAN A SENTENCE PER ACTION.** The fault was positional —
  an unhandled name falling into a guard that belonged to `get` — so a fix that
  re-words the guard leaves the fall-through in place. The set is also the one
  place a new business-scoped action goes; one left out of it answers "Unknown
  action", which is the honest failure rather than a misleading one.

  **CHECKED AS AN INVARIANT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT AS A SPELLING.**
  `tests/platform-admin.test.mjs` § 15 (new) reads the set out of the function
  and compares it against the `action === "…"` branches that actually sit below
  it: every branch below must be named (a discovery floor — more than eight is
  not a fault), **and every name must really be handled**, because a name in
  the set that nothing handles passes the gate and falls to the `business_id`

- [x] **9.19 — The fade at the bottom of every dashboard screen is 40px taller
  than the gap left for it, so the last line of content is always under it.**
  Found by DP Cowork during 9.4, 2026-10-07. **FIXED 2026-10-10 — see the paragraph below; the original text follows it unedited.**

  ***FIXED 2026-10-10, measured at the commit that carries this paragraph, with the numbers below taken from
  `receipts/scrim-clearance.json` (PASS, 11 of 11 targets, 33 assertions, canary caught) and its sabotage twin.***
  **The change is two lines in `app/src/theme.css`:** `--tabclear` is now `136px + safe-b` (was 96) and `.tabscrim`'s height
  is `var(--tabclear)` with nothing added (was `+ 40px`). The strip is the same strip it always was — solid to 76px, fading
  over the top 60px — so the look of the bar is untouched; what moved is **where the page stops**: the last pixel of content
  now rests where the fade has already ended. Cost, stated plainly: **40px more empty ground under the last row** on phone and
  tablet screens. Desktop (1024+) never had the strip and is unchanged.

  **WHY RAISING `--tabclear` WAS SAFE HERE** (CLAUDE.md's shared-variable rule, in full). The only readers are `theme.css`'s
  three (the page's bottom padding, the scrim's height, `html:has(.tabbar)`'s `scroll-padding-bottom`) and
  `tabbar-clearance.mjs`'s canary. The padding and the scrim are *meant* to be the same number — raising it is how the
  stylesheet's own comment becomes true. The scroll padding rises with it, so a focused control is now parked 40px higher,
  which is further from the bar, not nearer. **2.32's finding stands and is not contradicted:** a reserve never fixed focus
  parking, and this does not claim to — it fixes where the page ENDS. `--bk-bar-clear` is a different variable on pages with
  no tab bar and is not touched. **Shrinking the strip instead was weighed and rejected:** fading 76→96 is a 20px edge, the
  band `:1229` was written to avoid.

  **THE GATE, `scripts/scrim-clearance.mjs` (done-when (b)) — it reads PIXELS, because the scrim is `pointer-events: none`.**
  The fade's own opacity comes from a render with everything else hidden on a white ground; each text line in the last 40px
  of content is graded with and without that fade. **Red on the build before the fix, for real:** `app/src/theme.css` was put
  back byte-identical to `HEAD` (`git diff --numstat` empty, so the break landed) and the run reported **20 failures of 33
  assertions** — the fade 67% opaque over the band at all ten states, the calendar legend **6.78:1 → 1.92:1 in English and
  6.78:1 → 1.99:1 in Spanish at 320x640**, client rows 6.6:1 → 3.0:1, the calendar's bottom card 6.2:1 → 3.59:1. **Green after:**
  fade 1% over the band everywhere, every line unchanged (legend 6.4–6.7:1, clients 6.4–6.8:1). `--break=old-geometry` puts
  the old 96/136 pair back for the whole run (20 failures, receipt `scrim-clearance.sabotage.json`); the in-run canary does the
  same on the legend and was caught; `--break=canary` drops it and the receipt refuses (10 of 11 targets, canary MISSED).
  **Done-when (a):** at 320x640 in both languages, on the calendar legend and on Clients (text-dense, not the calendar) the
  last 40px measures 6.4:1 or better — above 4.5:1 — against what is painted over it.
  **A number that did NOT reproduce, said plainly:** DP Cowork's *1.47:1 in Spanish* — this run reads 1.95–1.99:1 for the
  same legend pressed to the content line. Their English figure (1.92:1) reproduces. The gap is probably the scroll position
  the legend was caught at (Spanish wraps deeper); the defect and its size are the same.
  **Done-when (c):** `tabbar-clearance.mjs` **PASS, 16 of 16 targets, 48 assertions**, canary caught; `bk-bar-clearance.mjs`
  **137 of 137 targets, 955 assertions, gate HELD, 0 outside the declared hold** (14.37's three rows still read *0 of N rows*
  covered at the end of scrolling). **Which instrument covers which:** the hit-test ones (`tabbar-clearance`,
  `bk-bar-clearance`) cover *can it be pressed*; `scrim-clearance` covers *can it be read* — the half gotchas 100 says no hit
  test can see. **What it does not cover:** the exact glyph pixels (it takes the worst fade opacity anywhere in a line's box,
  a floor), and any screen other than Calendar and Clients at 320 and 392 (the other tabs share the same shell strip, so the
  geometry is the same, but they are not each pressed).
  **Two instrument faults found and fixed while building it, kept because both printed a false defect:** the ground under text
  here is dithered by a noise layer, so a "most common pixel" background was the TEXT's own colour (1.37:1 on a label that reads
  6.5:1); and the page scrolls smoothly, so rects read in the same breath as `scrollBy` belong to a position the screenshot never
  sees. **Screenshots** before and after, 320 and 390 and 1440, are in the belt's `shots/9.19/`.

  **IN PLAIN WORDS.** The tab bar at the bottom of the app is glass, so a strip
  of fading ground is painted behind it — otherwise the page's own words show
  through the bar. The shell reserves a gap at the bottom of every screen so
  content stops above that strip. **The gap is 96px and the strip is 136px**, so
  **the last 40px of content on any dashboard screen sits inside the fade**:
  still visible, but washed out against it. On a short screen there is nowhere
  else for the content to go, so this is where the eye actually lands.

  **THE GEOMETRY, READ OUT OF THE STYLESHEET AT THIS COMMIT** (not inferred, and
  re-checkable in one pass):

  | | where | what it says |
  |---|---|---|
  | the gap | `app/src/theme.css:341`, `:1122` | `--tabclear: calc(96px + var(--safe-b))`, and `.app-main`'s bottom padding IS `--tabclear` |
  | the strip | `app/src/theme.css:1235` | `.tabscrim { height: calc(var(--tabclear) + 40px) }` — **the same variable plus forty** |
  | the fade | `app/src/theme.css:1237` | solid `--ink-0` from the bottom up to `calc(100% - 60px)`, then fading over the top 60px |
  | where it is | `app/src/App.jsx:610` | one `<div className="tabscrim">` in the shell, OUTSIDE `<main>` — so it is over **every** dashboard screen, not one |
  | where it is not | `app/src/theme.css:1441` | `@media (min-width: 1024px)` sets `.tabscrim { display: none }` and drops the padding to `--sp-6`. **This is a phone-and-tablet fault only** |

  With `--safe-b` at 0: content's last pixel comes to rest 96px above the
  bottom; the strip covers 0–136px; it is solid to 76px and fades from 76 to
  136. **96 to 136 is content, and all of it is inside the fade.** The overlap
  is not conditional on height — a short viewport is simply where there is no
  room to scroll past it.

  **WHAT IT MEASURED, AND THESE ARE DP COWORK'S NUMBERS, NOT RE-TAKEN HERE.**
  On the calendar legend at **320x640**: **1.92:1 in English, 1.47:1 in
  Spanish**, against **6.97:1 for the same legend at the project's five
  standard sizes**. The Spanish figure is the worse one because the legend
  wraps differently and lands deeper into the fade. *Not re-measured by this
  session on purpose: a browser sweep of the demo tenant while Lane A is
  measuring it is the collision CLAUDE.md § Commands and `docs/gotchas.md`
  describe, where the victim's run completes and simply comes back strange. The
  geometry above is what this session verified, and it is enough to say the
  overlap is real and exactly 40px.*

  **AND THE STYLESHEET SAYS, IN WRITING, THAT THIS CANNOT HAPPEN.**
  `theme.css:1147`, over the scrim: *“ONE NUMBER, `--tabclear`, SHARED WITH
  `.app-main`'s BOTTOM PADDING. The space the page reserves and the space the
  ground covers are the same space; two numbers is how one of them drifts.”*
  **They are not the same space. One of them is the other plus forty**, eighty
  lines further down in the same file. The comment is not wrong about the rule;
  it is a comment describing an invariant that the code beside it breaks, which
  is why every reader since has had no reason to look. That is the real cost of
  this one, and it is why (b) of the done-when is a gate rather than a careful
  pair of eyes.

  **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS.** 1.47:1 is not "a bit faint" — it is
  below the 3:1 this project treats as the floor for anything large and well
  under 4.5:1 for body text, so the bottom line of a screen is effectively
  unreadable rather than merely dim. **And it is every screen**, because the
  strip lives in the shell: the legend is where it was caught, not where it is.
  It has also been invisible to every check here, which is the second half of
  the finding and is written up as `docs/gotchas.md` 100.

  **`--tabclear` IS A SHARED VARIABLE AND CHANGING IT IS NOT LOCAL.** CLAUDE.md
  § Hard rules, *"BEFORE CHANGING A SHARED VARIABLE, FIND OUT WHETHER A PREVIOUS
  ITEM ALREADY DECIDED NOT TO"* — `--bk-bar-clear` is the worked example and
  this is the same shape. `--tabclear` is read by `.app-main`'s padding
  (`:1122`), the scrim's height (`:1235`) and `scroll-padding-bottom` together
  with `--hit-overhang` (`:1184`), and `theme.css:1147` already records that the
  one number is deliberately shared with `.app-main`, while `:1153` records a
  measurement that **`--tabclear` could never have fixed** a related fault.
  **So raising `--tabclear` by 40px is the obvious move and is the one most
  likely to be wrong**: it moves the reserved gap, the scroll padding and the
  strip together, and `scripts/tabbar-clearance.mjs`'s own `--break=rect` is the
  record of what a clearance sized to the wrong box leaves behind — four
  pressable rows under the bar while the run reports itself finished. Shrinking
  the strip instead re-opens what `:1229`–`:1234` was written to fix: words
  faintly readable along the bar's top edge.

  **Done when:** **(a)** the last 40px of content on a dashboard screen measures
  **at least 4.5:1** against whatever is painted over it, at **320x640 in both
  languages**, pressed on the calendar legend (where it was found) and on one
  text-dense screen that is not the calendar; **(b)** there is a gate that can
  SEE this — one that goes **red on the build before the fix** and green after,
  because `scripts/tabbar-clearance.mjs` hit-tests and `pointer-events: none`
  makes this strip invisible to it (`docs/gotchas.md` 100), and the
  credential-free contrast gates measure token PAIRS, which cannot describe a
  gradient composited over a label; and **(c)** if `--tabclear` itself moved,
  every consumer named in the table above is re-measured in the same change and
  `tabbar-clearance.mjs` is still green, with the reason it is safe now written
  in the commit — CLAUDE.md's shared-variable rule, in full.

  **What failing looks like:** a fix signed off by a hit test, which will report
  the strip uncovered while it is painted over at 1.47:1; or `--tabclear` raised
  on its own, which moves the bar's clearance and the scroll padding with it and
  can leave controls resting under the bar while every other line of the run
  reads normally.

  **THE TWO THAT ARE MORE THAN TIDYING.** The surcharge fix pluralises long day
  names **by a rule rather than a table** — add an `s` unless the name already
  ends in one — which is correct in English (*Saturday → Saturdays*) and in
  Spanish (*sábado → sábados*, while *lunes*, *martes*, *miércoles*, *jueves* and
  *viernes* are invariant), so it needs no catalogue entries and cannot drift out
  of step with them; `Intl.ListFormat` supplies the conjunction in the reader's
  own language, and the list is sorted **Monday-first** because a weekend is
  named Saturday-first in both, while the calendar grid stays Sunday-first
  because that is a grid and this is a sentence. And the job-page cap is **560,
  the measure that same record already gets in the desk's two-column layout** —
  three containers agreeing rather than one of them inheriting the width of the
  page it happens to sit on. **`--wrap` is untouched**, which is the
  shared-variable rule: the fault was one route taking the page width, not the

- [ ] **9.21 — The job record says "Receipt + thank-you sent." when the
  thank-you was not sent.** Found by DP Cowork at `96d7eb6`, answering a cold
  read of ROADMAP 6.4. **Filed, not built.**

  **IN PLAIN WORDS.** Press *Email the receipt*. If the server answers that this
  receipt had already gone out, it also says whether the thank-you went with it —
  and it can say **no**. The screen prints *"Receipt + thank-you sent."* either
  way, because the sentence is chosen **before** the press and the server's
  answer is thrown away. A detailer is told a customer got a thank-you that the
  customer never got.

  **THE THREE LINES, read at this commit:**

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | the server says so | `supabase/functions/send-invoice/index.ts:96` — `{ success: true, duplicate: true, thank_you_sent: attempt.thankYouSent }` |
  | the record gets it | `app/src/components/BookingDetail.jsx:363` — `sendReceipt` returns `answer` |
  | and drops it | `BookingDetail.jsx:140` — `act` does `await fn()` and **discards the return value**; the notice is picked at the call site (`:926`–`:927`) from `sentReceipt ? "Receipt sent again." : "Receipt + thank-you sent."`, both decided before the call |

  **WHY IT IS NOT JUST A WORDING FIX.** The only thing that knows what happened
  is the answer, and no caller of `act` can see one. So the fix is `act`
  returning its answer, which touches every caller of it — **and the number
  usually quoted for that is wrong.** The comment at `BookingDetail.jsx:141`
  says *"all four callers route through"*; `grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z])act\('` on
  that file returns **seven**: `:178`, `:182`, `:197`, `:487`, `:532`, `:652`,
  `:926`. **A change scoped to four would leave three behind**, and the three it
  would leave are ordinary status writes whose notices are also chosen in
  advance.

  **AND THE SAME DISCARD HIDES ONE MORE THING, which is why this is worth doing
  once rather than twice.** `idempotent: false` (`send-invoice/index.ts:286`) is
  the server's only way of saying *this send was not deduplicated at all* —
  which is every send until the `send_invoice_attempts` migration is applied.
  Nothing in the product can read that either. 6.4's entry records it as a
  decision rather than unfinished work; this item is the mechanism both answers
  would need.

  **Done when:** **(a)** a `duplicate` answer whose `thank_you_sent` is false
  produces a notice that does **not** claim a thank-you — pressed on a real
  duplicate, not simulated; **(b)** `act` returns what its function returned,
  and **all seven** call sites still show the right notice, checked by pressing
  each one rather than by reading; **(c)** every new or changed English string
  has its Spanish key in `app/src/lib/strings/appEs.js` in the same edit — both
  current notices already have one (`appEs.js:1587`, `:1588`), so a third must
  too; and **(d)** no call site is left choosing its sentence before the answer
  arrives **where the answer could contradict it** — the ones that genuinely
  cannot fail may keep their fixed notice, said out loud per site rather than
  left to a reader to work out.

  **What failing looks like:** the notice fixed for the duplicate case and still
  wrong for `idempotent: false`; or `act` changed for the receipt button alone,
  which leaves six callers on the old shape and the next session unable to tell
  which convention a given call site follows.

  *Filed by DP Cowork2, 2026-10-08. No `app/src` touched. The finding is DP
  Cowork's; the line numbers and the seven-against-four count are this
  session's, read at the commit carrying this entry.*

## Wave 10 — Copy

One pass, one list. All of it is the same defect: internal voice reaching
production. `CLAUDE.md` § Design already forbids it; these are the live
instances.

**A COUPLING FOUND WHILE RUNNING THIS PASS, 2026-09-20 — read before renaming
anything.** Some of this product's own user-facing strings are load-bearing
for the instruments that measure it: the width sweep opens a sheet by its
**visible text**, not by a stable selector, so renaming "Log a bulk job" to
"Add a fleet job" (10.1, applied and correct) made that screen undiscoverable
by name and the sweep reported it `NEVER MEASURED`. That is the gate working
— it named the gap rather than going quiet — but it means a copy pass has to
be cross-checked against the browser instruments before it runs, not only
against this repo's own tests. A button label, a sheet title, a tab name or a
heading a script would plausibly click by text is the shape of string to
check; plain paragraph prose is not, because nothing clicks a sentence by its
words. **The fix belongs in the check, not in reverting the string** — give
the instrument a stable hook (`data-*`, a route, a component name) instead of
a wording it is free to keep changing. Full detail: `docs/gotchas.md`.

## Wave 14 — The health audit, 2026-09-16

Andrew's ask: *"an honest picture of whether this product's features actually
work or just look like they work — especially anything touching money,
payments, and one detailer being able to see another detailer's customers."*

Everything below was **measured against the development Supabase project**
(`kguqylyzgyzfktkfnhjb`), not read off a document. The live business project
was not touched. Where a measurement contradicts a document, the measurement
is written down and the document is named.

### What is genuinely solid — say this out loud, because it is most of it

Four separate defences, each one checked rather than assumed:

1. **One detailer cannot read another's customers through the browser.** 51
   tables, every one with row-level security **enabled and forced**. Swept all
   51 as a signed-in detailer: 48 answered, **zero foreign rows**, own rows
   visible in 12, and a canary proved 63 foreign customer rows existed to be
   leaked. See 4.4 above for the full receipt.
2. **A new table cannot be forgotten.** A database event trigger
   (`rls_auto_enable`) turns row-level security on and forces it on **every**
   table created in `public`, and a table with no policy is deny-all. That is
   why the count is 51 of 51 and not "51 of 51 so far".
3. **The back office has no shortcut into the policies.** The obvious build
   gives twenty tables an `or is_platform_admin()` escape hatch. **Zero
   policies mention it** — measured. The back office reads everything through
   one service-role function behind one `platform_admins` check instead, and
   the 404 it returns is the same for "not signed in" and "not an admin".
4. **Stored prices are correct.** Every one of the **57** bookings in the
   database reconciles: `total = subtotal − promo`, before or after the
   business's own rounding. **Zero breaks.** So A2 4.1's "the summary lines do
   not add up" (item 2.2) is about **what the customer is shown**, not about
   what is stored — fix the display, do not go looking for bad arithmetic.

The Stripe code is also careful in ways worth keeping: the amount is computed
server-side from the booking row and never taken from the browser; the webhook
verifies the signature over the raw body, refuses an event whose Stripe account
does not match the booking's connected account, and is idempotent on a unique
event id.

### 14.1 — A note the product calls "Private" is public

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-16 — the detailer's private note on a job went to anyone
  with the booking link.** The reply now carries **31 named keys instead of 66**
  and `admin_notes` is gone, measured anonymously with no API key before and
  after. Receipt `receipts/receipt-fields.json`, evidence
  `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 14.1, check `tests/receipt-fields.test.mjs` (broken on
  purpose three times first). Original report: `BookingDetail.jsx:475` prints `admin_notes` under the label
  **"Private:"**. `get-booking-receipt` is a public endpoint and selects `*`,
  so it hands the whole booking row to an anonymous caller.
  **Measured:** an anonymous GET with **no API key** returned `admin_notes` of
  `"staff note"` and `"phone booking"` — the exact strings in the database.
  It also returns `payment_notes`, `stripe_payment_intent`, `stripe_session_id`,
  `miles`, `vehicle_condition` and the internal `customer_id`, `business_id`,
  `campaign_id`, `plan_id` and `plan_member_id`.
  **Why it matters in plain words:** a detailer writes "customer was difficult,
  do not go back" in a box labelled Private, and the customer can read it.
  **Fix:** replace `select *` with a named list of the fields the receipt page
  actually draws. The function already does exactly this for
  `business_settings` — one setting exposed, the rest private — so copy that.
  **Done when:** the anonymous receipt contains no field the customer's own
  page does not render, and a test asserts the list rather than the absence.

### 14.2 — The calendar link's "owner" view has no password on it

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-16 — the calendar link's owner view had no password on
  it.** An anonymous caller with no apikey and no Authorization header who
  typed `&audience=owner` on their own confirmation link got the detailer's
  copy: `SUMMARY:Chris Vogel · Express Wash` and
  `Customer: Chris Vogel · 562-555-0447`. The same call now returns the
  **customer's** copy, line for line, measured against the deployed function
  before (v50) and after (v51). A signed-in member of that business still gets
  the private copy, and the customer's own link was never touched. The
  membership is checked against **this booking's** business, so one detailer
  cannot open another's job either. The dashboard's Calendar control had to
  stop being a link — an `<a href>` cannot send a session — so it fetches and
  hands over the file, same geometry, verified in the running app at 320, 392,
  768 and 1440 with no console errors. The endpoint also took the
  `publicCeiling` rate limit `pay-booking` has. Evidence `docs/VERIFIED.md`
  § 14.2, receipt `receipts/ics-audience.json`, check
  `tests/ics-audience.test.mjs` (broken on purpose four times first, including
  once against the real unfixed deployment). Original report:
  `booking-ics?audience=owner` is unauthenticated. `audience` is a
  plain query word. Anyone who edits it on their own confirmation link gets the
  owner's copy.
  **Measured live, anonymous, no key and no token:** name `Chris Vogel`, phone
  `562-555-0447`, address `5 Anchor Ct, San Pedro, CA`, vehicle `BMW 3 Series`.
  The customer's own version of the same link does **not** contain the phone,
  which is the point — the two views differ and nothing enforces the boundary.
  **Not a cross-tenant hole:** a random UUID answers 404 and ids are random, so
  nobody can walk the list. It is the one link, in the one inbox, that flips.
  **Fix:** the owner's view needs the owner's session, the same way every other
  owner surface does. The customer's link keeps working untouched.
  **Also:** this endpoint has **no rate limit**, unlike `pay-booking`.
  **Done when:** `audience=owner` without a member session returns the customer
  view or 404, and a test tries the flip and is refused. **Closes 4.2.**

### 14.3 — Nothing anywhere records that an email was sent

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-16 — every email the product sends now leaves a row, and
  the row says what became of it.** One `email_sends` row per attempted send,
  written by `send-email` on **all six of its exits** — including the three
  that used to be a `console.warn` or a `console.error` and nothing else — and
  updated by a new `resend-webhook` when the provider reports what happened.
  Proved on the deployed functions by invoicing a real demo booking three
  times: the platform's own send counter moved by **4** and **6** rows were
  written (the two extra are the sends that never reached the provider, which
  is the half that was silent). Then six signed webhook events: a delivery and
  a bounce each found their row, a forgery was refused **400**, a genuine
  signature six minutes old was refused **400**, an unmodelled event type was
  acknowledged, and a late `delivered` could **not** un-bounce a bounced row.
  It is drawn on the client record under **Emails** — subject, date, and
  *Delivered* / *On its way* / *Bounced* / *Not sent* with the provider's own
  reason. Verified at 1920, 1440, 768, 392 and 320 with no clipping, no
  sideways scroll and no new console errors. **The message body is not stored**
  — the migration says why. An asynchronous bounce now also raises the
  *"this address bounced"* banner that has existed since 2.20 and could only
  ever see a synchronous refusal. Evidence `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 14.3, receipt
  `receipts/email-sends.json`, checks `tests/email-sends.test.mjs` and
  `tests/svix-signature.test.mjs` (broken on purpose four times first,
  including twice against the real deployment). **Andrew has one three-minute
  job before the delivery half works in production** — `FOR-ANDREW.md`.
  Original report: there is no per-message record of any kind. Measured: no table in the
  database holds a sent email. `platform_email_days` is a daily counter for the
  quota and nothing else. `send-email` receives Resend's message id and
  **returns it to its caller without storing it**; a provider failure goes to
  `console.error`, which is a function log nobody watches and which expires.
  The only trace is a timestamp on the booking saying *we called Resend*, which
  is not the same as *it arrived*.
  **Why it matters:** a customer says "I never got the confirmation" and there
  is no way to answer. This is the mechanism behind 3.1 and it is worse than
  3.1 describes — 3.1 says the owner cannot tell; in fact **nobody** can.
  **Fix:** one `email_sends` row per send — business, booking, kind, to,
  provider id, result. Then Resend's delivery webhook on top of it.
  **Done when:** every email the product sends leaves a row, and a failed send
  is visible on a screen rather than in a log. *Extends 3.1.*

### 14.4 — A paid booking can be cancelled and nobody is told about the money

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-17 — a paid booking could be cancelled and nobody was told
  about the money.** A confirmed booking already marked paid, worth **$195**,
  was cancelled by an anonymous caller with no key of any kind and the deployed
  endpoint answered `{"success":true,"booking":{"status":"cancelled"}}` — not a
  word about the money. The same call now also answers
  `"refund":{"owed":true,"message":"You paid for this booking. Coastline Auto
  Detailing will arrange your refund directly — call 562-555-0180…"}`, and the
  **detailer** gets *"This was paid. Refund $195 from your own Stripe — the
  money went straight into your account, so we cannot send it back for you."*
  in their cancellation email and on the job. Measured against the deployed
  function before (v65) and after (v68), with an unpaid booking as the control
  answering `owed:false`.
  **The cancellation still goes ahead** — the roadmap's second option, and
  `_shared/connect.ts`'s own reasoning: a refund on a connected account is the
  detailer's to make from their own balance, so the product says so rather than
  blocking the customer. Nothing was refunded and nothing reached into the
  detailer's Stripe.
  **THERE ARE THREE CANCEL PATHS, NOT TWO.** `update-booking` carries `status`
  in its allowlist, so the detailer's own **Cancel the job** button is a third
  writer beside `cancel-booking` and `respond-to-booking`'s decline. And the
  decline branch really is reachable with money on it — `payability()` refuses
  to charge a pending request, but `update-booking` also allows setting
  `payment_status` by hand with no status guard, which is cash taken up front.
  Two of the three send the detailer no email, so the instruction is drawn off
  the ROW on the job screen and covers all three.
  Verified at 1920, 1440, 768, 392 and 320 and with `?lite=1`, nothing clipped,
  no sideways scroll, contrast 4.95:1, no console errors. Evidence
  `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 14.4, receipt `receipts/cancelled-refund.json`,
  artifacts `artifacts/cancelled-refund/`, check
  `tests/cancelled-refund.test.mjs` (broken on purpose **seven** times first,
  including once against the real unfixed deployment and once by blinding its
  own comparator). **Not done, deliberately:** a customer reopening the
  cancelled link later is told nothing — the public receipt does not carry
  `payment_status` and 14.1 narrowed it on purpose. Original report:
  `cancel-booking` does not mention money at all. Measured: the file
  contains no `payment_status`, no `refund`, no `paid`, no `stripe`. A booking
  that is `confirmed` and already `paid` — **one exists in the database right
  now** — can be cancelled by the customer from their own link, outside the
  cancellation window, and nothing refunds it, flags it, or tells the detailer
  that money is sitting in their account for work that will not happen.
  **The design intent is defensible** — `_shared/connect.ts` says a refund on a
  connected account is the detailer's to make, in their own Stripe. **The
  product never says so to anybody.**
  **Fix:** refuse online self-cancellation of a paid booking and say to call,
  or allow it and put "This was paid. Refund $X in Stripe." in front of the
  detailer, in the email and on the job.
  **Done when:** cancelling a paid booking produces a visible instruction to
  somebody, and a test proves it.

### 14.5 — Every money path is proved only by arithmetic, never by money moving

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-17 — a payment has now actually settled.** A $195 test
  booking was paid with Stripe's `4242` card on the hosted checkout page that
  `pay-booking` produced, on the detailer's own connected account
  (`acct_1UCMp1JeoZ7g84se`, test mode). Stripe delivered
  `payment_intent.succeeded` and `checkout.session.completed` to the deployed
  webhook, which marked the booking `paid` with `pi_3UGa9SJeoZ7g84se1Torfagi`
  one second later, and the **Money screen's "waiting on payment" fell from
  $490 to $295** — seen on the screen, not only in its query. Before this the
  development database held **zero** connected accounts, **zero** bookings with
  a checkout session and **zero** with a payment intent.
  **Four things were found that no document here knew:** the Connect webhook is
  live and `docs/OUTSTANDING.md` § 13 still says it is not; Stripe's *"use
  blank test account"* shortcut yields an account that can never charge, which
  makes the product look broken when it is not; Checkout opens on Link's phone
  step so the card fields are absent from the page entirely, and Stripe reports
  that as *"Payment method Required"*, which reads exactly like a decline; and
  `pay-booking`'s idempotency key makes a naive re-run impossible for 24 hours.
  Check `scripts/e2e-payment.mjs` — 6 targets, 22 assertions, receipt
  `receipts/e2e-payment.json`, artifacts `artifacts/e2e-payment/`, **broken on
  purpose seven times**, and **two of those sabotages passed, which was a
  defect in the check** — both only loosened an assertion that was already
  satisfied. They were replaced, and the assertion they exposed was rewritten.
  Evidence `docs/VERIFIED.md` § 14.5.
  **Not done, deliberately:** the connected account was attached by writing the
  row rather than through OAuth — the handshake itself was run end to end the
  same morning and works, but it yields the blank account above. Stripe's own
  `refresh` set `charges_enabled`, so that value is measured and not typed in.
  Nothing was refunded and no payout was checked. Original report:

  **566 money assertions pass and not one of them touches a network.**
  Measured by counting `fetch(` in each suite: `connect.test.mjs` 126 checks,
  `payments.test.mjs` 83, `platform-billing.test.mjs` 357 — **zero network
  calls between them.** They import the decision functions and test them
  directly, which is genuinely good work: `payability`, `amountDueCents`,
  `cardStatus` and `verifyWebhook` are all real and all correct.
  **But nothing in this repo has ever proved that a payment settles.** No test
  creates a Stripe checkout session, no test delivers a webhook to the deployed
  endpoint, no test watches a booking go from owed to paid.
  **This is the exact shape `docs/how-we-run.md` warns about**: green beside a
  thing that has never happened.
  **Fix:** one end-to-end run in Stripe's sandbox — connect a test account,
  pay a test booking with a test card, let the real webhook mark it paid, then

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-17 — the contradiction is settled and the words are

  accountant CSV all count work done in the period, so a cash-basis headline

  **So 5.1 wins on the labels, the comment wins on the maths** — 14.7's own
  recommendation. The comment block is rewritten to say so rather than left
  contradicting the fix.

  **RE-MEASURED AND IT HAD MOVED: $295, not $230.** All time on the demo
  business: earned $4,745, collected $4,450, owed $295, expenses $1,102, so
  the screen read $3,643 against a cash position of $3,348. The extra $65 is
  **ROADMAP 14.5's own canary booking**, `pending`, dated 2026-09-11, left in
  place and flagged per 0.3. The check therefore asserts the IDENTITY —
  accrual net minus cash equals what is owed — not a dollar amount.

  `revenueIn`, expense filter, net, average job and quoted/added split, all of
  which `moneyAdvanced.js` already computed from the same rows for the advanced
  screen — 14.6a's defect with a new subject. They had begun to differ already:
  one hardens amounts with `num()`, the other used a bare `Number()` that turns
  the whole figure into `NaN`. **Worse, `moneyAdvanced.js` returned the accrual
  total under the name `collected` and the cash total under `collectedPaid`**,
  while `Today.jsx` uses `collected` for cash — so adding 5.1's *Collected*
  cell the obvious way would have shipped the overstatement under the one label
  that promises it cannot. Now `earned` / `collected` / `owed`, and every figure
  on both money screens plus the chart comes from one `advancedMoney()` call.

  *Earned* / *Expenses* / *Avg job* / *Jobs done*, then **Collected $515 and
  Still owed $295** beneath them. The back office says *earned*, not *taken*.
  Nine Spanish keys replaced eight in the same edit.

  **5.1's *Expenses paid* WAS REFUSED, ON PURPOSE.** An expense row has no
  paid/unpaid column, so that label would be a new unverifiable claim replacing
  an honest one. It stays *Expenses*.

  **5.1's DONE-WHEN WAS PRESSED, NOT ASSUMED.** *Mark paid* on the $65 job, in
