  Restored after each; the render is byte-identical to the clean snapshot and
  the run still takes **0.53s**, credential-free.

  ---

  **The original entry, unchanged, from here down.**

  **Found 2026-09-23 by pressing 8.10a's feature end to end instead of
  re-reading its entry.** 8.10a is correctly closed: both migrations are live,
  `get_public_business_profile` publishes `max_vehicles_per_booking`, and a
  real two-car booking goes through. **This is what pressing it found on the
  way past.**

  **THE MEASUREMENT, from a booking made through the real `create-booking` on
  a throwaway tenant.** One service at $100, medium vehicle, one extra small
  vehicle:

  | | one car | two cars |
  |---|---|---|
  | `total_price` | 115 | **215** ✔ |
  | itemised lines | 115 | service 115 + 2nd vehicle 100 = **215** ✔ |
  | **`subtotal`** | **115** ✔ | **315** ✘ |

  **The total is right and the itemisation is right. `subtotal` alone is wrong,
  by exactly the price of the extra car** — the second vehicle is inside the
  subtotal *and* listed again as a `price_adjustments` line
  (`{"label":"2nd vehicle · Small · Second Car","amount":100,"source":"vehicle"}`).
  `pricing.ts:655` is where the two meet: `subtotalBase = beforeAdjustments +
  adjustmentsTotal`, and on this path the extra vehicle is already in
  `beforeAdjustments`.

  **One car is clean**, so this is specific to the multi-vehicle path.

  **WHY NOBODY HAS SEEN IT, AND WHY THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART.** Multi-car
  booking was **unreachable for every tenant until 2026-09-21** — that is
  8.10a's whole finding. **No real two-car booking has ever existed**, so no
  receipt, invoice or screen has ever had to add these numbers up. The feature
  shipped, was unreachable, was made reachable, and **the first end-to-end
  press of it found a money fault in the same hour.**

  **WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS READ, kept apart.**
  - **Measured:** the stored row and `get-booking-receipt`'s response both
    carry `subtotal: 315` against `total_price: 215` with lines summing to 215.
  - **NOW MEASURED TOO — the email was rendered, 2026-09-23.** See the verdict
    below. The earlier reading was right that the base comes out at $215 and
    wrong about what happens next, which is worse than it guessed.

  ---

  #### THE VERDICT: THE STORED COLUMN IS THE BUG, AND THE TEMPLATE HIDES IT BY INVENTING A DISCOUNT

  **Settled by rendering the real `customerConfirmationEmail` with the real
  numbers, twice — once with the subtotal the product stored and once with what
  the template's own contract expects.** The template's contract is written in
  its own comment: *"`subtotal` already contains travel and every surcharge
  (2.8c), so the named services cannot simply be summed."* Under that contract
  a two-car booking with no discounts should store `subtotal = 215`, the same
  as the total.

  **What the customer's email says with the subtotal the product actually
  stored (315):**

  ```
  shape service                      $215
  2nd vehicle · Small · Second Car   $100
  Discount applied                  -$100
  Estimated total                    $215
  ```

  **What it says with the correct subtotal (215):**

  ```
  shape service                      $115
  2nd vehicle · Small · Second Car   $100
  Estimated total                    $215
  ```

  **SO: THE TEMPLATE IS FAITHFUL AND THE STORED COLUMN IS WRONG.** The fix
  belongs in the pricing engine, **not** in `emailTemplates.ts`. Nothing about
  the template needs to change.

  **AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FAULT.** The email **balances**.
  $215 − $100 + $100 = $215, so **every money-column check in this repo passes
  on it** — including `render-emails.mjs`'s own assertion that *"every money
  column reaches its own printed total"*. The arithmetic is self-consistent and
  **the story is fiction**: the customer is shown a $215 service they were
  never quoted and told they received a **$100 discount that does not exist**.

  **A wrong number that still adds up is invisible to every check that only
  asks whether it adds up.** That is this repo's oldest shape, arriving in the
  one place where the reader is a paying customer rather than a session.

  **THIS IS 2.2's CLASS, NOT 2.2's MECHANISM.** 2.2 — *"the summary lines do
  not add up to the total"*, closed 2026-09-20 — was **rounding**. This is
  **double counting**, on a path 2.2 could not have exercised because the
  feature was unreachable when 2.2 was fixed. The rule 2.2 established is the
  one being broken.

  **Done when:** a two-car booking stores `subtotal` equal to its own total
  when there are no discounts, the rendered email shows the service at $115
  and **no `Discount applied` line at all**, and a one-car booking is
  unchanged at 115/115. **The template is not to be touched.**

  **Not fixed here.** It is a money path, `_shared/pricing.ts` is imported by
  seven functions, and changing it needs its own item rather than a
  same-session repair at the end of a long night. **And it reaches no customer
  today:** there are no real detailers, and the deployed `calculate-booking`
  is one of the 14 functions behind this checkout, so this is a fault waiting
  at the same door as everything else on `FOR-ANDREW.md`'s publish row.

### 14.20 — ~~`tests/mail-sink.test.mjs` is RED over 40 addresses~~ DONE 2026-09-24. 39 were a credential or a word in a comment; the fortieth was a real leak

- [x] **DONE 2026-09-24. Inherited, not caused, 2026-09-23.** Found while running the mail
  guard after 14.19's work; confirmed red at `HEAD` before that session
  touched anything (`git stash -u`, re-run, same 12 passed / 1 failed).

  **THIS ENTRY HAS BEEN WRONG TWICE AND BOTH VERSIONS ARE KEPT, BECAUSE THE
  SECOND MISTAKE IS THE SAME SHAPE AS 14.19 AND WAS MADE BY THE SESSION THAT
  HAD JUST FIXED 14.19.**

  **Wrong the first time:** reported upward as *"40 undeclared addresses in
  `tests/email-sends.test.mjs`"*. **Eight are in that file.** Corrected
  unprompted the next turn.

  **Wrong the second time, and this is the one worth reading.** The corrected
  version said *"31 of the 40 are on `@detailplatform.com`, and that domain is
  charged — so those call sites can spend Andrew's 80 sends a day."* The probe
  quoted was real. **The conclusion was not, and `tests/_mail.mjs` disproves
  it three lines below the line that was quoted:**

  > *"A fixture LOGIN on a deliverable domain is therefore not a spender; a
  > fixture RECIPIENT is."*

  **A quote was lifted and the sentence underneath it that disqualified the
  conclusion was not read.** That is 14.19's own failure — reading the figure
  and not the meaning — committed while writing up 14.19.

  **WHAT THE 40 ACTUALLY ARE, classified by opening each one:**
  - **25 are `demo@detailplatform.com` sign-ins** — `page.fill("input[type=
    email]", …)` and `const OWNER = { email, password }`. The demo owner's
    login, live-confirmed all over this repo. **`mailer_autoconfirm` is true
    and no custom SMTP is set, so a fixture login sends nothing at all.**
    Cost: zero.
  - **14 are addresses written inside COMMENTS**, most of them prose
    explaining why that address is safe — `dashboard-notifies.mjs:91` is
    literally inside a block headed *"NOTHING REACHES A PERSON"*, and
    `edge-tenant-replay.mjs:929` is a comment about a recipient the function
    takes from an env var. Cost: zero. They are not call sites.
  - **That leaves at most one** worth a human's attention, and it was not
    confirmed as a live send either.

  **AND `detailplatform.com` IS NOT A TYPO.** It reads like one — this
  product is `detailingplatform.com`, six characters longer — and that
  resemblance is worth knowing. But it is the **established demo credential
  domain**, named in `admin-account.mjs`, ROADMAP 0.1, 9.16 and
  `platform_admins`, and confirmed live. Calling it a slip in this entry
  would have put a second wrong fact where the first one had just been
  removed.

  **SO THE DEFECT IS IN THE GUARD, NOT IN 40 CALL SITES.**
  `tests/mail-sink.test.mjs:101-112` reads every file in `tests/` and
  `scripts/` **line by line as raw text**, matches any `@domain`, and asks
  only whether the domain is reserved. It does not strip comments and it
  cannot tell a recipient from a login. So it reports 40 findings of which
  **at least 39 cost nothing**, which is worse than reporting none:

  > **A guard that cries 40 is a guard nobody reads, and the day a real
  > undeclared recipient appears it will be item 41 in a list everybody has
  > learned to walk past.**

  It is the same class as the checks 14.19 got past — **a check measuring the
  thing that is easy to measure rather than the thing that matters.** Here it
  is inverted: 14.19's checks were silent when they should have shouted; this
  one shouts constantly, which buys the same silence.

  **What the fix looks like:** strip comments before matching, and classify
  by role — an address passed to something that SENDS is a recipient; an
  address typed into a password form or held in an `OWNER`/`ADMIN` constant
  is a login and is free. `tests/_mail.mjs` already exports both halves,
  `sink("tag")` and `realMail(address, reason)`, and `realMail` prints every
  time it is called. **Not a blanket replace of 40 strings** — that would
  silence a guard instead of repairing it, and would rewrite 25 working
  logins to fix nothing.

  **NOT EDITED TONIGHT** because six of the flagged files were another
  session's (`contrast-insitu`, `scroller-clearance`, `tabbar-clearance`,
  `calendar-legible` and two more), and `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that
  `scripts/` is watched by nothing at all, so an unannounced edit there is
  the quiet collision.

  **Done when:** the guard reports only addresses that can actually cause a
  send; `node --test tests/mail-sink.test.mjs` exits 0; **and it is broken on
  purpose twice** — a genuine undeclared recipient added (it must fail) and a
  login left as it is (it must pass). A guard whose fix is "stop reporting
  things" has to prove it still reports the one thing it is for.

  ---

  #### BUILT 2026-09-24. THE GUARD IS FIXED, 40 → 2, AND BOTH SURVIVORS ARE TRUE

  **The fix is the one this entry prescribed, and no call site was blanket
  replaced.** `tests/mail-sink.test.mjs` now does two things it did not:

  **1 · IT STRIPS COMMENTS IN PLACE.** `codeOnly()` replaces every comment
  character with a space and keeps every newline, so the text keeps its exact
  length, its exact columns and its exact line numbers — **a finding still
  points where it pointed.** Same shape as the stripper
  `scripts/setup-inputs-contract.mjs` grew on 2026-09-23 for the same reason,
  copied rather than shared because a test importing from a script another
  session owns is the quiet collision. **The invariant is asserted, not
  trusted** (`2b-z`): a stripper that quietly ate code would move real
  recipients into the free bucket and nothing would say so.

  **2 · IT CLASSIFIES BY ROLE, AND THE DEFAULT IS "RECIPIENT".**

  | role | rule | free? |
  |---|---|---|
  | COMMENT | the address is not in the code at all | yes |
  | LOGIN | `password`/`secret` within one line of it | yes |
  | READ | `=== "addr"` / `!== "addr"` — a comparison reads a row back | yes |
  | DECLARED | `realMail(...)` or a `mail-sink: why` comment | yes |
  | **RECIPIENT** | **everything else** | **no — reported** |

  **The unknown case is "recipient", deliberately.** A guard whose default is
  "free" gets narrower every time somebody writes something new.

  **THE LOGIN RULE IS PROXIMITY, NOT A PARSE, AND THE CEILING IS NAMED IN THE
  FILE.** A genuine recipient written within one line of the word "password"
  would be freed. That was accepted over a per-file allowlist, which is the
  thing that file's own header spends a paragraph refusing. The upgrade, if it
  ever bites, is to require the address and the password to be arguments of the
  same call. **`password` is not `\b`-anchored** because `_` is a word
  character, so `\bsecret\b` misses `DEMO_SECRET`, which is how two files write
  it.

  **WHAT THE 237 OCCURRENCES ACTUALLY ARE — measured, not estimated.** `seen`
  is unchanged at 237, because classification happens on the RAW match and the
  stripped copy is only asked *"is this in the code?"* — nothing is discarded,
  so nothing can go missing silently.

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | free by reserved domain | 168 | 168 |
  | inside a comment | — | **18** |
  | fixture login | — | **24** |
  | read back by `===` | — | **2** |
  | declared | 29 | 23 |
  | **undeclared** | **40** | **2** |

  *`declared` fell from 29 to 23 because six of them are now recognised earlier,
  by role, and no longer need a declaration at all.*

  **TWO CALL SITES WERE DECLARED, AND THEY ARE REAL SENDS.**
  `tests/email-sends.test.mjs` invoices a finalised demo booking at
  `delivered@resend.dev` and `bounced@resend.dev`; **`resend.dev` is a real

  **BROKEN ON PURPOSE FOUR WAYS, ON EVERY RUN, NOT ONCE.** § 2a runs four

  flags everything are the same useless thing, and those four lines prove it is

  **AND BROKEN ON PURPOSE AGAINST THE REAL REPO, four times, 2026-09-24:**
  - a genuinely undeclared recipient planted in a new `tests/` file — **caught,

  - a line comment and a **multi-line block comment** — not flagged, the comment

  - two logins, one with `password` on the same line and one with `SECRET` two

  The sabotage file was deleted and the run returned to 168 files, 237

  **`node --test tests/mail-sink.test.mjs`: 20 passed, 1 failed.** The four

  **NOT EXIT 0, AND THE TWO THINGS THAT BLOCK IT ARE IN `scripts/`, WHICH THIS

  *Done when*, SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN QUIETLY PICKED.** *Done when* asks for

### 14.21 — A teardown written AFTER `browser.close()` instead of inside a `finally` leaves a full platform admin behind on a crash — DONE 2026-10-06

- [x] **Found 2026-09-25 by the ticked-item audit, in 6.2a's own words. Not
  built here: it lives in `scripts/`, which was another session's lane.**

  **THE PATTERN, WHICH IS THE PART THAT TRAVELS — read this before the line
  number.** A script that needs the back office mints a throwaway platform
  admin, does its work, and drops the row again. **If the drop is written as a
  top-level statement after `await browser.close()`, it runs on a clean exit
  and on nothing else.** A throw anywhere above it — a selector that stopped
  matching, a page that did not load, a `process.exit` on a failure — skips it,
  **and what is left behind is not a stray fixture row. It is an account that
  reads every detailer, every customer, and can suspend, impersonate and
  reprice.** `public.platform_admins` has four columns and not one of them is a
  permission, so every row is all-or-nothing (14.8).

  **It has already happened twice, on the same night, in the same way.** 6.2a
  records that `scripts/health-line-honest.mjs` had exactly this shape and **two
  crashed runs each left a live row**, caught within the hour by
  `tests/platform-admins-declared.test.mjs` — which correctly refused to
  allowlist them. **It is a defect that only fires when a run goes wrong, which
  is when nobody is reading the output.**

  **THE POPULATION IS THREE SCRIPTS AND ONE OF THEM IS WRONG — counted, not
  assumed.** Everything that mints one goes through `makeAdmin`/`dropAdmin` in
  `scripts/admin-account.mjs`:

  | script | where the teardown sits | verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | `scripts/shoot-admin.mjs` | inside a `finally` | **safe** — it was suspected during 6.2a and is innocent |
  | `scripts/health-line-honest.mjs` | inside a `finally`, with `--crash-after-signin` to prove it | **safe, and it is the worked example to copy** |
  | **`scripts/admin-contrast.mjs`** | **top-level, after `browser.close()`, with a second inline close-then-drop on an earlier exit path** | **UNGUARDED** |

  `scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs` no longer mints one at all — 4.5 removed that
  path deliberately when the standing demo login turned out to reach `/admin` —
  so it is not in this population. **Three minters, one hole.**

  **THE FILE ALREADY KNOWS.** `admin-contrast.mjs` carries a `ponytail:`
  comment admitting it, and the comment above that one explains why the drop
  was moved ABOVE the failure exits — which was a real improvement and is not
  the same thing as a `finally`. **Fixing the ordering of the exits does not fix
  a throw**, and the comment says so itself: *"Wrap the whole script if that
  ever stops being true, which it will the day something else reads that row."*
  Something else does read that row now: the declared-admins check, which went
  red on exactly this twice.

  **Fix:** put the browser section in `try { … } finally { await
  browser.close(); await dropAdmin(…); }`, the shape
  `health-line-honest.mjs` already uses, and delete the inline close-then-drop
  on the early exit path so there is one teardown rather than two.

  **A `finally` IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT — CORRECTED 2026-10-03, and the
  correction is worth more than the item.** The fix above says *put the teardown
  in a `finally`*, and that is right as far as it goes. **It does not go far
  enough: a `finally` does not run on a SIGNAL.** `timeout` sends SIGTERM, Node's
  default handler exits, and the block is skipped exactly as `process.exit()`
  skips it. **Measured the hard way the same night this item was written:**
  `scripts/restore-drill.mjs` has its teardown in a textbook `finally`
  (`:430`), was run under `timeout 110`, and **left a 51-table `restore_drill`
  schema in `kguqylyzgyzfktkfnhjb`.** `docs/gotchas.md` 90. **So this item's own
  original criterion would have passed a script that still leaks on the most
  ordinary way a session stops one.**

  **Done when — THREE exits, not one, and the signal is the one that was
  missing:**
  1. **Clean exit** — a normal run leaves `public.platform_admins` with the same
     rows it started with.
  2. **Crash** — `node scripts/admin-contrast.mjs --crash-after-signin`, a flag
     that has to be added, throwing at the same point the two real crashes threw,
     **after the sign-in and before the screenshots**, leaves the same rows.
  3. **SIGNAL** — the same run interrupted with **SIGTERM** (`timeout 20 node
     scripts/admin-contrast.mjs`, or `kill` on its pid) **also** leaves the same
     rows. **This is the clause a `finally` alone does not satisfy**, and closing
     it needs an explicit `process.on("SIGINT"|"SIGTERM")` teardown, not a
     bigger `try`.

  In every one of the three the table is read **immediately before the run and
  immediately after it, both readings printed by the run**, and
  `node --test tests/platform-admins-declared.test.mjs` **passes with zero
  failures** afterwards with no edit to `docs/platform-admins.md`. **Its
  assertion count is read off the run, not quoted here.**
  **What failing looks like:** two of three green and the third never attempted,
  because **the signal case is the only one nobody reaches by accident** — a
  crash happens to you, a clean exit is the happy path, and a SIGTERM arrives
  only when somebody gets impatient, which is precisely when nobody is reading
  the output.
  ***COLD READ 2026-10-02, ON THIS ENTRY'S OWN CRITERION, WRITTEN HOURS EARLIER
  BY THE SAME SESSION.*** Two faults. It said **"18 passed / 0 failed"** — **a
  typed count of the thing being measured**, so adding one assertion to that test
  makes this criterion unmeetable, which is **exactly the fault diagnosed in 3.4
  the same day.** And it said *"read off the table in both directions"*, where
  "both directions" in this repo means **a sabotage proved two ways**, not
  before-and-after — so the phrase said something other than what was meant.

  **What failing looks like:** the table gains a row named something like
  `contrast-admin@…` that nobody declared, the declared-admins check goes red,
  and the only way to make it green is to delete the row by hand — which is the
  state this item exists to make impossible rather than merely detectable.

  ***BUILT AND RUN 2026-10-06 (Lane B, on the manager's go and under the throwaway-admin ruling): TWO OF THE THREE EXITS ARE
  PROVED, THE SIGNAL EXIT IS NOT, AND THIS ITEM STAYS OPEN.***
  **Lane exception, recorded:** `scripts/admin-contrast.mjs` (the item's own file) and one line of `scripts/admin-account.mjs`.
  **What was built.** The whole run is inside `try { … } catch { crashed = e } finally { await teardown() }`, one teardown
  instead of two, no `process.exit` inside the try; `--crash-after-signin` throws after the sign-in and the tab list, before the
  screenshots; `process.on(SIGINT | SIGTERM | SIGBREAK)` runs the same teardown; `--drop-leftover` removes the account by its
  address. **The ruling, as built:** the account is flagged as a test account twice (address
  `admin-contrast-test@detailplatform.com`, and the row's note now starts `TEST ACCOUNT`), removed at the end of every path,
  and its password is random per run, held in memory, never printed or written, and redacted from any error text. The table is
  read **by email only** (the note column has held a password) before the account exists and after it is gone, and both
  readings are printed.
  **Clean exit, run:** `node scripts/admin-contrast.mjs` printed `platform_admins BEFORE: ["demo@demo.com","demo@detailplatform.com"]`
  and, after, the same two, then `clear of the floor`, exit 0. **Crash, run:** `--crash-after-signin` printed the same BEFORE
  and AFTER and `deliberate crash, proving the teardown runs`, exit 1, and the log holds no password. **`node
  tests/platform-admins-declared.test.mjs`: 18 passed, 0 failed, declared 2, in the table 2, undeclared 0, missing 0**, with no
  edit to `docs/platform-admins.md`. `node --test tests/admin-contrast-teardown.test.mjs` (8 pass, browser-free, in-process
  sabotage of each exit) holds the structure, and runs `--drop-leftover` against a fake backend that returns the note column
  if anyone asks for it, to prove the roster read never does.
  **THE SIGNAL EXIT, WHERE I COULD NOT PROVE THE CLAIM.** `timeout N node scripts/admin-contrast.mjs` (Git Bash, N = 6 to 11,
  more than ten interruptions after the sign-in, some of them the controls below) left `platform_admins` as it was **every time**, and no auth user behind. **That is not
  evidence for the handlers, and three controls say so:** (1) the same interruption of a copy **with the handlers removed**
  also came back clean (the table showed the row at five successive polls and gone within a second of the kill); (2) a marker written
  **synchronously at the top of the handler** never appeared, so the handler did not run; (3) the process wrote nothing at
  all after being signalled, not the AFTER reading and not the teardown's own marker. Something removed the row about a second
  after the process died, and **I did not find what**; it is not in this script. **A genuine hard kill does leave it:** a
  minting process stopped with `Stop-Process -Force` left the row and the auth user for a full 20 seconds of polling, and
  `--drop-leftover` removed them (that run's row is gone; the table is the declared two). So on Windows the handlers are
  unproven, `timeout` is not a faithful SIGTERM, and **the sentence the item asks for, that a SIGTERM leaves the same
  rows, is true of the `timeout` runs and unexplained**.
  **Order, found on the way:** the first signalled run left the auth user behind (the row had gone, the user had not), because
  the browser was closed before the account was dropped. The teardown now drops the account first, reads the table and prints
  it, and closes the browser last.
  **What would close it:** an interruption that Node actually receives as a signal and a way to see what removes the row (the
  Management API's logs for `platform_admins` deletes around a kill would name it), or the manager accepting the `timeout`
  runs plus `--drop-leftover` as the standard. **Not ticked either way until one of those.**

  ***TICKED 2026-10-06, ON THE MANAGER'S RULING (DP Cowork2, Lane B): THE CLEAN AND CRASH PROOFS PLUS `--drop-leftover` ARE THE
  STANDARD.*** The manager took the second of the two ways out. **What that does and does not say:** the clean exit and the
  crash exit are proved in a browser, the table read by email before and after, `platform-admins-declared` 18 passed, 0
  failed; `--drop-leftover` removes a row a hard kill leaves behind, proved by a real `Stop-Process -Force` kill. **What is
  still not proved, and is not claimed:** that the signal handlers are what removed the row in the `timeout` runs. The three
  controls above still stand (a copy with the handlers removed came back clean too, and the handler's marker never fired), so
  on Windows the SIGINT/SIGTERM clause is **accepted as covered by `--drop-leftover`, not demonstrated for the handlers.** The
  third done-when sentence was relaxed by ruling rather than met; a session that finds out what removed the row (the Management
  API's logs for `platform_admins` deletes around a kill) can reopen it with that, and nothing here forbids it.

  **DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY DECLARING THE ROW.** 14.8's rule: a check that absorbs
  whatever it finds is worthless, and the roster is read by the check and never
  the reverse.

  **Cost:** one `try`/`finally`, one flag, one run. No migration, no deploy, no
  browser session a person has to watch — the crash flag does the watching.

### 14.22 — `Clients.jsx` writes two words in bare English thirty-three lines below the line that translates the same two words

- [x] **Found 2026-09-25 by the ticked-item audit, named inside 9.6's own entry
  as "worth its own line, not folded into this commit", and verified still
  present. Not built here: `app/src`.**

  **BOTH LINES, SO THE CONTRADICTION IS ON ONE SCREEN RATHER THAN REDISCOVERED.**

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | `app/src/screens/Clients.jsx:709` | `{owner ? t("lifetime") : (visits === 1 ? t("visit") : t("visits"))}` |
  | **`app/src/screens/Clients.jsx:742`** | **`{facts.visits === 1 ? "visit" : "visits"}`** |

  **The same two words, the same screen, thirty-three rows apart, one wrapped in
  `t()` and one not.** 709 is the client LIST row, added by 9.6. 742 is the
  client RECORD card, which predates it. A detailer using the product in Spanish
  reads `visita`/`visitas` in the list and then **`visit`/`visits`** when they
  open somebody.

  **WHY IT SURVIVED, AND IT IS THE SAME REASON EVERY TIME.** `appEs.js` is keyed
  on the English text, so an unwrapped string does not fail — **there is nothing
  to look up, so there is nothing to miss.** No error, no console line, no red
  test. `CLAUDE.md` names this exact mechanism for RENAMED strings; this is its
  other half, a string that was never wrapped at all.

  **Fix:** wrap 742 the way 709 already is. **Check the keys exist before
  assuming** — 9.6 records that `"visit"`/`"visits"` had no bare key until it
  added them, and that `"lifetime"` already did and was reused rather than
  duplicated. If the keys are there, this is one line.

  **Done when:** **no bare `"visit"`/`"visits"` string literal remains in
  `app/src/screens/Clients.jsx`**, proved by a command whose OUTPUT decides:

  ```bash
  grep -oE '.{2}"visits?"' app/src/screens/Clients.jsx | grep -v '^t('   # must print NOTHING
  ```

  **— and the client record card is opened on the demo tenant with the language
  set to Spanish and reads `visita` or `visitas`**, read off the screen, not off
  the catalogue.

  ***THE COMMAND CHANGED ON 2026-10-03 BECAUSE THE OLD ONE WAS RUN AND COULD NOT
  TELL A PASS FROM A FAIL.*** It was `grep -n '"visits?"' …` *"returns only
  occurrences inside a `t(` call"*. **Executed against today's file it prints
  lines 709 and 742. Executed against a copy with 742 fixed it prints lines 709
  and 742.** Byte-identical two-line output either side of the fix, because
  `grep -n` prints LINES and the question is about OCCURRENCES — and one line can
  hold a wrapped and an unwrapped one. **The reader had to eyeball, so it was a
  prompt to look rather than a gate.** The replacement prints the two characters
  before each occurrence and drops the ones that are `t(`: **today it prints
  `? "visit"` and `: "visits"`; against the fixed copy it prints nothing.** Both
  halves measured, not reasoned — the fixed copy was made in a scratch directory
  and `app/src` was not touched.
  **AND THIS IS THE FIRST FAULT IN THIS AUDIT THAT ONLY EXECUTION FOUND.** A read
  graded this criterion a PASS in batch 13: it names a file, a command and a
  screen, which is everything a read checks for. **Running it took four minutes
  and showed the command was decorative.**

  **What failing looks like:** the grep comes back clean because somebody
  deleted the word instead of translating it, and the record card now shows a
  bare number with no noun. **The screen read is the half that catches that**,
  which is why both clauses are here.

  **THE BROADER NUMBER, SO NOBODY THINKS THIS IS THE ONLY ONE.**
  `tests/spanish.test.mjs` reports **10 of 1611 dashboard strings with no
  entry**. Whether this is one of the ten was **not** established — the audit
  found it by reading 9.6, not by running the test. **Do not close the ten on
  the strength of this one line.**

  ***CLOSED 2026-10-06 (Lane A).*** The wrapping itself was done on 2026-10-03 (`aff219b`, and proved then on the Spanish screen). What
  kept the box open was the entry's own command, which still printed one line: **the comment explaining the fix quoted the very word

### 14.23 — Nothing opens a closed `<details>` before the tap-target sweep measures, and eighteen files use one

- [x] **Found 2026-09-25 by the ticked-item audit. 4.5 named it as requirement 2
  and closed without it, deliberately and in writing. Not built here: it needs
  `scripts/` and the browser.**

  **4.5's own words, from the six requirements it learned by getting them wrong
  first:** *"Open every `<details>` first. 29 of 41 `.choice` controls on
  Booking rules sit inside two closed foldrows that still report full-size
  rects. **A gate that skips them prints clean over 71% of its population.**"*
  It then closed on `/admin`, where `grep -c "<details" AdminPage.jsx` is zero,
  and named the leftover: *"`BusinessInfo.jsx`, `Campaigns.jsx` and
  `Notifications.jsx` do have `<details>` rows and are NOT proven to open them
  before measuring."*

  **MEASURED, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THREE SCREENS:**

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | occurrences of the string `details` in `scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs` | **0** |
  | occurrences in `scripts/lib/tapProbe.mjs` | **0** |
  | files under `app/src` using `<details>` or `<Folded>` | **18** |
  | in `BusinessInfo.jsx` / `Campaigns.jsx` / `Notifications.jsx` | **2 / 1 / 5** |

  **WHICH KIND OF FAULT IT IS, STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE THE TWO KINDS NEED
  DIFFERENT FIXES.** `tapProbe.mjs` filters candidates through
  `checkVisibility`, so a control inside a closed fold is **never discovered**
  rather than measured and wrongly passed. **So this is a silent coverage hole,
  not a false green** — which is the better of the two and still the thing
  `docs/silences.md` exists for, because a control that is never discovered
  also never appears in the `n of N` the probe prints. **Its own coverage
  numbers cannot show it.**

  **TWO SCRIPTS IN THIS REPO ALREADY SOLVE IT, TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, AND NEITHER
  IS WIRED IN.** `scripts/sweep-widths.mjs` opens every `<details>` before it
  measures — its own comment says *"a closed `<details>` anywhere on a screen is
  content no width has measured"*. `scripts/tabbar-clearance.mjs` refuses to
  measure them and **counts the refusal into its receipt**. **Either is
  correct. Having neither is the gap.** Pick one and say why in the commit:
  opening them measures more, counting them measures honestly, and the wrong
  answer is a third mechanism.

  **Fix:** in `scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs`, before each screen's walk, either
  open every `<details>` or record the count of controls skipped for sitting
  inside a closed one — and put that number in the receipt either way.

  **Done when:** one run of `node scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs` **captures its
  own baseline** — the settings doors walked **twice in the same run, once
  without opening closed folds and once with** — and reports **both
  discovered-control counts**, with the difference named per SCREEN. **The
  difference is the population nothing has ever measured, and it goes in this
  roadmap line.** If the counting route is chosen instead, the run reports a
  **non-zero skipped-inside-closed-fold figure** in
  `receipts/sweep-tap-targets.json`, by screen, and that figure goes here.
  **A run reporting zero difference on every screen that has a `<details>` is a
  failure of this item, not a pass**, until somebody explains why.
  ***TWO FAULTS FROM A COLD READ, 2026-10-02, ON MY OWN CRITERION.*** It asked
  for a count *"strictly higher than **today's**"* — **a baseline it never
  recorded**, so a stranger has no number to compare against and the baseline
  moves while they look. This repo's own discipline is *"the before number, so
  the size of this is visible without re-measuring anything"*; capturing both
  counts in one run makes the comparison self-contained. And it said a run
  showing no change *"on any of the eighteen files"* — **a category error**: the
  eighteen are `app/src` files that USE `<details>`, while the sweep reports
  controls per SCREEN and never mentions a file. **The unit was wrong, which
  would have made the failure condition unreadable.**

  > **THE ONE LINE FOR WHOEVER HAS THE BROWSER, before any code is written:**
  > *with the dev server up and the demo tenant seeded, open the settings doors,
  > run `document.querySelectorAll("details").forEach(d => d.open = true)` in
  > the console, and count the focusable controls before and after. The
  > difference is the size of this item.* Five minutes, and it tells you whether
  > this is worth an hour or worth a line.

  **What failing looks like:** the fold is opened, the count does not move, and
  somebody concludes the gap was imaginary — when what actually happened is that
  the probe opened the fold on a screen that has none. **Name the screen the
  number came from.**

  ***BUILT, RUN AND TICKED 2026-10-06 (Lane B, on the manager's go). Lane exception, recorded: `scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs`
  only; `tapProbe.mjs` was not touched.***
  **The route chosen is the opening route, and why:** it measures more, and the counting route's only advantage (honesty
  about a gap) is kept by the census below, which prints the closed count beside the opened one. The walk now probes each
  screen as it arrives, opens every closed `<details>` on it, waits for it to settle, probes again, and closes them again;
  **the second probe is the measurement, the first is the baseline**, and a screen with no closed fold is probed once, as
  before. It is the default; `--no-folds` restores the old walk.
  **The baseline, both counts by screen, one default run** (`node scripts/sweep-tap-targets.mjs`, `receipts/
  sweep-tap-targets-dashboard.json`, `dimensions.fold_census`): **248 screens, 68 of them carry a closed `<details>`, and
  opening them measured 966 controls that no run had measured, every one clear of the 44px floor** (the run reads `clean`,
  PASS 248/248, 809,894 assertions, 0 failures, canary 5 of 5). An earlier full run with the flag gave 960 on the same 68

  |---|---|---|
  | Today | 1 | 2 |

  Booking rules at 32 is the figure this item's own source, 4.5's requirement 2, predicted ("29 of 41 `.choice` controls sit

  **The 12 rows that gained nothing are explained, and none is a probe opened on a screen it does not belong to:** the

### 14.25 — The credential scanner's population is markdown only, so the file types that actually held a password were never in its net — BUILT 2026-10-06

- [x] **Found 2026-10-03, by a password sitting in a `.mjs` comment that no check
  in this repo was ever going to see. Not a verdict fault — a POPULATION fault,
  which is `docs/gotchas.md` 89's exact shape one level out.**

  **THE MEASUREMENT, one line of the check's own source.**
  `tests/no-credentials-in-markdown.test.mjs:137`:

  ```js
  const files = execFileSync("git", ["ls-files", "*.md"], { encoding: "utf8" })
  ```

  **That is the whole net.** It reports *"165 files · 130,000 lines · 6 rules · 0
  findings"* on every run, and **every one of those 165 files is markdown.** The
  six rules are good — they match SHAPES rather than known values, which is why
  they caught a fourth account's password the first cleanup missed. **The rules
  were never the problem.**

  **WHAT IT MISSED, AND IT WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL.**
  `tests/platform-admin.test.mjs:1303` carried the master login's password inside
  a comment — a sentence quoting it to explain why that account should not be an
  admin. **It sat there through every green run of the credential check**, because
  a `.mjs` file is not in `ls-files *.md`. Removed 2026-10-03; the value is in no
  file now, and the sentence survives without it.

  **AND TWO CLEANUPS HAVE NOW HAPPENED WITH NO GUARD LEFT BEHIND EITHER TIME
  — checked, not assumed.** The markdown sweep of 2026-09-25 produced this check,
  which covers markdown. The `scripts/` sweep of 2026-10-02 (`9ce9b65`, 40-odd
  files) added **zero** files under `tests/` — `git show --name-only 9ce9b65 |
  grep -c '^tests/'` returns 0. **So `scripts/` was cleaned and is unguarded, and
  `tests/` was neither.** A cleanup without a guard is a state, not a property:
  it is true on the day and nothing keeps it true.

  **Fix:** widen the population to every tracked text file that can hold a
  literal, and keep the six rules exactly as they are. **Rename the file if it
  stops being about markdown** — a check called `no-credentials-in-markdown`
  invites precisely the assumption that let this through.

  **Done when:** the check's population includes **`.mjs`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`,
  `.json`, `.yml`/`.yaml`, `.sql`, `.html`, `.css` and `.txt`** as well as `.md`,
  the file count it prints **rises from 165 to the real number of tracked text
  files**, and **it has been proved by planting a credential-shaped literal in a
  `.mjs`, a `.json` and a `.yml` in turn and watching it go RED and name the file
  and line each time** — then removing all three and watching it go green. **Three
  plants, three reds, three removals, each printed.** The planted value is a
  throwaway that exists nowhere else and is never a real login.

  **What failing looks like, and it is the thing this item is about:** the check
  still printing **0 findings** while its population excludes the file somebody is
  worried about. **Zero findings over a population that excludes your subject is
  not a pass — it is a measurement of something else.** The second failure shape:
  widening the net and letting the three plants pass because a rule keyed on
  markdown punctuation (a backtick, a table pipe) does not fire in a `//` comment
  — **which is why the plants are the criterion and the file count alone is not.**

  **One thing it must NOT do.** `.env`, `app/.env.production` and anything
  git-ignored are outside this: they are not tracked, the rule is about what gets
  committed, and widening to untracked files would make the check fail on a
  working credential doing its job. **`git ls-files` is the right spine; only its
  pattern is wrong.**

  **BUILT 2026-10-06 (DP Cowork2).** The check is now
  `tests/no-credentials-in-tracked-text.test.mjs` (renamed with `git mv`; the
  live pointers in CLAUDE.md, `docs/gotchas.md` and `docs/platform-admins.md` follow it,
  the two dated write-ups that quote the old name are left as history). The six
  rules are untouched. The net is `git ls-files` minus binary-by-extension minus
  anything with a NUL byte, so a new file type is scanned by default.

  **What it prints now:** `1002 files (165 markdown) · 398189 lines · 6 rules · 6 finding(s)
  · 6 declared`, taken at `1a03cdd` plus this commit's working tree by
  `node tests/no-credentials-in-tracked-text.test.mjs`. It had printed 165 files and
  0 findings.

  **The done-when, with the plants.** § 2e writes a credential-shaped throwaway
  into a `.mjs` (line 2), a `.json` (line 3) and a `.yml` (line 4), runs the REAL
  `population()` and `scanFile()` over them, and requires each to come back naming
  its own file and line; § 2f removes them and requires an empty population.
  **Run every time, so the three reds and three removals are permanent, not a
  one-off.** The plants run through the production functions, not a copy.
  **Broken on purpose, three ways, all run:** `--break=md-only` (the old net)
  went 6 failed (the three plants "not even in the population", the text-file
  floor, the extension list, and the declared exceptions); deleting the map.html
  declaration from a copy named `app/public/map.html:303 [pair]`; declaring 2 where
  3 exist named `tests/staff-roles.test.mjs [assignment] declared 2, found 3`.

  **WHAT IT FOUND, and it is the thing the item was for.** Six lines, no value
  printed anywhere. **One is real:** `app/public/map.html:303`, the demo owner's
  login beside the words "sign in first", on a page that ships with the site, and
  the same value as the one in `.env` (compared as a yes or no). It reaches the demo
  business only. **FOR-ANDREW.md has the DECIDE row**; it is declared in the test
  as OPEN and printed on every run, so a green cannot be read as a clean tree.
  The other five (`tests/booking-engine.test.mjs`, `tests/tenant-isolation.test.mjs`,
  `tests/staff-roles.test.mjs` x3) are accounts those tests create for themselves and
  match no value in `.env`; declared FIXTURE by exact count per file and rule
  (gotchas 98), so a new hit in the same file still goes red and a fixed one goes
  red until its line is removed. They cannot simply move to env: `ensureUser`
  signs back in with the same password after a 422.

  **Two cuts, said plainly.** The widened net scanned the check's own canary lines
  and found them, so the canaries are now built from two pieces rather than the
  scanner exempting itself. **And a password in code with no digit in it is still
  invisible** (`password: "someword"`); the header carries the measurement and
  the command (22 candidate lines at `1a03cdd`, none matching `.env`) and says why it

### 14.38 — The job record scrolled sideways 16px at 320 in Spanish, and `1fr` is why — FIXED 2026-10-08

- [x] **Lane A, `app/src/theme.css`, commit `dcdd271`. Found by Andrew in the 320 Spanish shot taken for 4.7:
  "Recordatorio" cut off at the right edge of the pinned bar, and the four-way payment `Segmented` squeezing
  "Perdonado" against its own edge.** Numbered 14.38 because no open item owns the job record's pinned bar; 9.11e
  is the adjacent one and it is somebody else's, in progress.

  **Measured on the record at five widths in both languages before anything was changed**,
  `document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth` against `clientWidth`: **336 vs 320 at es@320, and exactly 0 difference on
  the other nine.** One width, one language, and the whole page moved for it.

  **`.actions-row`'s own comment claims the control "divides rather than overflows", and `1fr` does not.** It is
  `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, so every track is floored at its content's min-content width; a single long word cannot wrap,
  so the floor wins and the GRID grows past its container instead of sharing it — the three tracks measured
  **97.4 / 94 / 110.4 inside 288px of room**. `minmax(0, 1fr)` on all four of the row's declared shapes makes the
  comment true, and that is the part that generalizes: **no label in a language nobody has written yet can scroll
  this page again.**

  **That stops the page moving; it does not make the words fit, and they are different jobs.** With tracks capped at
  88.9px, Spanish's "Calendario" (97) and "Contactos" (94) still want more than their share, so the three-up row goes
  to two columns **in Spanish only**. Shortening one translation was available — `t("Reminder")` has exactly one call
  site — and was the wrong fix for that reason: the bar's own ceiling is *"~9 characters / ~60px of text, measured at
  320"* and Spanish breaks it on all three words at once.

  **The `Segmented` takes the same shape for the same reason, and the scoping is the load-bearing part.** The
  `max-width: 360` block already drops SIX options to two columns and says in the same breath **"SCOPED TO SIX, so
  nothing that fits today moves"**, citing the four-option payment control at 23–297 inside 301. **That measurement
  was taken in English and is not true in Spanish.** So the new rule is scoped by language rather than by child count
  — `html[lang^="es"]`, which `lib/localeStore.js` already keeps true for screen-reader voice — and the English
  four-up that the earlier item deliberately left alone **is still deliberately left alone**. This is the
  "say in the commit why it is safe now" case from CLAUDE.md: the premise was disproved, not the judgement overruled.

  **AFTER, same ten measurements: sideways scroll 0 everywhere, console clean on all ten.** English unchanged at
  every width — en@320's row 2 went 88.91/88.91/90.19 → 89.33/89.33/89.34, which is `minmax` stopping the third track
  stealing 1.3px, bar still 160px, `Segmented` still one row of 67px. **Spanish at 392 and above unchanged to the
  pixel.** Only es@320 moves: bar **160 → 208px**, row 2 two columns at 138px with all three labels full size and
  nothing clipped, `Segmented` **2×2 at 136.5px** with every label on one line instead of four 67px tracks on two
  lines each.

  **The taller bar breaks the rule that stops a focused control landing under it**, so `scroll-margin-top` goes
  10rem → 14rem under the same language-and-width scope. **Proved rather than reasoned: 176 focus stops tabbed on the
  job record across en/es at 320 and 392, 0 landing under the bar or off screen.** `keyboard-walk.mjs` is clean at 167
  stops but walks Today, Calendar, Money, Clients, Business and Booking step 1 and **never the job record**, which is
  why that walk was taken by hand.

  `pinned-bar.mjs` PASS, 17/17 targets, 119 assertions, canary failed as required. `var-scope-guard.mjs` reads 1865
  rules and every root-level `var()` still resolves. 19 credential-free checks pass. **`sweep-widths.mjs` and the full
  battery were skipped on purpose** — another session was driving a browser at the demo tenant — so the width evidence
  here is this session's own ten measurements and ten frames, said plainly rather than left to look like a sweep.

### 14.31 — The pointer-staleness tool is not in the repo, so every grade it produced is unrepeatable

- [x] **14.31 — A measurement nobody can re-take is a claim. The git-delta
  pointer tool decided 53 pointers into four buckets on 2026-10-02, caught the
  one wrong citation it was graded against, and **ran out of a scratch directory
  that no longer exists.**

  So `docs/open-items-read-as-a-stranger-2026-09-25.md`'s grade table has a
  population a reader can reproduce (the pinned `git grep` is written beside it)
  and a **bucket column they cannot** — *still-good*, *changed-below-only*,
  *suspect* came from code that is gone. **That is the difference between a
  snapshot with a re-take command and a snapshot with an apology**, and it is the
  fault `docs/gotchas.md` 92 asks every number in this repo to avoid.

  **The method is written down and was proved twice**, so this is transcription
  rather than design: date each pointer with `git blame -L<n>,<n> --porcelain`,
  ask whether the target moved with `git log <sha>..HEAD -- <target>`, and sum
  `git diff --unified=0` hunk length changes where the hunk's old start is at or
  before the cited line. **It must also carry the thing the original could not:**
  a pointer that was wrong on the day it was typed into a target that has not
  moved comes back *still-good* **for ever** — all three `857` rows were exactly
  that — so the receipt states that `still-good` means *has not drifted*, never
  *is correct*.

  **Done when** `node scripts/pointer-age.mjs` writes a graded receipt naming
